reviewsWithKeywords.text: Grounds are big and there is something for everyone to doLots of restaurants, museums and attractions, places to visit I would recommend the AIDS Memorial Park, Japanese Tea Garden, Museum of Sciences During my visit I was forced to look for washroom outside the park as all were closed because of Marathon in park on that day...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful oasis in San Francisco
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must visit when in San Francisco. Lots of areas to explore although be prepared to pay for many of them including the museums, flower conservatory, Japanese tea garden etc. It’s big so if you want to see much then a bike is a great way to get around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a gift to San Francisco!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park has so very much to offer, with world class museums, gardens, walking spaces and all conveniently located in the downtown area of San Francisco.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Day Out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great place to wander around and fill a day. There are many attractions within the park e.g Japanese Gardens, Academy of Sciences, Segway Tours and plenty of walking trails. It is also very easy to get there by public transport.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always a beautiful place to vidit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No matter how many times I visit this park, it never ceases to amaze. It’s close enough to my favorite restaurant by the Ocean.  The grounds are very lush right now and in the winter we can go back to see the tulip bloom by the Dutch windmill  it’s just plain beautiful and lots of places to walk on sidewalks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wish we had more time here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We only had a short amount of time to spend in the park. When we visit San Francisco again we are going to set aside an entire day to take in the many activities in the park. It’s beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Feels like Central Park of San Francisco.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I enjoyed most of this park. We went twice while spending a week in the city. The first time was a nice, sunny and pleasant day. It was a weekend, so the park was full. We enjoyed walking around the conservatory and seeing the one small waterfall.  Also got a nice meal at a food truck. The tea garden had a huge line so we came back another day for that and glad we did. I adored that tea garden and was a real highlight of the trip. The one day we went clear to the end with the windmill. It was middle of week and bad weather. No one really around and the area smelled like urine. Didn't stick around there long, but did enjoy the other part of the park. Overall a nice stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: For a unique view of the Golden Gate Bridge...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: ...try and climb Strawberry Hill in the middle of the boating lake, the views from there are amazing! The hill itself is a butterfly sanctuary, so it’s quite pleasant in itself.The park in general is a very nice place to be- there’s a lot of different things to see. Be aware that the Japanese Garden and Botanical Gardens are paid for features. The whole park is very long and will take a good few hours to leisurely walk around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Golden Gate Park, SF
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice, relaxing area to walk around a lake pathway. Take your belongings out of your car, our windows were broke out and backpacks taken after returning to our vehicle. This is a Big problem all over SF.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Delightful many-faceted green corner of the city
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We discovered this by chance,viewed frm the top of a bus tour. Then we went back on our own,starting at Ocean Beach (Metro) and just walked. It was a really relaxing place and clearly beloved by many of the locals-families with dogs,jpggers and courting couples among others.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see if you're in SF. We drove through with our tour guide, seeing many beautiful portions of this gigantic park!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went through on a tour and was able to stop and look around. It's absolutely gorgeous and worth the time to go and see this while in San Francisco, even with younger kids. They loved the sites and the open spaces.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Still my favorite park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On this last visit we didn't have much time, but wanted to come walk around. The weather was warm and we ended up just walking around the duck pond. There was construction near the cross over, so we just walked around. My 6 year old niece enjoyed walking near the ducks and swans and there were turtles as well. It was a nice relaxing walk on our last full day in SF.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We like this park!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On a return visit to SF we stayed on 24th near the park. We enjoyed walking around and through the park, seeing bison and the windmills. My wife loves running and went around a few times. The location is great near the ocean at one end and Haight Street at the other. Best of all we attended Outside Lands on the Sunday, lovely weather and saw Paul Simon close the show, a good week.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rampant Theft!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I didn’t heed the warning of a kind woman who told me that there has been break-ins of vehicles. On our last day of a wonderful vacation-our rental car was broken into and thief stole our carry-on luggage with laptops, iPads and my kids iPhones. So just please be aware- our car was parked on Nancy Pelosi Dr by the Science Academy. We were only gone about 2 hours in the mid-morning. Do not leave your rental car—it is a target!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wish we had more time here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Golden Gate Park on a Saturday at the end of June and had a very positive impression. We found street parking on the northeastern edge of the park on a side street off Arguello Boulevard and probably could have found a spot on Fulton Street as well. It was a little short of a mile walk to the de Young Museum from where we parked and a pleasant jaunt. Be advised that the park is very large and driving from the northeast corner to the northwest corner along Fulton Street is 3 miles. The BEST TIP I have to share is one I learned from the Trip Advisor San Francisco forum: be sure to go to the top floor of the de Young Museum (no charge to do this!) to see the views of the city. The museum guards were all “cool” with the three of us and others just walking in and by-passing the admission line. This was the highlight of our visit to the park!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, and Huge!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a huge, iconic park in San Francisco. We had actually gone to the California Academy of Sciences, which is actually within the park, and decided to spend some time in the park as well. Be sure to select a sunny day to enjoy the park; unfortunately, it was quite cold and foggy when we visited, so we really couldn’t spend a lot of time there. We rented the family bike (which is rather expensive) to go around the park. We had some lovely views of the rose garden and the lake etc., but riding that bike is tough!! The park is huge, and of course we couldn’t manage to see all of it. There are a lot of portions within the park which have paid entry. So plan properly before visiting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very big park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very big park for walking, biking or relaxing. Not recommended by me if you have limited time as a tourist. Just too big and not best value of limited time. But if you do have time or you are local - great place to visit on a regular basis.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Nice and Great Playground for Kids!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a huge park!  We have visited the Japanese Gardens and Botanical Gardens which are beautiful. The latter has the largest flowers and roses I have ever seen!  There is also an awesome playground for the kids with a carousel (extra $), various slides, zipline for little ones, ropes to climb and swings. Bring a piece of cardboard so that they can slide fast down the natural stone slide. You can also bring lunch and drinks for a picnic. Awesome place. Check their calendar for other events!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just gotta take the stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Only touched the tip of the park near Haight Ashbury but took a nice stroll thru the park. Lots of open space and picture moments. Ran across some locals bowling and kids riding the slides on cardboard boxes. Glad we stopped.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Park Like No Other
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden Gate Park is a free park similar in shape but larger then New York's Central Park. Within the park is the deYoung Museum, the California Academy of Sciences, the Japanese Tea Garden (oldest public one in the US): all requiring entrance fees. Statues abound through out the park along with two windmills, lakes, a 1914 carousel as well as a botanical garden. Don't miss the conservatory of flowers for its 1879 building alone but also for the stunning plants. It's a lovely spot to rent a bike for a sunny day, picnic or visit one of the many attractions. Check what events are taking place. There is always something.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the Japanese Tea Garden and walked through the park. It is huge and better to ride a bike to see a lot more. All the arrangements of the plants are amazing and beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ran right through it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ran the Second Half of the San Francisco Biofreeze Half Marathon, and ran through Golden Gate Park.  It was exceptionally beautiful, and I encourage anyone to stop by and spend a few days there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden Gate Park is a really wonderful place to visit on a sunny day in SF.  There are several wonderful museums:  the science museum and the De Young, plus the flower conservatory, or, you can just enjoy the beautiful scenery and relax in the park.  If you go to the De Young, be sure to take the elevator up to the top of the tower to take in the amazing 360 degree view!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A couple of hours in the park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We could have stayed much more in the area. We visited the fort: very nice view on the bay and the bridge. Some history to share with kids.Some walk around to see the bridge again. And finally the palace of fine arts. There is more to see obviously, but we didi not have enough time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Golden Gate Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Plenty of road side free parking but it fills up early. One hour walk from one end to the other. Beach at the end.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Golden Gate Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This has to be one of the most beautiful city parks in the country. We loved the Japanese Tea garden ($7/ adult). We found several of the museums to be very expensive so we didn't see them. We tried to get information at one booth, but unfortunately the volunteer there was misinformed about the park. We walked great distances, but didn't really know how to access this great resource. An information booth should have been there with options affordable for families to participate.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Such a beautiful park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved spending a few hours here. You could totally spend the whole day if you wanted to. There is a lot to do and see even for the kids. My kids loved the playground. It’s a long walk from one side of the park to the other so if you have children bring a stroller. We rented a bike but it was so crowded that it was hard getting around peacefully. Overall, loved this park and would absolutely go back again on our next visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Time-off
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Finally a place which is quiet, calm, relaxing and not overcrowded. If offers so many attractions, Botanical garden, Science museum, playgrounds,...I took bus to the beach and walked from there across the park. It was like in a dream!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful break from the city!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Only being in San Francisco a few days, we planned to be at Golden Gate Park for half of a day.  That wasn't near enough time.  We maybe only made it half way through the park!  It is HUGE with so much to do and see!  Things like the Conservatory of flowers, Japanese Tea Garden, DeYoung Museum, Stow Lake, etc. took us more than half a day!  We were disappointed that we couldn't see and do everything.  We loved how beautiful the grounds were, which were well labeled with many signs and maps.  This is a must do if you are ever in San Francisco, but I would reserve an entire day if you can!  Another helpful note is that there are some areas that have an admission fee such as the botanical gardens or the Japanese Tea Garden and other areas where you can rent bikes, boats, etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice break
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful way to get off the busy city streets. Take a Segway tour. It was so much fun and really very easy to operate.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must Do in SF
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I'd say Golden Gate Park is a must if you're in San Francisco. Plenty to do and see, relaxing, a variety of attractions, indoor and out.  We went twice in five days and only saw half of it.   Easily accessible by bus from all parts of the city.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: California in a nutshell
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden Gate park is an amazing and beautiful place. I first visited a few years ago and we explored the beautiful botanic gardens. Just walking across the beautiful greens was spectacular. Last week we visited the California Academy of Sciences museum. The entry price (substantial at $36 for adults) provides a full day of entertainment. There is an aquarium, a planetarium, and many natural history exhibits. We had a delicious and surprisingly reasonably priced lunch at the cafe. We especially loved the rainforest exhibit with all the butterflies. I highly recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nature, calm, green, fitness, tai chi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I just can say this place is awesome, totally a must in SFO, the Botanical Garden catch you and the environment is so beautiful. I truly recommend to give a complete ride around and enjoy the morning 😊

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful walk through all the gardens
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked all over Golden Gate Park, enjoyed tea in the Japanese Tea Garden and enjoyed ourselves thoroughly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Large, beautiful and diverse park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is very much worth a visit.  It is free (although the botanical garden and Japanese tea gardens and museums have entry fees), and it offers diverse opportunities for sports, walking, hiking, botanizing, photography, picnicking and year-round special events.  We only got to see a small part of this splendid park, but look forward to spending more time on our next visit.  I should mention that I had my cell phone out taking pictures and out of the corner of my eye I saw a man seemingly angling towards me and when I switched hands he veered to my other side. Perhaps it was a coincidence but when I put it away, he walked away.  You might want to keep an eye out and keep your phone, purse or camera close.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So many places to walk. Beautiful outdoor space. Well used by all the local populace. We enjoyed all the huge trees, the many flowers blooming and the rose garden.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a beautiful day walking through this park, stopped in at the museum and continued our journey through the gardens.  This is a must see in San Francisco!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Yet another free national park done right
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not to be missed and a great place with interesting and approachable engineering exhibits and explanations. Quite windy and a bit chilly even in July on the bridge, and too many tourists obv, but not be missed. Great views near the 1st tower. Free presidio crissy field ride is good. Dont take the presidio hills route which is a waste of time. After than catch the free downtown bus from Presidio transit center.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Japanese Tea Garden
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I really enjoyed the garden once I got past the cashier who was very rude to me after taking my money.  I asked if there was a map and she gave me a dirty look and just waved her hand at me like keep moving.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This is must!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden Gate Park is wonderful. This place is so beautiful you can spend hours of time just strolling through the acres and acres of green or just take a nap if you need a rest. I love the atmosphere, so many people, so many gorgeous views. The park is huge! We especially enjoy picnics on the park. Take a basket and fill it with yummy delights then head over to the Park. You’ll definitely have a GREAT time!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed in the Sunset area and walked to the park every day. There is so much to see-the botanical gardens, the Japanese tea garden, museums, etc. it was great to spend time in the city and then walk through the park. The views atop Strawberry Hill are worth the short, steep hike, not to mention the waterfalls you can see on your way up. This park is a must-see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Easy to get lost - but don't miss!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The city is not good about signage.  You are likely to pass right by the location you are looking for without realizing.  The botanical gardens, tea garden, and conservatory are a plant-lover's paradise.  Lunch at the museum was delish!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Free Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I had wasted several minutes looking for the parking lot. There is no need to do so since there are some places that you can do street parking. The park is huge, so at least bicycle is recommended if you want to hop around a few spots. The park is huge and free. It would be an ideal place to do picnic or even a lunch bbq. With the timing right (seasonwise), rose garden would be very beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you want a relaxing few hours in lovely surroundings, this is the place, so quiet, so beautiful, nice for a picnic

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is really big and nice.It is the best place for cycling or walking for a long time and so smooth.It has different parts with different kinds of flowers  and they are changed with changing the season and I definitely recommend it.It has a contemporary museums like De Young and botanical garden that are nice to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park had a lot to offer.  Gardens, golf course, walking trails. Etc.   I thought it was the best San Francisco had to offer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Way to Spend a Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The history of this park and the transformation of this local area is fascinating. Learn the history and then tour the park to appreciate it even more. There are many things to do for all ages. It is very clean and well maintained. A wonderful place to spend a day with the family and friends.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I only visited a fraction of this vast park which is one of the best I´ve ever seen. On top of the enormous variety of plants in the park itself, the Botanic Gardens and Japanese tea garden, there are other attractions well worth visiting such as the De Young Museum and the Academy of Sciences Museum. There are lots of places to eat or have a picnic. My only regret is that you generally have to pay to get into these although the Botanic Gardens was free when I was there. This can make a day out a bit pricey especially with a couple of kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Park!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So much to see and explore. If you want to get lost there you could all day long. Rent a bike and enjoy discovering all the treasures it has to offer!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Plan on visiting here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden Gate park is a must for all tourists and residents.   It has something for everyone from the garden lover to kids to animal lovers.  It is a huge park great for running and cycling or just having a picnic.  We ate at some wonderful restaurants just south of the park as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Drove though - Didn't stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful Park which we had allowed more time to explore this park   Wanted to go to the Tea Garden but didn't have enough time.  If we ever return that will be first on the list.  Heard it was amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An enticing variety of activities and sites.............
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Expect to spend about 4 full days if you want to do all of this great attraction, which includes miles of walking and biking trails, restaurants, museums, a giant greenhouse and a diverse and lush vegetation throughout. There is easy access to the all of the park plus free parking. Best advice: be sure to obtain a map of the park before you go. The weather was perfect while we were there, but a rain/wind jacket is advisable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Expensive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful huge park but beware, very expensive as you have to pay to go into some of the gardens.The Japanese Tea garden is lovely but the tea and snacks very over priced

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the Stowe Lake inside the park. The boathouse is charming and there are canoe and paddle boat rentals. There is a great walking path around the lake, which wasn't steep at all and took about 45 minutes to get around walking at a strolling pace. There were geese with babies as well as many other birds. There were quite a lot of flowers in bloom for the time of year. It is a beautiful and relaxing place to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely worth a visit, rent a bike if you can!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful part of San Francisco and we spent 4 hours cycling, sitting and drinking coffee. It's a lot larger than you expect, but the good news for anyone cycling is that it's not too hilly! Highly recommend a visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Despite having been to San Francisco twice before, it wasn't until my third visit that I finally came to the park.  We didn't walk around too much but we circled the park by car and saw sooooo many people taking picnics, jogging, walking, etc.  We went to the Academy of Sciences and that was a majority of where we spent our time at the park.  My aunt & uncle have apparently been to some concerts and gardens in the park, loving them all.The park is 20% larger than Central Park but I don't find it as walkable or nice.  Still, like I mentioned, there were so many people - certainly thousands.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Plan to spend a whole day!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So much to do in this park we were so suprised! We uber-ed there which I recommend because parking seemed very tight. We did the BEAUTIFUL botanical gardens & the Monet exhibit at the Art Museum. The area around the park has some cute restaurants and shops. The grounds were very well kept and ended up being our favorite part of our visit to San Fran!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too much to see, do, experience and it's all wonderful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No matter what your interests are, something in this phenomenal park will make a visit worthwhile.  Whether it's simply the assortment and arrangements of plants, the museums, or the ability to exercise in a beautiful setting.  This park is excellent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wide open spaces
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Despite there being a lot of people around, we never felt crowded. There is tons of space and lots of beautiful plant life to experience with sunny or shaded areas to sit and quietly enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a nice walk here today. The weather was perfect, sunny & warm with a slight ocean breeze. A nice thing to do & a different view of the bridge

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's Huge and stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We only saw a small part of it, but it is huge like Central Park in NYC, you could easily spend all day there, perhaps hiring a bicycle to get around  (available at the gate), would be idea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family Time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden gate park s filled with amazing destinations. Stow lake, Botanical gardens, Spreckels lake, conservatory of flowers, etc. Take a #1 California bus, 2 Clement bus, 38Geary bus and exit on 6th AVENUE. Clement and 6-8 Avenues has numerous Chinese take out foods. Gourmet Dim Sum and Good Luck Dim Sum are great!! Cash only. Order your baked pork buns, shrimp dumplings, egg rolls and chow mein etc at Gourmet Dim Sum, great price and delicious! Either place among many are great. Fill up that pink bakery box and walk into golden gate park on Fulton Street. Clement,then Geary then Anza, Balboa, Cabrillo and then Fulton Street. You will see numerous places to sit and enjoy your food. Buy a cheap bag at Goodwill on 10th and Clement and a straw blanket at another Chinese dollar store in clement . You will have a great day!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So much to see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Park has so muchThe trees that span from the haight to the oceanThe littke lakesThe cultural places luke the musuems the tea gargen the house of flowers the festivalsThe carosal and kids play plays

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun place for everyone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is huge! Lots of things to do for everyone and anyone. My favorite would be the children’s park. Lot of over size hermit crabs, a giant fish & nice big waves to play. There’s this really cool slide made out of cement with lots of cardboard of help go down thF slide! My 3yo couldn’t stop climbing up the stairs to slide down!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Come and Enjoy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Golden Gate National Park is a wonderful place to see the Bay and the Golden Gate Bridge.  Take the time to relax and ride a bike or just stand and  watch the Bay and the Birds not to mention the people. On a nice day you can see people surfing at the base of the Bridger. Don’t forget to stop in at the Warming Shack and Snack Bar for some refreshment and to sit and get out of the Bay wind. The profits are all for a good cause – The Golden Gate National Park Conservancy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not what we expected
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is pretty, but goes on forever, so don't expect to hike from one end to the other.  There is also a ton of greenspace with not many attractions or things to see or do in between.  It's not like Central Part in New York.  After walking almost 2 hours, we eventually called an Uber to take us to Ocean beach because we weren't even half way through the park.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Massive park with some stunning little books and crannies, definitely worth a visit.We were there in February so the evenings were a little chilly but the sun was shining and we managed to find a large pond with birds and a waterfall, we sat down after a lot of walking and took in the scenery, it was so calming and tranquil.We only saw a tiny part of the park so can only imagine what the rest is like given its size, the place is HUGE!Would love to come back and make a proper day of it and hope that one day, I will.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is huge and includes lots of things to do, as well as just beautiful landscaping to enjoy on a stroll, run, or bike ride.  Very well-maintained.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots to see and do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such an amazing space to explore. So many things to see and do.Everything from japanses tea gardens, to Chinese pergolas, and bison!Definately worth a visit, plan a whole day so you can take in all there is to see and do in a relaxing manner

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful gardens in a very big and busy city. A botanical oasis.  Parking along streets. Picnic on many benches, enjoy the many flowers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A good day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is plenty to see at this park, and it is very easy to reach by bus.  You will need more than half a day to see it all.  Plenty of walking involved.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful park, lovely to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Still a great place to visit! I was fortunate enough to attend the Bill Graham Benefit Concert here many years ago. Large open space, plenty of great spots to picnic and relax. Bring your walking shoes, a blanket, a good book and a smile. Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A large park in the city
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The large park is minutes from the city. It has botanical gardens, Japanese themed garden and a lot of walking and running trail. A good place to savor the gardens, have picnics and/or have walks or run. People watching is also suggested.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Golden Gate Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful acres of landscape and open space right in the middle of the city, the botanical gardens green house was especially  interesting and we loved that there were so many other places to see and do inside of the park compound.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Escape from the City
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the first place we visited during our weekend stay in San Francisco.  It was a great place to start the day.  There are a large number of trails that take you past a  variety of wildlife and flowers.  We started our visit with a hike around the lake and to the top of Strawberry Hill, which offered a panoramic view of the city and the Golden Gate bridge.  Our kids loved walking on the stepping stones near the waterfall. We also walked to the Japanese Tea Garden in the park and then drove to the windmills.  We were able to do all this in less than 4 hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A huge Park with more things then you'll be able to find
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For many Golden Gate Park is something they just drive through. Or they've heard about it in a story or a book or TV show and think they have a picture of what's in Golden Gate Park. Well I'll say this no matter what you think's in there, there's a whole lot more. Depending upon the time of year there are many things that bloom around the park tulips bamboo trees, all kind of flowers, and a whole bunch of things I haven't found yet. There are windmills made in honor of Queen wilhemina, there's a buffalo Paddock with buffalo in it, there's a science museum the living roof, and a planetarium oh, there are walking trails oh, there are running trails, there a bike routes, and many buildings to explore if you can find where they're at. It's a long Park and goes all the way to the ocean, and in between the winding roads bring so many things. Come early for good parking. Come early for free parking. I have had a good time every time, and we'll be back for more Good Times. Sometimes it's the science museum, sometimes it's the flower gardens by the windmills, sometimes it's just a walk in the park

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful park, Japanese Tea Garden is a Must!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park was beautifully designed and has been excellently maintained. There is plenty to offer here for families, such as the playpark near Robin Williams meadow, and the California Academy of Sciences museum (incl. a dinosaur display!). Personally, I was enthralled with the Japanese Tea Garden which is beautifully curated and actually does serve teas and small snacks! I'd recommend renting bike and riding around on a Sunday because it's the one day of the week where they close the park to car traffic. Gorgeous!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nice Japanese tea Garden
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A pleasant visit in the month of April. The garden is located in  the middle of Golden Gate Park, which is 20% larger than Central Park of New York. The garden is very well maintained and was clean. Flowers bloom and birds chime. It requires about an hour to strode along and take photos. The best part is the admission free before 10 AM.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The sun is shining and all is beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: People always talk about the cold summer weather in San Francisco. Here is my take on it....layer up and have fun! If you don't like the weather wait a few minutes. It will change. I highly recommend wick away clothing. You can be warm when it's a bit cloudy and windy and then good when the sun emerges. I always bring a light sheet to lay down on the grass and snacks and water. The view is epic and the people watching even better. It's simply a great place to chill, especially on a clear day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful spot🌴
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Golden Gate Park there’s many different spots big big park many different places to go and walk many different places for the children to play together ⛲️♥️ gorgeous park plus horse stables 🎻

reviewsWithKeywords.title: All free
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the trip out for a break away from the city. You have to pay for the better areas (conservatory of flowers, botanical gardens etc) but there is ample parking and picnic space. If you have children the play area is great.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing park area!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is huge and has many different areas to it.  ie. soccer fields, gardens, historic windmills, trails.  Too much to mention.  Very clean as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Botanical gardens are wonderful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I walked around the botanical garden for over an hour one recent morning. It was so peaceful and beautiful and I really appreciated the zen like calmness. Great place to meditate or just relax. The grounds are immaculate and it is hard to believe you are in an urban area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of my Favorites
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love San Francisco. One of my favorite places in the city in the city is Gold Gate Park. It is beautiful to walk around for exercise or just a casual stroll. The are many pedestrian friendly pathways. I enjoyed walking by the pond watching paddle boaters enjoying their afternoon. The Botanical Gardens is filled with flowers and interesting plants. I did just, on this visit, stumble upon two Dutch Windmills at the edge of the park. However, my favorite part of the part of the park by far is having tea at the Japanese Tea Garden. There is an admission fee of about $9 to walk around the garden. I think it is worth it. There is a Coy Pond, pagodas, flowers, bridges and shaded pathways with benches. You can also enjoy tea and treats. There is also a gift shop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can't imagine San Francisco without it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From the botanical gardens to the De Young museum to the free music, this is a beautiful place with something for everyone. A nice escape from the more hectic aspects of the City, and definitely a respite from touristy places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a walk at the golden gate park and we enjoyed it. The park is so big and we had a Segway tour at the park. It was fun and informative. We didn’t have a chance to visit the Japanese tea park.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Verdant Jewel of SF
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Regardless of weather or season, one should spend time at GGP to marvel in the beauty and serenity of this 150 year old city oasis. Granted-San Francisco in general is a beautiful city-but the park provides literally miles of green lushness for you to run, walk, or drive through, or better yet, to plop down in for a picnic or a respite with a book and maybe a bottle of iced tea or rosé.One of my family’s favorite places is Stow Lake, because we enjoy feeding the waterfowl and strolling around the lake and environs. Recentlymy elderly dad fell near the lake despite using his cane. While I sat with him on the ground waiting for him to stabilize enough to get up, several passersby stopped to inquire if they could help. A group of four men and a woman helped me get Dad up and to a nearby chair. What does that incident have to do with GGP? Well-the Park is a place where the community comes together to enjoy nature among fellow San Franciscans. On that day, I was reminded of our good fortune to be residents of this great city and to have such kind and caring neighbors-strangers though they may be.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enjoy hours at Golden Gate Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful Japanese Tea Garden with blooming cherry trees. A very interesting museum, de Young, with a Monet exhibition and a tower of free access and magnificent views. The California Academy of Sciences museums with a varied offer to children, teenagers and adults. People dancing old time melodies here and there. Exuberant vegetation, painters, picnicers and all kinds of activities. Unforgivable not to go there on a sunny say.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning outside space
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having spent a few days visiting the city, getting out to this lark was a welcome relief from the buildings for me! I was surprised to find it so tastefully designed, maintained and with interesting features to explore! It was a very romantic to wander the paths, enjoy the plants and wildlife, and discover the various different areas. We visited the Japanese garden whist here as well which is well worth it also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful park worth the time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited GG Park with our teenage sons. They enjoyed our brief time their seeing how SF residents enjoy the green space in their city. The Japanese Tea Garden closes in the late afternoon so plan your visit accordingly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the World's Great Parks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden Gate Park is one of the world's great parks in the Western Part of San Francisco. The park stretches from the Richmond and Inner Sunset Districts, near the famous Haight Ashbury Area and ending at Ocean Beach, the Outer Sunset and the Outer Richmond/Precidio Areas. At the Ocean there is famous Cliff House on one end and the Windmills at Judah/Outer Sunset District on the other end, with great sand dunes and wonderful sun sets, thus the District name. In the center of Golden Gate Park there is the Botanical Garden, japanese Tea Garden, Academy of Sciences Museum and other great museums and places to explore. Golden gate Park is a must visit place on any visit of San Francisco.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just go it’s lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park is stunning for a walk cycle and explore. There is lots to do and the scenery and atmosphere is fab. If your visiting you must go and take it all in

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful park.  Lovely to walk through.  Its so great that the locals and toutrist alike have this wonderful park to explore.  We went to the De Young for the Monet exhibit and next to it was the Japanese Garden with the trees in full bloom.  Just Beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Huge expanseof parkland.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The largest park ion San Francisco and lots of walking to see all the sights. Park has a lake with paddle boats to hire and a rsetaurant. Other sights are the many play areas, golf course, flower exhibits, chinese garden etc. You need time here. Name is deceptive as it is not that close to the Golden Gate bridge. Well worth spending time here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enjoy a day of bicycling in the park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bicycling is such a fine way to explore this park.  We had our own bikes, and I don't know about bike rentals, but assume that there are some. Take a picnic lunch.  Stop at the deYoung Museum, California Academy of Sciences, botanical gardens, any number of smaller attractions.  It is a great way to experience some of the history of San Francisco and to people-watch.  From one end to the other, it is about 8 miles (our calculations), but the many side attractions can make it into a 12 mile ride on relatively flat terrain. We started on the East side and ended up at the Beach Chalet for lunch... A beautiful early spring day.  At least on a weekday, the roads are reasonably un-crowded and there are special bike paths that take you on an adventure.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relax and spend the day!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So much to see in GGP!!!  The windmills are spectacular!!!  Plus you can stop by the buffalo paddock!!!  There are several there. Take s stroll through the Japanese gardens.  Gorgeous anytime of the year!!!  The conservatory of flowers is stunning!  The building was badly damaged in storms several years ago and repaired to it’s original beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Central Park of San Francisco
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lot to see in this park and very close to the Botanical Gardens.  People relaxing, sometimes a bit too much as we encountered a man relieving  himself in the middle of a path.  Not sure he was homeless either.  Other than that a nice peaceful place to talk a stroll

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Oasis of calm (cliché alert)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a beautiful park, so much to see and do. Or you can just stop and chill and enjoy the sunshine (weather permitting).  It is huge. To visit all parts you either need a bike, or 2 or 3 days on foot.  But well worth it for kids and adults alike.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't overlook
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is beautiful and has world class museums. Although the creator of the park hated sculptures in nature, others can appreciate art and nature in one great setting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must Stop Photo Stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is too beautiful to miss while in the bay area! Take some time to enjoy the city without bring in the city ;)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So much to do, from barbeques, pedal boats, Lindy hop dancing and beautiful gardens. Well worths visit. Amazing to see so much wildlife in such close proximity to everyone also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice run at the park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park was very clean and well maintained.  I ran around the park (inside loop) and it was a nice route.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant place to sit or to walk around
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This small park was lovely to walk around or sit and relax for awhile. You can watch the swimmers braving the cold water and admire some of the old ships docked nearby. Quiet place to gather your thoughts or jsut to admire the scenery

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must visit for SF from local resident
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyed the beauty of the park on Saturday.  Some streets in the park closed to auto traffic on Sunday,  highlights to visit are the California Academy of Science and the Dejoung Museum.  Across the concourse from each other. We saw the excellent Monet exhibition at the Dejoung yesterday. Nice walking opportunities abound. Be sure and go up in the Dejoung observation tower for a 360 degree view of the City. Admission is free.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very popular park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We toured the park via segways on a nice Sunday afternoon and it was packed with people. It was very pretty with some interesting areas, unfortunately I was too busy trying not to run someone over on my segway to see all the sites. I'd recommend walking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Japanese Tea Garden
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed driving around  this nice park seeing all of the interesting trees.  We saw the Japanese Tea Garden and decided to visit.  We have a huge amazing one at the Missouri Botanical Garden in St. Louis if you are ever in St. Louis.  This is nice because it is compact, has nice simple trails and you get to see some very pretty trees and shrubs and nice buildings.  The cherry blossoms were blooming and they were beautiful.  Definitely worthwhile.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful park. My 17 yr old didn’t find it too exciting though. We walked around, ate some food (but finding food wasn’t that easy).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, safe, friendly and so very much to see!!Great walking and bike riding.We will be back to explore more!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Space
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely take the time to explore this beautiful green spaceIt’s very peaceful.  Lovely walking paths and cleanLoved it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Soul of San Francisco
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Much like New York's Central Park, Golden Gate Park is the place San Franciscans come to play.   Its sprawling lawns host soccer and touch football games while bikers enjoy the roads through the park. Add the beautiful botanical exhibits at the gardens and consevatory, the  world class art at the DeYoung Museum and the animals on display at the California Academy of Science, and you could fill a week without leaving its borders, but you'd want to go beyond to nearby restaurants serving a variety of cuisines that represent the diverse tastes that feed the city's heart and soul.  For us, it is a spring traditional to visit the botanical gardens. We head to the deYoung when an interesting new exhibit is on display. Street parking can be tough but we've never had problems getting parking in the lot that serves the CalAcademy; increase your chances to find a space by getting there before 10 am, especially on weekends.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must Do - On any List!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Truly this is the most unbelievable park I have ever been to....!  Like Central Park,  it is man-made and dates back to 1871 - and the  turn of the century.  At one time, it had been uninhabitable land of sand dunes - now it is an incredible paradise of nature.  We had the great fortune of spending an afternoon here - on a Segway Tour that left from the Music Area of the park... We went in gardens that were exotic and remote, around lakes, and to the important landmarks.... the deYoung Museum (featuring Monet), the William Shakespeare Garden (with plants and flowers mentioned in his plays), a serene Aids Memorial grove of remembrance, a Music Concourse with a huge band shell, the Academy of Sciences (with a living roof), the Japanese Tea Garden, the Botanical Gardens, and the Conservancy of Flowers.   Hippie Hill, a gentle sloping green space - overlooking Robin Williams Meadow -was the site of the Summer of Love in 1967 - and hosted musicians and bands like Janis Joplin, the Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane, and George Harrison.  (It is still used as a concert/event venue to this day.)   There are so many other places - just on the Eastern Part of the park, that we did not even have time to sample.... There are reportedly two windmills on the west side of the park - and tulips in bloom in March.Throughout our travels, we witnessed the genius of John McLaren who is credited with planting over two million trees within northern California - and taming the wild lands into this beautiful park... Exotic species were brought in from around the world and grown within the park's boundaries.  Today, we were told that the park employs 300+ gardeners...and it is indescribably beautiful with walkways, lakes, gardens,  blooms and blossoms everywhere! It is truly one of those places one needs to visit many times - but will appreciate from the moment you arrive....A fabulous hint:  the tower at the de Young Museum is free.... From its vantage point, one can see in all directions - in the park and to the city beyond.  (just follow the signs inside to the elevators...)A caution:  We had a lot of problems with Uber Drivers not being able to "locate us" - even though we were right at the east entrance of the de Young Museum.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tranquil spot easily accessible from downtown.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On a sunny day, this is a lovely place to wander and chill. The botanic gardens are delightful and we loved the old carousel, at 2 dollars a ride for adults and 1 dollar for children, it’s a bargain! You can walk there or get a no7 bus, also very cheap.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the Best City Parks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I decided to walk from one end of Golden Gate Park to the other. We took the Muni bus to the start of the park and went through the Botanical Gardens and Japanese Gardens. We then kept walking towards the Pacific through miles and miles of this beautiful park. It was a week-day, so many of the paths were relatively empty.  What started as a sunny, blue-sky warm day at the top of the park, turned into chilled cloudy fog as we neared the ocean.  Most of the walk is down-hill, and there were bikes for rent as well. When we reached the windmills and ocean at the bottom, we exited the park and took the Muni Bus back to our hotel. The gardens charge an entrance fee, but the rest of the park is free. It was a lovely way to spend an afternoon in San Francisco.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An incredible diversity and a must - just remember to truly embrace you need to spend the day and bring your walking shoes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots to do.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing park. The space for children to run around in and burn off energy is vast. Through out the park there are lots of separate areas, from children's play areas to gardens to explore or to sit and watch the day go by. We only got to see a small section of the park the main area being The Japanese Tea Garden which was spectacular. The Pagoda's could do with some refurbishing but the whole area was stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely open space
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great park for outdoor activities and picnics. Great movie screening in the summer. Very busy at weekends

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best seen by bike
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I hired a bike a cycled around the park,  I started at the bike hire from a rental place close to the Ferry building. The city's cycle lanes make it easy and safe to get there. I hadn't been on a bike in years and wasn't sure about cycling in the heavy traffic.  But I felt fairly safe using bike lanes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day here is a day in Paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So much to do in the park. Arrive early and there is plenty of parking on the street (4 hr). The museums, flowers, running, walking, and green beauty surrounds you!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this park - gr3eat place in the city
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love the deYoung Museum, the Botanical Gardens, and just walking around. You can take a city bus to/from almost anywhere. Uber is also available, and not expensive as the city itself is surprisingly small.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So much to do and see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long rainy day of walking in the park- Saw the bison, one of the windmills, de Young Museum, Botanical Gardens and Japanese Tea Garden. Loved all of it. I would rent a bike or segway if I returned again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Refreshing Experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Golden Gate Park in San Francisco is a public park and is bigger in area than the Central Park in NY city. It is a pleasure exploring this park by just walking around. There are several things to see within this park. It is truly a refreshing experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rode around to take in the scenery of this absolutely huge park. It is a beautiful place and has great story behind how it was built from barren hills.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A gorgeous 1000 Acres with 10 Lakes!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I’ve been exploring new areas in SF in an effort to socialize a foster dog. Although I have been to the museums and gardens, I had never spent much time walking around the lakes. There are 10 of them - I had no idea!! Lovely walkways, varying terrain, water life, birds and a mix of facilities available. A lovely way to spend an hour, an afternoon or a day!Golden Gate Park is an underutilized gem in a city that is not short on beauty. EnJOY!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its beauty comes from its position in Golden Gate Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden Gate Park is big. It's close to 50 city blocks from east to west and 4-5 from north to south. There are many attractions including museums, gardens, the Botanical Gardens (aka the Strybing Arboretum, one of the jewels in the crown of this much-jewelled city. My favorite places are: 1. the arboretum, free to local residents but inexpensive to tourists and one of the best anywhere in the country; the canopied-by-trees space between the De Young Museum and the Academy of Sciences; and Stow Lake, with its island which has a pagoda and is suitable for jogging and walking, where you can hire a boat or simply sit on the edge watching the ducks and geese and seagulls. Of course there is a huge variety of trees and birds everywhere in the park. Sometimes it's good to walk - and you can walk for miles here, accompanies by people in lovely solitude. There is a bison paddock, children's playgrounds, polo fields, and a stables where you can hire horses or go on a hack during the summer. To my mind, the museums and the tropical house in the picture above are replicas of better institutions elsewhere in the US or Europe. It might be said that Europeans (and I include Brits) will be disappointed by the De Young and Academy since their home versions are likely to be bigger, more comprehensive and, ironically, more culturally cutting-edge.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Expansive with Attractions Included
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a bike tour of Golden Gate Park and learned of its history and took in the beauty on a gorgeous sunny day.  The California Academy of Sciences, de Young Museum, Botanical Gardens were all included in the park.  We stopped and entered the Botanical Gardens for a delightful visit.  The Park itself is huge with ponds, grassy open areas, tons of trees and plenty of opportunities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An heaven of peace
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park must be seen from spring when the flowers are out, but it is an heaven in the town (or rather on the side of the town), with great museums, a lovely Japanese garden, lakes, walks, picnic areas,...We also were fascinated by the bison paddock.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Huge park with lots of attractions
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful park, you can spend hours walking through it's pathways. There are some museums and attractions inside the park but those are way too expensive

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and so much to do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is such a beautiful, unique park with so much to do from walking/running, museums, canoeing, to botanical gardens and more. The scenery is breathtaking easily one the top 3 best parks I’ve been to in the world (compares to Central Park NYC, Hyde Park London, Vondelpark Amesterdam, etc). Spent either half day or full day here so worth it. Walking the length of park will take a couple hrs but well worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Two Windmills
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I'm a windmill freak and was surprised that the park had two authentic Dutch windmills--both were amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rented bikes and rode through the park. Fun adventure. Wish we had more time. Beautiful place. So much to see

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and Massive Park! Worth a few steps to see it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Staying in Richmond district, we decided to take a walk through Golden Gate Park all the way to Ocean Beach.  It took us a few hours but was well worth it.  This park has everything! Paddocks, angling lakes, roller bladers, a cycling track, a polo/soccer field, a museum & café, Japanese Gardens, lush green fields, windmills fitness stations and lakes to name a few things!Reaching the beach at then end was the icing on the cake!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nature's Beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had the opportunity on a recent trip to enjoy Golden Gate Park. This is a must off the concrete path of the city and has many beautiful paths to enjoy with gardens and museums. It by far beats the usual tourist sites of the city and is an enjoyable scenic delight. There is an observation tower (elevator) at one of the museums to get a panoramic view of the entire city to take photos of all the different parts of the city. Well worth your time!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Huge Green Space
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most green you will see in San Francisco. I’ve heard the park is bigger than Central Park. Lots of trails for biking, running, whatever you’re up for. Fields of grass for romping. The views of Golden Gate Bridge from the Bay Area of the park are beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to spend the day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park is beautiful.There are many interesting options for things to do, like the Academy of Sciences, the Japanese tea gardens and so on.You can also find a quit place to just sit around and rea a book.Lovely.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful spot in SF full of surprises.  From windmills to buffalo the park has a lot to offer including de Young

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mahoosive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a little gem in the city. There are plenty of things to do in this park without even putting your hand in your pocket. They even have a Bison enclosure... Bison in San Francisco. We wondered around whilst looking for the big bus stop. If you don’t like walking...... stay away. I’d imagine in the summer it’s absolutely stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another way to blow through a day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I highly suggest taking the street car down Irving towards Ocean Beach and walking the length of the park back towards the university. Stop at the Devils Baking Company to load up for breaks...nothing better than sitting in the grass and having a snack lol. Even just wandering around the East end is a great experience, even on a busy Sunday I was able to explore the trails/ stay away from the crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing if you love long walks in the nature
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Golden Gate Park (far from the Golden Gate Bridge) is a very very long park. You should really go if you like nature and long walks. We walked for hours across the entire park until we reached the beach facing the ocean. The walk back was another 50 blocks, but still enjoyable. Plus a good way to keep fit :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Japanese Tea Garden- Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What can I say about this place....Its simply stunning!What a lovely little hidden gem. Had a wonderful time.Definitely worth the entry fee. Everyone should visit this place when in the vicinity.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent several hours here, brought a picnic lunch and enjoyed a great time.  They have a very nice playground for children.  I took advantage of a walking trail.  There are public bathrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Didn’t expect this
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I didn’t expect the park before the bridge. The drive was awesome and the trees were so cool. Do it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very different from parks we are used to. We thought this would be a fairly walkable park but were definitely mistaken, it is a lot bigger than we were led to believe and there are a lot of roads throughout which made it quite hard to get fully lost and enjoy the park experience. We had also read there was plenty of places to rent bikes (around and in the park) to ride through on but this wasn’t the case either, we were half way through the park when we found a bike rental and had already decided to leave. Over all it was nice, pretty and clean but not what we were expecting at all. I would call it more of a collection of small parks or gardens with stuff in between, than an actual park.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's such a large park you could walk round it all day. I particularly enjoyed the Japanese tea garden which is $9 to enter but is very beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful park!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Golden Gate Park during our SF visit.  The place is amazing!  Unfortunately it was raining on and off during our visit but that didn't stop us.  We enjoyed the beautiful landscaping and went to the Flower Conservatory.  That place was such an enjoyable place to be.  The whole park is super family friendly we saw joggers, families with kids in stollers, biking and dog walkers.  Very enjoyable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are so many places to get a great view of the bay, the bridge, and the whole area. Wasn’t too crowded when we went on a Sunday morning. Good location to park and then walk the bridge. Clean restrooms and easy access from the 101. Enjoy your day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked around and enjoyed the beautiful nature amongst the big city. The Science Museum was amazing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You haven't seen San Francisco if you don't explore Golden Gate Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden Gate Park is the city's garden and playground. There are numerous sculptures, meadows, lakes, picnic areas and secluded spots to enjoy a private moment. In addition there us the Japanese Tea Garden,  the de Young Art Museum, the California Academy of Sciences....plus the Rose Garden, Conservatory of Flowers, the Bison Herd (really!) and you can rent a row boat on Stowe Lake. And, out near Icean Beach there are two working Wind Mills with flower gardens that were built more than 100 years ago and refurbished in the last 20 years. Whatever you're looking for in a city garden you can find in Golden Gate Park.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots to see and do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went here as part of our Hop On Hop Off tour. We spent hours here. The Japanese tea gardens are beautiful. The Buffalo paddock is cool.  The Museum & Conservatory of Flowers worth the trip. The gardens and sculptures are huge and beautiful. There are food trucks there too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to wander around
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited during our recent trip to San Francisco.  We followed a self-guided walking tour from our guide book which we really enjoyed.  The park is clean & felt safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Something for everyone!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Whether its the pond, biking, the De Young museum, watching people to Tai Chi or reality jousters just playing around, the water falls, the lovely trees and parks....there is truly something here for your entire family to enjoy. We walked this park for several days and kept discovering new things!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park is beautiful, we went on a sunny, cold day early January and it was wonderful. The Japanese Tea Garden inside this park is very tranquil and pretty. Worth going and exploring.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: New Years Special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We met our friend at Golden Gate Park while on vacation in S.F. over new Years. Two attractions were free.The De Young Museum and the Flower Garden.We only had time for one so we went to the museum. It is a beautiful place with many galleries and lots of variety in art forms.Take time to go to this museum in the morning and into the city in the evening!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a beautiful park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent some time here and was impressed by the actual size and diversity of this park. It was very pretty place to wander and it was greta to see so may people and families enjoying the area.Well worth  a look.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This place is huge
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I didn't even cover the whole thing but very cool place to visit. You could spend many days here and see many things without leaving this area. Be prepared to spend some time. Visited in August 2017.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Central Park West
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful park in he middle of a beautiful city.  Whether you are enticed by museums, aquariums, botanical gardens, cultural attractions such as the Japanese Tea Garden, statues of previous leaders in music, and countries alike or, wish to visit a few sites so important in the 60's and hippie movement, you will find it all here.  Enjoy my friends and do not forget to wear a flower in your hair.  PEACE!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super visit with wonderful weather!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a Christmas visit and the weather was great.  Lots to see and the views are great.  Such a wonderful relaxing place to visit.  So many nice people to meet.  Take the time to visit, enjoy the park and you will have great memories.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Country in The City
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are an outdoor person and especially traveling with children, GG Park is a must do for you. From the Panhandle (beginning east end) to the Ocean (west end to watch a sunset) it is a 3+ mile walk, run or bike to explore the beautiful mini gardens (e.g. rose, dahlia), Japanese Tea Garden [savor a cup of tea], Botanical Garden and Conservatory of Flowers; enjoy a paddle boat ride [a children favorite] on Stow Lake; art at the Fine Arts Museum (aka DeYoung); science and natural hx at the CA Academy of Science (see an albino alligator/children love this place/good caferteria); ride the carousel by the tennis courts; watch the Bisons; participate in a variety of lawn sports/even golf; and Dutch windmills. When you reach the ocean, take care of your hunger pains & thirst at the Beach Chalet Brewery & Restaurant - maybe see the sunset if you time it right. On weekends & holidays there is a free shuttle bus that stops at the major attractions. Also, the main thoroughfare is closed off to traffic.    Or simply pack a picnic lunch and pick a spot to enjoy the peace and tranquility of nature. It is easy to get to by public transport from downtown SF on the #5 Bus to 8th Ave & Fulton (middle of the park where museum, Japanese Tea Garden, CA Acad of Sci, Botanical Garden are located). There is something for every body.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best place for a run
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went for a run by myself through The Panhandle and Golden Gate Park on a rainy Saturday morning. There were heaps of runners out, and most importantly I felt very safe. (I was visiting from Australia.) This is not what I expected from a big city park. It is superb! Whilst I know it is not natural, it certainly feels it. I love that it is not a well manicured botanic garden type park. It is big - you can find any distance run you like. It is pretty flat, and there are heaps of paths to take. As someone who has been running forever, this is definitely one of my favourite runs ever. I highly recommend it for a walk or a run. It is also a great place to go and relax solo or with friends and family. Lovely, lovely haven in the city of SF.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful park to cycle through to the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rented bicycles from the cycle shop, Avenue Cyclery, which was much better than the tour companies. From there, we cycled though the park all the way to the beach. It was a Sunday, so the road we were on (JFK Drive) was closed for cars, which made the experience so much less stressful. The park is beautiful, and there is lots to see. At the beach, we got a coffee from the Beach Chalet, then cycled back up. The return journey was a bit hilly, but generally doable. We’ll definitely be back to see the things we missed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Highlight of our visit to SF
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park is beautiful and a wonderful way to escape from SF the city into SF the California coast. The botanical gardens are off the scale amazing, so well organized and labeled. Make sure you get to the scent garden, never experienced anything like it. So many plants with strong and alluring scents, too many to try to list. Best 3 hours of our time in SF!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful scenic park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park is full of beautiful scenery & a variety of activities inside the park. You can see bison (on loan from the zoo), a botanical garden, & the flower conservatory. Great park for walking, riding bikes, or renting segways or mini cars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice place for family and friends. Great for pets as well! Large open grassy areas are perfect for a family game of Frisbee or just for frolicking about.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply magnificent!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is so beautiful and full of splendor!  Great for families or a great stroll in the park. There’s something for everyone here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The vision of John McLaren
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I imagine that like me, most visitors would be amazed by the sheer size of Golden Gate Park – at over a thousand acres, it is actually 20% larger than New York’s Central Park. Close to fifteen million visitors come to the park every year. This park dates back to the late nineteenth century. Today, it is hard to believe that before 60,000 trees were initially planted here, this was just an expanse of arid sand dunes. The credit for this goes to the vision of John McLaren, this park’s superintendent for over fifty years starting 1887. The first major event held here was the California Midwinter International Exposition in 1894. The park's most famous attractions including the Japanese Tea Garden and the building that later became the de Young Museum came up in those very early days.The Golden Gate Park demands at least a full day of exploring. This park is quite literally miles of green, dotted with lakes, trees, flowers and more than 7000 kinds of plants – all in the heart of San Francisco! Apart from the famous Japanese Tea Gardens (please see my review of the Japanese Tea Gardens), Golden Gate Park is home to many others including the Botanical Garden, Rose Garden, Tulip Garden, and Garden of Shakespeare’s Flowers (embellished with quotes from Shakespeare’s works). The Conservatory of Flowers is an indoor garden of rare tropical plants housed in what is reputed to be the oldest glass and wood Victorian greenhouse in the Western hemisphere – close to a thousand butterflies flitter around as you walk through here. There is also the AIDS Memorial Grove set up in 1988 to honour the millions of people affected by AIDS, which was later designated by Congress as a national memorial. Built and maintained by volunteers, this happens to be the first AIDS memorial set up anywhere in the United States.While here you can also visit the California Academy of Sciences which is quite an experience – a natural history museum, planetarium, aquarium, a living rain forest, a coral reef system. Right across from the California Academy is the art collection at the de Young Museum – a collection of American art spanning the 17th through 21st centuries, plus art from other continents as well. The 9th floor Observation Level of the Hamon Tower at de Young Museum offers a spectacular view of the city and the Pacific Ocean. While admission to Golden Gate Park is free, both the California Academy and de Young are ticketed attractions.Other attractions in the park include:Stow Lake – a man-made lake where pedal boats and row boats are available on rent. Great place to while away an afternoon.Strawberry Hill – this island in the middle of Stow Lake is the highest point in the park. If you take the Rustic Bridge or the Roman Bridge and walk up to the top of the hill, your reward is an excellent view of Mount Tamalpais in Marin County and the Golden Gate Bridge. Buffalo Park – where you can see the majestic American bison roam in an open habitat.Beach Chalet – located steps away from the Pacific Ocean – enjoy the fantastic ocean view at this place where you can also have lunch or dinner.Spreckels Lake – a wonderful place to jog or stroll around, or just sit down and relax under the Monterey Cypresses.Hippie Hill – having acquired some notoriety for the flower children who gathered there in the 1960s, the meadow and the slope are a good spot to relax and watch people go by.Music Concourse – was built to stage the performances of the California Midwinter International Exposition of 1894. Don’t miss the statues of historical personalities lining the concourse. One of the high points here is the grove of pollarded elms, maples and walnut trees.San Francisco’s amiable, invigorating weather makes Golden Gate Park a great spot to tie the knot. The park authorities are happy to suggest the many locations available here where thousands of couples have exchanged their wedding vows in these sylvan surroundings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Multitudes of attractions to savour in the sylvan paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A marvellous and vast park with an abundance of interesting attractions. We enjoyed strolling in parts of the fabulous amenity.We took in some of the sights, including the Academy of Sciences and de Young institution, both excellent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is so beautiful! Definitely go see if you can, there's lots to see in the park. The de Young museum is amazing, and houses a beautiful collection of art.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved the park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unfortunately I wasn’t able to spend much time hear, but there’s lots on offer from museums to botanical gardens, Japanese tea garden, the bison paddock, and lots of lovely park land and beautiful walks down to the coast/sea ( I didn’t have time for this unfortunately)I got the bus from the city centre, walked into the parked and visited the Japanese tea gardens, it was very well kept and relaxing, I also had tea in the Japanese tea house while watching the coi carp fish. After I took a walk though the park, past lakes and boating lakes to the bison paddock

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely huge park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are so many beautiful places in this park and I especially enjoyed the spectacular views from the de Young Museum (free). My favourite place was the quiet Shakespeare garden with flowers mentioned in his plays, beautiful trees and the Bard's bust.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Walk!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even in December the walk through this park was awesome, lots of yummy fragrances from different flowers and herbs!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Golden Gate Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This park is huge!  Something I would have never even known was there if I didn't take a hop on hop off bus tour.  A pretty part of San Francisco and some cool history to go along with it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The science academy, is a must see, a fantastic experience for family’s, the hands on experience for children is fantastic.Having experts on hand to explain things is great. We will visit again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best day of the trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is something for everyone in this amazing park. The art museum, the science museum, Japanese tea garden, or just strolling around. It is a wonderful way to spend a day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not to be Missed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: GGP is one of the most beautiful parks in the country, only rivaled by Central Park in NYC. The Botanical Gardens are gorgeous any time of year, not to be missed, the Conservatory of Flowers (above) is a hot-bed of tropical plants, and currently they are having a light show reflected on the glass panes nightly, two world class museums, the DeYoung Art Museum with exciting exhibitions and the Academy of Sciences, designed by Renzo Piano, has a tropical forest, filled with butterflies, colorful birds, and a planetarium, and an aquarium not to be missed. Stow Lakes is popular for traversing and paddling boats in the warmer weather. Lastly are the buffalo. Rental bikes. And there's more!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Place For A Walk!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was touring the city on the HopOn HopOff bus and I got out to walk around Golden Gate Park.  Lots to see and do and beautiful on a nice, sunny day.  I would recommend getting to Golden Gate Park via public transit versus trying to drive in and park!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 17% vehicle burglary happened in Golden Gate Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Do not leave anything inside your car. Our car window was broken and a camera was stolen. Called 911, but Policemen didn't show up. The park looks peaceful, but it is a crime site. Be careful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An amazing variety of things to do here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A treasure for a city where space is at such a premium.Paths available for walks and biking vie with a world class art museum and a Japanese garden.Be warned- free parking is tough to snare tho there is a pay lot available

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Oasis of the city
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This 3.5 mile long and half mile wide park stretches from the Haight to the Pacific Ocean and is marked with nooks and crannies.  Highlights are De Young Museum, California Academy of Sciences, San Francisco Botanical Garden, AIDs Memorial Grove, Japanese Tea Garden, Conservatory of Flowers and a century-old carousel.  Worth walking around to enjoy the highlights.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnificent Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very large park with lots of things to see. You could easily spend an entire day here just  walking here and there. There are impressive views from the top of Strawberry Hill of San Francisco. If you like big trees and very fresh air then you will love it here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't limit yourself with Japanese Tea Garden!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is an amazing park and greatest place to spend times during week-end. Everyone wants to go to Japanese Tea Garden to take some pictures but still you don't have to spend that much money to enjoy the park. There are many amazing places in Golden Gate Park which are free to enjoy with great views and nature. Go to Botanic Garden, and Strawberry Hill. But still, you can try Japanese Tea Gardens as well for less than 10$.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wish I could have spent more time here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful green space inside a crowded city. Was in the park for a morning race but could have easily spent the better part of the day here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rent a bike
