reviews.text: The park is huge! It has many smaller gardens and attractions within. We had a toddler so we visited the Koret Playground and the Academy of Sciences which is wonderful for kids. We were there beyond the traditional summer holidays (mid Sept) but they did have a concert and a play in the park on a Sunday afternoon. Would take the whole day to do proper justice to the park. At the eastern end you can enjoy the beach.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: Loved this park. It's huge. Academy of Science, de Young museum, Japanese garden, they're all inside the Park. Must visit

reviews.title: Stunning place for a stroll
reviews.text: We needed a bit of greenery and space after a few jam packed days of sightseeing and this was just the place to unwind. Loads of green space, places to sit and enjoy the sun.

reviews.title: A Day in Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park was an excellent alternative from visiting the Golden Gate Bridge. I love, this park! It reminded me of Rock Creek Park in Washington, DC. There was so much to do here. There are several gardens that you can visit as well as a museum. There’s tennis courts and soccer fields, a Dutch windmill and an exit/entrance directly across from the beach. This is an excellent place for any type of traveler - solo, group, kids, etc. I spent 3-4 hours here, but it could certainly be a full day excursion.

reviews.title: Great space
reviews.text: Loved this space with all its offerings museums, gardens withing a garden, ponds and lots of open space on the edge of the city.We parked at the Ocean end for free roadside, near one of the windmills, got there fairly early I suppose. Definately got busier as day went on. We got the free shuttle from there to the other end of park, it runs about every 15 minutes

reviews.title: A breath of nature in the busy city
reviews.text: If you're looking for a quiet place to go for a walk during your trip to San Francisco, this is definitely the place to do it. My two recommended activities in the park would definitely be the hike up Strawberry Hill and sitting on a bench along Stow Lake. Don't underestimated the size of the park: I was there for almost two hours and still only explored about half of the park.

reviews.title: San Francisco/Oakland trip
reviews.text: Huge park with a lot a history stop to see in it. Got to see the old Keezar Stadium, or what's left of it, where the 49ers once played. Also where Dirty Harry filmed a few scenes. there's even a bison ranch in the middle of this park.

reviews.title: Awesome park with so many things to see.
reviews.text: Awesome park with so many things to see. It is almost impossible to cover everything in one day. We should spare 2-3 days easily to enjoy all the buildings or parks.

reviews.title: Blast in the park
reviews.text: Needed more time to spend in this park. There is some much to do there. With all the grassy areas it would be a wonderful place to bring the family and have a picnic. The history and statues all around the park are awesome. I really enjoyed relaxing people watching.  When we were there they had a ton of food trucks which was cool. Plan on spending several hours there. Enjoy and relax.

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: This was a huge park.  Wonderful music park with a plateau for shows.  Lots of eating/toilet facilities around with walks between specific areas.  We visited on a Sunday and there was a roller dance off taking place where people congregated with in-line skates or roller skates and danced(!) along to 80s music blaring from a ghetto blaster.  Great atmosphere.  The only downside was that they charged for entry to the Japanese Flower Garden and the Botanical Garden.

reviews.title: Beautiful Park!
reviews.text: We rented bikes to explore the park and had a wonderful time!  There are many little parks within the big park and many places to find nature and peace.

reviews.title: Fun Repeat Trip to Golden Gate Park, San Francisco
reviews.text: We have been to Golden Gate Park a number of times.  This time we went on a sunny February day midweek (Thursday).   We had a nice lunch at the cafe at the de Young museum. We paid for admission to the Japanese Gardens.  We had hot green tea at the cafe there.We wandered the area and enjoyed.  We liked seeing the various statues.We then went to the Conservatory of Flowers.We had a good repeat visit to Golden Gate Park, which is larger than New York's central park.

reviews.title: Great picnic spot
reviews.text: This was a nice spot to stop by for a stroll, picnic and relax. The gardens and trails are well kept and maintained.

reviews.title: Lovely park
reviews.text: We visited the de Young Museum and enjoyed it. We decided to walk to the Buffalo Paddock, knowing it would take us a while (about 45 minutes) and were disappointed the bison were not actually grazing that day.

reviews.title: Stunning place
reviews.text: I need to come back to visit the Japanese tea garden and the Botanic Gardens.  But the park itself is stunning and the California Academy of Sciences is right there too.

reviews.title: Japanese Tea garden
reviews.text: As I expected from a Japanese garden, I was slightly disappointed from the garden itself, that did not look as trimmed or looked after like traditional Japanese gardens.We did enjoy the little café on the premesis.

reviews.title: Spectacular site
reviews.text: Magnificent views of the Pacific coastline and lots of things to do and see for the whole family. From concerts to picnics with breathtaking forestry, this park has it all.

reviews.title: Really one of best spots while visiting San Francisco
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park in San Francisco is like Central Park in New York City.A huge, wonderful park.The Japanes Tea Garden is very nice.There are some nice trails, long walking/biking paths, some open areas designated for segways and great scenery.You can easily spend the day here.There is something for everyone here, awesome, natural beauty, steps away from the crowded streets of the city.  Very clean and well maintained, perfect place to get out of the city for a bit.Really one of the best spots while visiting San francisco. Great for just having a peaceful time with nature.We will go back for sure.

reviews.title: Great daytime fun!
reviews.text: Great fun and a must see when visiting San Francisco.  There are so many things to do from museums, to botanical gardens, and more.  We started off our day early and grabbed some breakfast at one of the shops that line the edge of the park.  Great atmosphere and good food too!

reviews.title: If you have 1 day, skip the bison end
reviews.text: While I'm sure the Dutch windmill on that end is amazing in bloom, we only made it to the bison and had to come back the next day to explore the other end. There were only 6 bison and it wasn't very impressive. The conservatory of flowers and gardens on the other end of park were spectacular. The park was huge and glad we had 2 days to explore. There were signs we saw for free shuttles in the park on Saturday and Sundays. That would help a lot if you don't have time to walk from one end to the other.

reviews.title: Huge place to explore
reviews.text: I spent a few hours on a bike exploring the park. There was so much going on. On that day I was also lucky there was a free classical music concert. There is the rose garden, the Japanese garden (with admission fee), the windmills, people having picnics and even rollerblading. Also so many trails to cycle along and view beautiful scenery. My favorite thing was at the western end of the park you see the ocean!

reviews.title: Beautiful and very clean
reviews.text: I was very surprise by our visit here. We wanted to do the Segway tours, but were turned off by the price. Then we tried the bike rental place and were completely ignored by the man working the booth. So we decided to walk to the botanical portion of the garden. There are so many different things to see and do here in the gardens. What surprised me with the separate admission....had hoped this would be completely free.

reviews.title: A lovely park and a must visit place in SFO
reviews.text: We walked downhill from the top of Twin Peaks to the eastern end of the park and walked all the way through to the western beach end. We must have walked 8 miles in all. The park is 3.5 miles long, but the end to end walk is much longer as the paths are windy. Lots to see as you stroll through including the Bison enclosure, Japanese Garden (entrance fee), windmills, botanical garden, conservatory (entrance fee), dahlia garden etc.

reviews.title: Stay All Day!
reviews.text: I love to meet a friend in front of the ROSE GARDEN. What a photo op! This is a world class park so don’t be in a hurry; pack a lunch and wear layers especially in the Summer when you might expect and not get warm temps! Visit the DE YOUNG MUSEUM and THE JAPANESE TEA GARDEN! Wear comfortable shoes and walk the length of this fabulous park right down to the Pacific Ocean! Wear a hat besides a baseball and show that you are ready for anything!

reviews.title: A Nice Park
reviews.text: Not much to say but that its clean and nice with a big area to walk around and sightsee. Worth stopping off to see

reviews.title: So much to see! So much to do!
reviews.text: My daughter, son-in-law and I visited the Park to see The Japanese Tea Garden but also took our lunch and enjoyed the peaceful surroundings near one entrance. Bicycles were available to rent but we chose to walk after parking near the Japanese Tea Garden area. The grounds are fabulous and we only saw one part. My daughter and I entered the Tea Garden and enjoyed the serenity and the exquisite plantings and beautiful statuary and paths. There is a Tea House but we had just finished lunch so did not visit it. However, we did find some nice things in the gift shop. It was well worth the $10 entrance fee ($7 for seniors). My son-in-law chose to visit the de Young Museum instead and we met him there. A special exhibit of Soul of a Nation: Art in the Age of Black power was drawing many visitors. The gift shop there was very nice with a range of children's items, books, pottery, clothing, jewelry, art. Both places are well worth the time to visit. The Golden Gate Park is huge and has something to offer for everyone.

reviews.title: Japanese Tea Gardens
reviews.text: You can't take a bad photo here. It's not very big but it's very beautiful. The trees are stunning. It cost $10 and it was worth every penny.

reviews.title: The fame of the city !
reviews.text: Coming to San Francisco and visiting this famous landmark is an experience which is nostalgic . I vast open park with the natural and beautiful landscape is a treat . A walkers paradise for a memorable time with the families can be a treat.The good weather adds to it . Easily accessible and popular it is one attraction not to be missed .m

reviews.title: Beautiful Park!
reviews.text: We saw this park when we went by on the city tour bus and then went back because it looked so beautiful.  We walked around the park, but you can also hire bikes.  Lovely if you want to get away from the hustle and bustle of the city!

reviews.title: Clean
reviews.text: Lovely park with Japanese tea gardens you pay a charge to enter .Very big and clean .Lovely place to go on a warm day Loads of interesting statues through out.There’s the botanical gardens we didn’t go in here but heard it’s worth a visit .The nicer side of San Fran.

reviews.title: Botanical gardens
reviews.text: Visited the golden gate park and botanical gardens on New Year’s Day. The botanics are well laid out and worth a wander for anyone interested in gardening or just happy to appreciate beautiful plants/ nature. The golden gate park is enormous with lots of aspects to enjoy within. Bring a picnic and wander to your hearts content!

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: Breathtaking the park is beautiful go early best before it get crowded all theme parts of the park have fee Japanese garden botanical garden Ect.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park is one of the great parks of the world
reviews.text: We’ve been to over 60 countries and Golden Gate Park ranks up there with the best.  The DeYoung Museum and the Academy of Sciences are wonderful and the scenic walks and drives are beautiful.  Amazing as it was built on sand dunes.

reviews.title: North cal trip
reviews.text: Lots to see, such a beautiful park, botanical gardens, academy of science, lots of  attractions for all the family and trails to run and walk.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Great park... beautiful and lots to do. Botanical Gardens, California Academy of Sciences, De Young Museum, and more. And a short walk out of there to Haight Ashbury and a few other neighborhoods. We took the bus there from Fisherman’s Wharf. Very convenient.

reviews.title: A beautiful walk
reviews.text: Took the bus to Ocean Beach and then did the walk back through the park to Haight-Ashbury. Beautiful day with lots to see and do. Did not pay for any premium park experiences but just the walk was enough to appreciate the beauty of the place.

reviews.title: Beautiful spot to relax, picnic, chill in SF
reviews.text: What nice and relaxing park in SF. Bring some snacks and a blanket and just hangout in this beautiful park. Nice quaint spot with very nice flowers

reviews.title: Tons of Things to See and Do
reviews.text: This 1,000+ acre park was once mostly sand dunes, so the transformation to the current pastoral oasis in the middle of a very densely developed city is remarkable. Don't miss it.

reviews.title: Huge green space
reviews.text: Very huge urban park built on reclaimed sand dunes is home to ten lakes.park filled with gardens,flowers,huge trees,wildlife,play grounds and also  has a museum.Beautiful place for city dwellers to relax and reconnect with nature.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: Really great place to go to relax. Lot's of different things to do there: tea garden, museums, trails, etc. Lots of parking.

reviews.title: Such beauty to behold...
reviews.text: In May of this year my son and I walked from San Francisco City Hall to the Pacific ocean, but not before finding our way through Golden Gate Park. It was a peaceful wonder living alongside a bustling city and it was a joy to see and hear. I believe this is also where we came upon a Botanical Greenhouse of tropical plants and orchids - a must have experience for me. Check out Golden Gate Park - you will not regret it!

reviews.title: A Gift From the City
reviews.text: Among all of the "Hussel and Bussel," in the City, you find this wonderful oasis. A great place to relax and enjoy natural beauty.

reviews.title: San Francisco is a rose and it has thorns!
reviews.text: Best part of SF is that most GO-TOs & MUST SEEs are free.  Golden Gate Park is free!  You can ride your bike. You can take a picnic in the multiple open fields. Go for a walk. Check out some of the gardens (some with admission). The Park is right off of the avenues with tons of local eateries within walking distance. Quite a few boutique shopping spots as well.  I take all my out of towners to the Park!  It’s a jewel in the middle of the city.  It’s our Central Park.  Having said that, I have to be honest with ALL travelers.  San Francisco is a Rose.....with thorns.  San Fran is a property crime haven!  Tourists’ cars are targeted heavily.  Leave ALL valuables at your hotel or Airbnb!!!!!!!!  Leave absolutely nothing in your car!  Watch your valuables at all times.  We also have a homeless issue but for the most part, other than being grossed out by public urination and defecation, it shouldn’t ruin your trip.  SF is a beautiful rose with thorns.

reviews.title: Get a museum pass!
reviews.text: We thoroughly enjoyed the Japanese Garden and teahouse.  Also the conservatory.  When we found out that the Academy of Science was $40 per person for seniors, we balked.  When we return, we will get a museum pass and visit three or more to make it worthwhile.

reviews.title: Japanese tea garden
reviews.text: We went to Golden gate park in the rain. There is lots of places you can visit in the park but you have to pay to go into the different buildings. We paid 10$ each to go into the Japanese tea garden then paid for our tea but to me it was worth it. Not only sitting watching the rain and drinking tea but walking around the garden was beautiful and very relaxing after spending days in the city.

reviews.title: Large park with a lot of non-inclusive amenities
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is a great place to go if you want to spend an entire day paying to go into different smaller areas to see things.  We arrived on a bus tour and were surprised to have to spend even more to see things that most other cities would offer free of charge (Japanese Tea Garden, for example).

reviews.title: Fantastic park
reviews.text: Huge urban park with a wide variety of attractions. Particularly enjoyed the San Francisco Botanical Garden and the nearby Japanese Tea Garden.

reviews.title: A great walk with extras!
reviews.text: Fabulous walk. Even though it was a dull day, this was a lovely experience. From Maclaren Lodge named after one of the founders in the mid 19th century to one of the two Dutch windmills on the Pacific Coast. Lots of hidden places of interest too along the way....

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: A gorgeously designed park with so much to do in it.  One tour guide talked about how some people compare it to Central Park, but in my mind there's no comparison.  While this isn't anywhere near as large, there's much more to do and the weather is far more amiable.  There's an authentic Japanese tea garden, some museums, and lovely running trails and such.

reviews.title: Views of the Golden Gate Bridge
reviews.text: We saw the Golden Gate Bridge from the Alcatraz Tour, Pier 39, the Welcome Center Area, On the Bridge!, Grand View Park, Baker's Beach via a wine tour, and Golden Gate Park.  A year ago we saw if from Crissy Field and Grand View Park.  There are many, many places to see the Golden Gate Bridge, but wherever you choose give the fog (Karl) a chance to move.  You will see majestic and beautiful views as the fog moves in and out and about.

reviews.title: Nice park feels smaller than it is
reviews.text: I can’t help compare this to Central Park. Similar size. This one feels smaller for some reason. Also feels more forced. There are a lot of roads running through it and around it and it is noisy. Many attractions cost money. Japanese Tea Garden is now $10 in the off season. Disappointed in the pagoda there. Seems they could have done a better job maintaining it instead of asking for donations to restore it. Rest of the park is a nice walk but I’m not sure it’s worth a special trip. Can stop in Haight-Ashbury when you are done.

reviews.title: Relax and enjoy nature
reviews.text: Wow, what a beautiful place to enjoy and visit. I crossed it by bike as it is pretty big 😉. I absolutely liked the area of strawberry hill. You continue west and end up at the Pacific Ocean. Amazing!

reviews.title: A Great Place To Find Tranquility
reviews.text: I come here to think and write. It's a great place to lose yourself. The botanical gardens are very interesting if you like plants. It's all free.

reviews.title: Spent the day here, wandering around.
reviews.text: Once we figured out the parking (free, in designated rows in the middle of JFK or MLK Drives), we walked around here for hours.  Saw the outside of the deYoung Museum, Botanical Garden, Conservatory of Flowers buildings (all magnificent).  Spent the $9 to walk through the Japanese Tea Garden.  Walked through the poignant National AIDS memorial. Found Rainbow Falls from a distance  Walked to Strawberry Hill to see the Golden Gate Bridge in its glory.  Walked up the ‘hill’ to the Prayer Book Cross, and found the very top of Rainbow Falls right next to it.  Along the way, noticed the ‘ticky tacky houses on the hillside’, which are the subject matter of the song ‘Little Boxes’ (used as the theme song for the tv series, Weeds).Whether you have 1 hour or many hours, this is a great place to visit.

reviews.title: Nice option
reviews.text: The Golden Gate Park is a good option to spend a Sunday morning walking and resting. Very good for runners and bikers too. If you are a tourist there are attractions such as the Botanical Garden, Japanese Tea Garden, the Young Museum and the Flower Conservatory that are all at walking distance and can be visited in the same day.

reviews.title: botanical garden
reviews.text: if you ate in sf and not visiting golden gate park half of your life is vested the best area that you can spent time in other musicale event Japaneses tea garden botanical garden flowers , science or art museum that they are all peace of art

reviews.title: Pretty but Busy
reviews.text: This is a nice area but it can get very crowded. Try to go early in the day and you will avoid some of the crowds.

reviews.title: Golden Gate, Golden Opportunity
reviews.text: Okay, I’ve seen some large and impressive parks around the world including in my home City and Golden Gate Park is one of the best. There is a wonderful diversity in the the biology and landscape. Coupled with interesting views, lakes and attractions such as the Japanese Gardens, De Young museum, Bison paddock or windmills it’s a must do in San Francisco. We walked the entire length and width of the park, eventually making it to the ocean.

reviews.title: Bigger than Central Park
reviews.text: A loop around Golden Gate Park is over 7 miles. A loop around Central Park in NYC is about 6 miles.  One of the few places in the city with free parking unless you park in the garage at the Science museum area.  Great place to get a run in.  Park at the end near Ocean beach and reward yourself after your run with a delicious meal or beer at the outdoor seating area in Park Chalet

reviews.title: SF favorite
reviews.text: Must do in SF. Went to the California science museum and saw the rainforest and aquarium exhibits, the Japanese garden, and ate at the food trucks. Great walk!

reviews.title: Amazing Science Museum!
reviews.text: Best science museum we've been to.  Give yourself about three hours to see the aquarium, rainforest, africa exhibit and planetarium

reviews.title: Great spot for relaxing nature visit
reviews.text: The park is huge! I only visited part of it at Stow Lake, Strawberry Hill, the rose garden, and a several meadows. Great walk and relaxing place to escape the crowd. You can see great sun set and a glimpse of golden date bridge.

reviews.title: Great place to escape the crowds!
reviews.text: Beautiful gardens to explore. Japanese Gardens were really nice and The waterfalls were a nice walk. Didn’t get a chance to go into the museum but it looked like it would have been interesting. Will have to plan more time next visit.

reviews.title: Lovely park
reviews.text: We went to Haight Ashbury, which was great, picked up a Picnic and walked through the park. We didn't know there was a shuttle bus that took you through the park. Unfortunately we left it too late to use it. It goes right down to the coast and a lovely restaurant overlooking the coast. We went there by car the next day. It's called the Beach Challet.

reviews.title: We were disappointed
reviews.text: Went here but was disappointed that you had to pay an admission charge for each attraction which would have made it expensive.  Gardens are well kept though but we were not willing to pay separately to go into the Japanese Garden and then Conservatory

reviews.title: Avoid the Weekend
reviews.text: While nice due to a no car policy in a great many areas of the Park, it also is a Mecca for tourists on weekends, so if you want to avoid crowds, go during the week, when you can actual enjoy myriad experiences: tea in the Japanese Garden, a stroll through the Rose Garden, the beauty of the Arboretum and the butterfly garden inside, the great Redwood “garden”, a stroll around Stoll Lake, a run through the Park, or hiking trails through endlessly lovely little fern strewn, hidden flowered settings, or the latest at the De Young Museum. And so much more.

reviews.title: Super nice
reviews.text: Spent a good portion of the day here and were not disappointed. Large area to explore. Close to a lot of other activity and places to visit.

reviews.title: Natural beauty
reviews.text: Wow, this is never ending.  Many beautiful parts to this park.  It was a great day spent outdoors exploring.  It is well worth the extra exercise.

reviews.title: Beautiful Park
reviews.text: This huge park, a bus ride away from the centre of the a City has much to offer, not just the debYoung Museum and the Music Concourse, but access to the Botanical Gardens and the delightful Japanese Tea Gardens.

reviews.title: Great park, many things to see and do
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is similar in shape than Central Park in New York City but is 20 percent larger! It is full of gardens, playgrounds, lakes, picnic groves, trails, and monuments, plus many events and activities to look for. We took almost a day to visit and did not have enough time. The park itself is very beautiful and well kept. The Conservatory of Flowers, the De Young Museum, the Japanese Tea Garden and the California Academy of Sciences, home to an aquarium, planetarium, a four-story Rainforests of the World dome and natural history museum,  Don't miss it!

reviews.title: Golden gate park
reviews.text: Golden gate park offers activities for everyone. We enjoyed an afternoon at the aquarium and rain forest. Get tickets for the planetarium show when you arrive.  DeYoung museum is worth a visit.  Beautiful day, wish we had time to do a bicycle or segway tour

reviews.title: Lovely!
reviews.text: I had no idea! I knew virtually nothing about this park before I arrived and was pleasantly surprised the whole time. I arrived via a walk up Haight, and rented a bike right there. Bikes all the way through and down to the ocean! So many pretty stops along the way. The park smells amazingly fresh of eucalyptus trees.

reviews.title: Lovely park hours to enjoy
reviews.text: We did not see one tiny bit of this extraordinary place. We walked to the outdoor concert shelter and to the Tea Garden. The view from the tower...So much more to see. Plan for several hours here.

reviews.title: Beautiful park....with vandalism nearby
reviews.text: Had a terrific and educational visit to the Conservatory of Flowers. It is a true jewel and refuge within the city. Unfortunately our car, which was parked next to the conservatory was vandalized. Police said it is a regular occurrence. Be forewarned.

reviews.title: Beautiful Park
reviews.text: Really enjoyed the Park and all the walking trails, museums and gardens. Highly recommend taking a picnic and enjoying the Park.

reviews.title: The park is bigger than Central Park, NYC
reviews.text: A huge park and you can spend the whole day over there. Few museums that can take you more than a half day to visit. You can run, you can play balls, you can walk, and picnic, do whatever you feel like to do (legally).

reviews.title: Relaxing walk at the Japanese tea Garden
reviews.text: The Japanese garden is a real gem inside Golden Gate Park. The environment is very calm and relaxing and the little kiosk inside allows you to immerse yourself in nature in front of a nice tea or ice cream. Worth going for a walk if you have some spear time.

reviews.title: So much to see!
reviews.text: The  name Golden Gate park might mislead as it is not really next to the Golden Gate Bridge....There is so much to see and do at this park: the Japanese gardens, the science museum or simply enjoy this large magnificent park!

reviews.title: Rivals Central Park
reviews.text: Beautiful park the goes from the middle of San Francisco to the ocean.  Home of many great concerts including the free ones in the late 60's. Some must do sites in the park, the Tea Garden, the Flower Conservancy, the museum of arts.

reviews.title: Beautiful Japanese Tea Gardens
reviews.text: As visitors, we paid $10 each  entrance fee but passed a really pleasant hour here. We had actually got off here in the park as it was one of the stops on the Bug Bus tour. The gardens are quite small but very tranquil and picturesque and enjoyable to stroll around. We even tried a cup of Japanese tea, Glad we came and would recommend a visit

reviews.title: Deceptively large- spend some serious time here
reviews.text: As per my review title it’s deceptively large with a wide range of things to view and take in. Maybe jog round it or walk casually and take in the sights and sounds!! Beautiful.

reviews.title: You can spend a day without spending ,Free or You can spend a lot and see a lot morere..lot
reviews.text: This park has so much to see from Great Beach into the park to a full sized Dutch windmill, Lake with boats med owes, polo,fields Japaneses gardens, Huge glass green house with every plant you can imagine, Aquarium, Planetarium, Roof gardens,, butterfly exhibit Museums, green forest walking paths, Horseback rides and lots more.

reviews.title: Awesome...SPEND ALL DAY THERE
reviews.text: Loads to do. Botanical Garden, Japanese Garden, museums.....there is so much to see and it is all great. Plan AT LEAST 5 hours there (there are food places...so plan lunch there also). If you come to SF and do NOT go to Golden Gate Park, you will HAVE TO COME BACK!

reviews.title: Great botanical sight
reviews.text: Nice pathways for walking or jogging.  Beautiful flowers and fauna.  Peaceful area to have a picnic or walk your dog

reviews.title: San Francisco's Jewel of a Park
reviews.text: Is there a better metropolitan park anywhere? Yes, the buffalo roam here - a small herd. Science museum, art museum, rose garden, palm trees, horse riding, Japanese tea garden, a golf course, soccer fields, tennis courts, arboretum, open play spaces, ponds Outside Lands rock festival which has hosted the likes of Stevie Wonder, Paul McCartney, Tom Petty and almost everyone else. Plus the ultimate Fall festival - Hardly Strictly Bluegrass Festival which is completely free to get in as a gift to the City - original from Warren Hellman and now from his heirs - no sponsors, no corporate signage just 6 stages of continuous well curated music for three days every October. The park roads close on the weekend for even more space for bikes and skaters. All this and much much more capped at the West End by Ocean Beach and the Pacific Ocean. SO fortunate to have this wonderful gem right here in the City.

reviews.title: A Beautiful Area
reviews.text: Definitely worth checking out. There is something for everyone here. The tea room is a must. Huge area with lots to do.

reviews.title: Last minute side trip
reviews.text: Beautiful park, quiet, serene in the middle of a noisy, traffic congested area.  Free parking's a bit difficult, but for a short period of time the garage is not bad.

reviews.title: Lovely Park
reviews.text: Walked from one end to the Ocean at the other and then back - really nice walk (about 9 miles). Lakes, meadows, windmills, colourful flowers,lots going on including drumming jamming session at Hippie Hill.

reviews.title: Bigger than Central Park NYC - so be prepared!
reviews.text: This was a great walk. I did the length of the park, including the Botanic Gardens ($9 entry), down to Ocean Beach and back up the other side of the park.  Thank heavens it was a mildly cook day.  This park is way bigger than I imagined. Great intertwining tracks, lakes & sports fields.

reviews.title: Fantastic Park
reviews.text: It´s a nice place to spend half a day; the botanical and Japanese Gardens are a must see. We Got early and found parking space on the inner streets and walked our way around

reviews.title: The park is great
reviews.text: This park is so beautiful! In the summer, its always busy and it is a perfect spot to everyone, all kinds of people. Must do.

reviews.title: Beautiful and Relaxing
reviews.text: My husband and I didn’t stay long but the area is beautiful and perfect for a sunset picnic. When we were there, there was yoga and people reading...just an awesome relaxing place!

reviews.title: One of America’s Great Urban Parks
reviews.text: Although it’s very different than typical city parks such as Central Park, Chicago’s Lincoln Park or Denver’s City Park, GG Park packs a great number and variety of attractions in its environs. Go for nature, special gardens, art. the conservatory or a concert. Go for hiking, biking, or roller skating. Just go and enjoy this outdoor paradise.  It’s easy to teach on public transportation too.

reviews.title: San Francisco
reviews.text: Site of old world  war 2 airfield with some original buildings  left where maintenance  was undertaken it was stated many aircraft  came  in with significant  damage etc bullet holes etc they were often repaired and returned to service  within  24 to 48 hours....This area is also a great viewing  point for photos  etc of the golden gate bridge

reviews.title: Walk to the Ocean
reviews.text: This is a long thin park on the west of SF. There are areas where you might have to pay so look up botanical and Chinese gardens for prices. The rest of the park caters for almost every other outdoor pursuit and may not be what your expecting if you want large vistas and picnics. Excellent walk to the Ocean and take some wood for the fire pits at sun set if you get a chance 🔥

reviews.title: Too large
reviews.text: Unfortunately we didn't have enough time to visit most of the park.  The part we visited was fun with music and entertainment.

reviews.title: So much to see, so little time
reviews.text: Thankfully we had a car because seeing everything here or trying to walk it would be next to impossible. A bike would have been handy.What a beautiful place right in the middle of the city! wowsome truly breathtaking sights. First Tuesday of the month was a great day as many of the museums were free.

reviews.title: Really worth a visit
reviews.text: Fantastic park to visit with museums, galleries and the superb Japanese tea garden. Spent all day roaming the park and never got bored.

reviews.title: Walked through the botanical gardens.
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is so beautiful.   We enjoyed the Botanical gardens today.  It was a true “living” experience.   The park has so much to offer.

reviews.title: Amazing views
reviews.text: You must go when there is no clouds or fog, but the views are amazing. The place is well kept, the traffic getting there can be heavy but you should go accordingly.Definitely a place every one visiting San Francisco should visit.Recommend for sure, bring a light jacket

reviews.title: Probably the most underrated city park in America
reviews.text: When you hear the discussion for best city parks, Central Park is going to be up there. Not even up there, AT THE TOP. No park is more famous than Central Park. And Central Park deserves all the superlatives. I'm not going to make this Central Park vs Golden Gate Park review. However, the point I wan to make is that I think GGP is somewhat of a huge hidden gem when it comes to city parks in the country. Looking at the reviews, you may think otherwise but most people who come to San Francisco don't have GGP on their mind. To me, GGP is my FAVORITE city park in the whole country. Its MASSIVE and has so much going on. There's museums, art sculptures, a Bison farm (YES) a gigantic Dutch Wind Mill that's right on the beach that's connected to the park. Acres and acres of open fields and green space. Running trails,  boat paddling, you name it, you can do it and they it there. Its truly a gem of a park in the whole United States I think. If you love city parks and you're in San Francisco, you owe it to yourself to visit this park. Its a park you can visit any time of the year, there's always something great going on. And oh yeah, ITS MASSIVE. Other notes: Like many other parks, you can ride a bike or a segway. And since its a MASSIVE park, there's a little bus that picks you up and drops you off at areas of the park,

reviews.title: Walk the Park.
reviews.text: We caught a number 5 bus down to the Great Highway which is far as the bus goes. Take in the Ocean View there and start your walk next to the Dutch Windmill along John F Kennedy Drive. To appreciate the beauty of the park you really need a full day and comfortable footwear. Ideally grab hold of a local tourist map before you go because this gives you an overview and you won’t get lost.  The De Young Museum in the grounds on Hagiwara Drive is worth a visit but there is an entrance charge. You will also find restrooms there and a food outlet.

reviews.title: This is a great park to visit.  It is 20x bigger than Central Park. You would need at least a day to visit
reviews.text: This is a great park to visit.  It is 20x bigger than Central Park. You would need at least a day to visit. I had the opportunity to visit while driving a Gocar. It is a lovely park.

reviews.title: There are so many parts of the park to see!
reviews.text: Make sure you stop by the Nature Conservancy while you are at Golden Gate Park.  This is a beautiful park with so many attractions and places to walk.

reviews.title: GG Park on a Segway
reviews.text: We recently rented Segways from Golden Gate Park Segway Rentals and had a BLAST touring the GG Park and beyond. We have been on Segway tours before and enjoyed them, but it was even more fun to rent and go out on our own. It is really fun, and a great way to cover a lot of ground in a short time. Instead of giving tours, this place rents them to you and turns you loose on your own. We first went to Alamo Square and the Painted Ladies, then through the entire length of GG Park to the beach. We rode up the hill to the Cliff House and to Land’s End (great views), then back to the rental place. Good equipment, good service, great fun!

reviews.title: Beautiful Park
reviews.text: We loved this park and were really surprised how large it was. We started from Stanyan and walked to the opposite end, where there was an amazing beach. No swimming allowed but really worth seeing. We stopped here and had a coffee but it was really a restaurant. Beautiful views from the restaurant and it looked good although a bit pricey. We walked about 12 miles that day and still didn’t see everything. There is a boating lake which also does refreshments. There are toilets in the park and they seemed clean with good hand washing facilities. Nice place to go to relax.

reviews.title: Beautiful park
reviews.text: We hopped off the hop on bus, walked through Haight Ashbury and across Golden Gate Park. The park is laid out beautifully, the Japanese Tea Garden was amazing. A real haven of peace and calm in the city.

reviews.title: went 3 times, and we would certainly come again
reviews.text: the park has so much to offer! we came 3 times and we only stayed 6 nights. enjoyed the botanical garden, the de young museum, the science museum, and the japanes tea garden

reviews.title: Ok for a walk
reviews.text: The lake in the middle was pretty. You have to pay to go into the botanical gardens and japanese tea gardens which are probably the nicest parts. We chose not to. There was a live band on the weekend playing which was nice.

reviews.title: Something for Everybody
reviews.text: One of the best urban parks in the country. Nice paved walkways make it easy to get around and put in the miles. Wonderful vegetation, lakes, a rushing stream, fly casting pools, boat rentals, tennis courts, tea garden, and a couple of museums. Like I said, something for everyone. We like to visit and take long walks, discovering something new every time. Check it out.

reviews.title: Active, Green Park
reviews.text: This green space rivals the mall in Washington, DC.  Lining the sides are various museums including the de Young. Under the central green area that has ample seating and some pop-up vendors, you'll find a public paid parking garage or sometimes a program on the outdoor stage at one end  There's also limited street parking, but beware of street closures, especially on weekends. For a taste of vibrant San Francisco, head to Golden Gate Park.

reviews.title: Wonderful place
reviews.text: We were really impressed with GG Park - one of our favourite spot in SF.Loved the Japanese Tea Garden - really beautiful spot and great for a tea and snack.Also visited the Botanical Gardens (really nice), the windmill and bison field. Highly recommended. Free parking too.

reviews.title: Very nice
reviews.text: We visited Golden Gate Park. It is very large and beautiful place full of green trees and grass. It is a cool relaxing oasis in the heart of bustling San Francisco.

reviews.title: Much variety
reviews.text: You'd never believe this much peace, fresh air, trees and wildlife could exist in a city.  There are vast open areas including Strawberry Hill, an island with hiking trails leading to great views.  There's also the botanical gardens, the Japanese garden, and the flower conservatory.  Each of those has a separate admission fee, but the costs are reasonable and necessary to keep these places looking good.

reviews.title: Nice green
reviews.text: Japanese Teagarden...Japanese green tea … Fortune cookies... Your future is inside:)It's a great move out on a sunny day.

reviews.title: Beautiful park
reviews.text: Wow we spent sometime here during our stay it was great you could easily spend a whole day there highly recommended

reviews.title: Summer 2019
reviews.text: We were here in August. It exceeded all expectations. There was more to see and do then could be accomplished in 1 day. The gardens the musuems all were terrific.

reviews.title: Nice
reviews.text: Lots of people using the park, nice tree lined area, Keizer Stadium in the park, busy, busy traffic!

reviews.title: So much to do!
reviews.text: The park is beautiful and there are tons of things to do. Multiple of the bigger attractions do require entry fees, though. It was well worth the time to drive through and stop by some of the options.

reviews.title: Cool place
reviews.text: This was very interesting; coming from the Midwest to the big city.  It’s defiantly something to drive through- take a bus tour they will tell you a lot about the 3 mile long park.

reviews.title: Delightful Japanese Garden
reviews.text: Spent the afternoon in the park and we were lucky that the guided walk in the Japanese Garden was just starting. Really interesting and well worth the visit

reviews.title: Japanese Tea Garden is gorgeous!
reviews.text: The park is huge and you can walk all day there from one end to the other. We did the Japanese Tea Garden and de Young Museum to have that special view from the tour. The rest of the day we walked in the park along the road and the lakes to get to the Windmills and Tulips to end up at the beach. It was nice and lots a of variety with the 2 bisons you can see on the way but our tens were a bit disappointed with that. They expected ore of them. It's a nice day out to see art, culture, enjoy the sun and see the beach.

reviews.title: Paused and refreshed, fully.
reviews.text: The lungs of SF, no matter where you look you will see trees. Don’t hesitate to see everything, so much, the flowers, the art, the science, and most of all, the incredible beauty sitting on sand. Enjoy!

reviews.title: Once is enough
reviews.text: Glad I went ,wouldn't make a special trip to see it again. Traffic ,parking ,a problem. But must have been interesting in days of stick shift cars.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is a staple of San Francisco. Golden Gate Park is to the City of San Francisco the same as Central Park is to New York City. There are so many things to do in the Park. You can stroll around Stow Lake, go to the Japanese Tea Garden, visit the California Academy of Sciences (that have the aquarium and the Rain forest among other places) you can visit the De Young Museum, go to the Batanical Gardens or even walk around the Park or the old wind Mills. There is definitely something for everyone. Give Golden Gate Park a try. You'll be happy you did.

reviews.title: Beautiful park, enjoy the walk or the muesums
reviews.text: Love this park, just for strolling through. Relaxing and nice to see lots of locals just out enjoying the park. Start near the Conservatory of Flowers and walk all the way through ending at the Beach Chalet Brewery.

reviews.title: So fun!
reviews.text: You could literally spend all day here, it is a gorgeous, big park! I definitely recommend the botanical gardens, it is stunning!

reviews.title: Japanese Tea Garden is a must
reviews.text: Lovely place with a great atmosphere, walking distance to Haight Ashbury street, tea house great matcha and desserts! Golden eagle in the tree

reviews.title: Good for a day
reviews.text: Grounds are big and there is something for everyone to doLots of restaurants, museums and attractions, places to visit I would recommend the AIDS Memorial Park, Japanese Tea Garden, Museum of Sciences During my visit I was forced to look for washroom outside the park as all were closed because of Marathon in park on that day...

reviews.title: Beautiful oasis in San Francisco
reviews.text: A must visit when in San Francisco. Lots of areas to explore although be prepared to pay for many of them including the museums, flower conservatory, Japanese tea garden etc. It’s big so if you want to see much then a bike is a great way to get around.

reviews.title: What a gift to San Francisco!
reviews.text: This park has so very much to offer, with world class museums, gardens, walking spaces and all conveniently located in the downtown area of San Francisco.

reviews.title: One of the best
reviews.text: Golden gate Park is probably one of the strangest, but definitely one of the best Urban parks in the country. It's got just about everything you could walk in a park. There are fantastic museums, bodies of water, wild animals, hippies, and plenty of roads and trails for hiking and bicycling. The east side of the park borders San Francisco Haight-Ashbury. So the crowd here oh, well, is very Haight-Ashbury. The west side of the park is at the Pacific ocean. Park at either end and walk to the other, but make sure there's plenty of daylight for the return trip. Or, maybe, take Uber for the return.

reviews.title: Great Day Out
reviews.text: This is a great place to wander around and fill a day. There are many attractions within the park e.g Japanese Gardens, Academy of Sciences, Segway Tours and plenty of walking trails. It is also very easy to get there by public transport.

reviews.title: Always a beautiful place to vidit
reviews.text: No matter how many times I visit this park, it never ceases to amaze. It’s close enough to my favorite restaurant by the Ocean.  The grounds are very lush right now and in the winter we can go back to see the tulip bloom by the Dutch windmill  it’s just plain beautiful and lots of places to walk on sidewalks.

reviews.title: Wish we had more time here
reviews.text: We only had a short amount of time to spend in the park. When we visit San Francisco again we are going to set aside an entire day to take in the many activities in the park. It’s beautiful.

reviews.title: very pretty
reviews.text: We drove through Golden Gate Park on our Big Bus hop on hop off bus tour. The little  that we saw, was very pretty. If you are in the area, it would be worth spending some time there.

reviews.title: Feels like Central Park of San Francisco.
reviews.text: I enjoyed most of this park. We went twice while spending a week in the city. The first time was a nice, sunny and pleasant day. It was a weekend, so the park was full. We enjoyed walking around the conservatory and seeing the one small waterfall.  Also got a nice meal at a food truck. The tea garden had a huge line so we came back another day for that and glad we did. I adored that tea garden and was a real highlight of the trip. The one day we went clear to the end with the windmill. It was middle of week and bad weather. No one really around and the area smelled like urine. Didn't stick around there long, but did enjoy the other part of the park. Overall a nice stop.

reviews.title: Glorious flowers
reviews.text: The Conservancy of Flowers and the lawns and gardens surrounding it are magnificent.  Love the folks ignoring the "No Dogs" signs.  The park is huge and very easy to get lost in; we never found the Japanese Tea Garden until we were driving out and passded it.  Be prepared to walk long distances.

reviews.title: For a unique view of the Golden Gate Bridge...
reviews.text: ...try and climb Strawberry Hill in the middle of the boating lake, the views from there are amazing! The hill itself is a butterfly sanctuary, so it’s quite pleasant in itself.The park in general is a very nice place to be- there’s a lot of different things to see. Be aware that the Japanese Garden and Botanical Gardens are paid for features. The whole park is very long and will take a good few hours to leisurely walk around.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park, SF
reviews.text: Very nice, relaxing area to walk around a lake pathway. Take your belongings out of your car, our windows were broke out and backpacks taken after returning to our vehicle. This is a Big problem all over SF.

reviews.title: Incredible park but we witnessed a car break in broad daylight.
reviews.text: Incredible park but we witnessed a car break in broad daylight. It was prett disturbing. Really e joyed the grounds until that hap poo ened.

reviews.title: Delightful many-faceted green corner of the city
reviews.text: We discovered this by chance,viewed frm the top of a bus tour. Then we went back on our own,starting at Ocean Beach (Metro) and just walked. It was a really relaxing place and clearly beloved by many of the locals-families with dogs,jpggers and courting couples among others.

reviews.title: one of the premier urban parks worth it for bay to breakers
reviews.text: My best memories of this park are during the bay to breakers footrace held annually on the last sunday in may. This is a sprawling park that has something for everyone including: museums, picnic grounds, japanese garden, plenty of lakes, windmills, etc.On the weekends you will find plenty of joggers, roller skaters, picnickers.I mention the bay to breakers because this the last portion of the 12k race which is uniquely san francisco at least in the years when i participated in the 90's. But still for anybody that wants a great walk of 12k from downtown to the ocean side its worth doing.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: A must see if you're in SF. We drove through with our tour guide, seeing many beautiful portions of this gigantic park!

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: We went through on a tour and was able to stop and look around. It's absolutely gorgeous and worth the time to go and see this while in San Francisco, even with younger kids. They loved the sites and the open spaces.

reviews.title: Still my favorite park
reviews.text: On this last visit we didn't have much time, but wanted to come walk around. The weather was warm and we ended up just walking around the duck pond. There was construction near the cross over, so we just walked around. My 6 year old niece enjoyed walking near the ducks and swans and there were turtles as well. It was a nice relaxing walk on our last full day in SF.

reviews.title: We like this park!
reviews.text: On a return visit to SF we stayed on 24th near the park. We enjoyed walking around and through the park, seeing bison and the windmills. My wife loves running and went around a few times. The location is great near the ocean at one end and Haight Street at the other. Best of all we attended Outside Lands on the Sunday, lovely weather and saw Paul Simon close the show, a good week.

reviews.title: Rampant Theft!
reviews.text: I didn’t heed the warning of a kind woman who told me that there has been break-ins of vehicles. On our last day of a wonderful vacation-our rental car was broken into and thief stole our carry-on luggage with laptops, iPads and my kids iPhones. So just please be aware- our car was parked on Nancy Pelosi Dr by the Science Academy. We were only gone about 2 hours in the mid-morning. Do not leave your rental car—it is a target!!

reviews.title: Wish we had more time here
reviews.text: Visited Golden Gate Park on a Saturday at the end of June and had a very positive impression. We found street parking on the northeastern edge of the park on a side street off Arguello Boulevard and probably could have found a spot on Fulton Street as well. It was a little short of a mile walk to the de Young Museum from where we parked and a pleasant jaunt. Be advised that the park is very large and driving from the northeast corner to the northwest corner along Fulton Street is 3 miles. The BEST TIP I have to share is one I learned from the Trip Advisor San Francisco forum: be sure to go to the top floor of the de Young Museum (no charge to do this!) to see the views of the city. The museum guards were all “cool” with the three of us and others just walking in and by-passing the admission line. This was the highlight of our visit to the park!

reviews.title: Beautiful, and Huge!
reviews.text: This is a huge, iconic park in San Francisco. We had actually gone to the California Academy of Sciences, which is actually within the park, and decided to spend some time in the park as well. Be sure to select a sunny day to enjoy the park; unfortunately, it was quite cold and foggy when we visited, so we really couldn’t spend a lot of time there. We rented the family bike (which is rather expensive) to go around the park. We had some lovely views of the rose garden and the lake etc., but riding that bike is tough!! The park is huge, and of course we couldn’t manage to see all of it. There are a lot of portions within the park which have paid entry. So plan properly before visiting.

reviews.title: Refreshing Space!
reviews.text: We walked up from the muni bus stop (short cut from the crowds of Hop On/Off bus) into the center concourse.  We enjoyed tea and snack and contemplation in the Japanese Tea Garden before entering the Academy of Science.  Great snap shot science museum with a fun combo of natural history, sea, animal and plant life, including a roof top garden and rain forest.

reviews.title: Very big park
reviews.text: Very big park for walking, biking or relaxing. Not recommended by me if you have limited time as a tourist. Just too big and not best value of limited time. But if you do have time or you are local - great place to visit on a regular basis.

reviews.title: Very Nice and Great Playground for Kids!
reviews.text: This is a huge park!  We have visited the Japanese Gardens and Botanical Gardens which are beautiful. The latter has the largest flowers and roses I have ever seen!  There is also an awesome playground for the kids with a carousel (extra $), various slides, zipline for little ones, ropes to climb and swings. Bring a piece of cardboard so that they can slide fast down the natural stone slide. You can also bring lunch and drinks for a picnic. Awesome place. Check their calendar for other events!

reviews.title: Very nice park
reviews.text: We spent several hours roaming around the Golden Gate Park.It is one of the best.  Particularly enjoyed the dog park.  Must have been 70 dogs in there.

reviews.title: Just gotta take the stroll
reviews.text: Only touched the tip of the park near Haight Ashbury but took a nice stroll thru the park. Lots of open space and picture moments. Ran across some locals bowling and kids riding the slides on cardboard boxes. Glad we stopped.

reviews.title: A Park Like No Other
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is a free park similar in shape but larger then New York's Central Park. Within the park is the deYoung Museum, the California Academy of Sciences, the Japanese Tea Garden (oldest public one in the US): all requiring entrance fees. Statues abound through out the park along with two windmills, lakes, a 1914 carousel as well as a botanical garden. Don't miss the conservatory of flowers for its 1879 building alone but also for the stunning plants. It's a lovely spot to rent a bike for a sunny day, picnic or visit one of the many attractions. Check what events are taking place. There is always something.

reviews.title: Wonderful Area
reviews.text: We visited the Japanese Tea Garden and walked through the park. It is huge and better to ride a bike to see a lot more. All the arrangements of the plants are amazing and beautiful.

reviews.title: Ran right through it
reviews.text: Ran the Second Half of the San Francisco Biofreeze Half Marathon, and ran through Golden Gate Park.  It was exceptionally beautiful, and I encourage anyone to stop by and spend a few days there.

reviews.title: Gorgeous!
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is a really wonderful place to visit on a sunny day in SF.  There are several wonderful museums:  the science museum and the De Young, plus the flower conservatory, or, you can just enjoy the beautiful scenery and relax in the park.  If you go to the De Young, be sure to take the elevator up to the top of the tower to take in the amazing 360 degree view!

reviews.title: A couple of hours in the park
reviews.text: We could have stayed much more in the area. We visited the fort: very nice view on the bay and the bridge. Some history to share with kids.Some walk around to see the bridge again. And finally the palace of fine arts. There is more to see obviously, but we didi not have enough time.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: Plenty of road side free parking but it fills up early. One hour walk from one end to the other. Beach at the end.

reviews.title: Sprawling
reviews.text: Pretty great park, can spend a whole day here finished doff with a lovely beer at the restaurant by the sea.Only problem is it is SO big, if you exit randomly, you'll likely find yourself in some residential area no where near anything. So take plenty of beers for hydration.

reviews.title: Gorgeous Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: This has to be one of the most beautiful city parks in the country. We loved the Japanese Tea garden ($7/ adult). We found several of the museums to be very expensive so we didn't see them. We tried to get information at one booth, but unfortunately the volunteer there was misinformed about the park. We walked great distances, but didn't really know how to access this great resource. An information booth should have been there with options affordable for families to participate.

reviews.title: Such a beautiful park
reviews.text: We loved spending a few hours here. You could totally spend the whole day if you wanted to. There is a lot to do and see even for the kids. My kids loved the playground. It’s a long walk from one side of the park to the other so if you have children bring a stroller. We rented a bike but it was so crowded that it was hard getting around peacefully. Overall, loved this park and would absolutely go back again on our next visit

reviews.title: Time-off
reviews.text: Finally a place which is quiet, calm, relaxing and not overcrowded. If offers so many attractions, Botanical garden, Science museum, playgrounds,...I took bus to the beach and walked from there across the park. It was like in a dream!

reviews.title: Lots of nice places
reviews.text: Having just driven through in a tuor bus, but it seemed a very Nice Place to visit for a picnic or walk. Impressive, almost unbelieveble to learn about the work and creation of the park.

reviews.title: Beautiful break from the city!
reviews.text: Only being in San Francisco a few days, we planned to be at Golden Gate Park for half of a day.  That wasn't near enough time.  We maybe only made it half way through the park!  It is HUGE with so much to do and see!  Things like the Conservatory of flowers, Japanese Tea Garden, DeYoung Museum, Stow Lake, etc. took us more than half a day!  We were disappointed that we couldn't see and do everything.  We loved how beautiful the grounds were, which were well labeled with many signs and maps.  This is a must do if you are ever in San Francisco, but I would reserve an entire day if you can!  Another helpful note is that there are some areas that have an admission fee such as the botanical gardens or the Japanese Tea Garden and other areas where you can rent bikes, boats, etc.

reviews.title: so much to see and do in this beautifully diverse park
reviews.text: There is so much to see and do in this beautifully diverse park that cuts across San Francisco from the Pacific Ocean to the Haight!The art and science museums, the playgrounds, the lakes (Stow Lake is my favorite), the meadows, the Arboretum, the Japanese Tea Garden, the bison, hippie hill, the merry-go-round, the windmills, the scenes of beauty, the feeling of peace.

reviews.title: Nice break
reviews.text: Wonderful way to get off the busy city streets. Take a Segway tour. It was so much fun and really very easy to operate.

reviews.title: Pleasant walk
reviews.text: Teens loved the park. Easy transport by bus. Entry free but museums and Japanese tea garden have entry fees. Conservatory and smell of flowers great. Kiosks for snacks and hotdogs. Academy of Sciences took 2.5 hours as teens loved to read and assimilate information.

reviews.title: A Must Do in SF
reviews.text: I'd say Golden Gate Park is a must if you're in San Francisco. Plenty to do and see, relaxing, a variety of attractions, indoor and out.  We went twice in five days and only saw half of it.   Easily accessible by bus from all parts of the city.

reviews.title: California in a nutshell
reviews.text: Golden Gate park is an amazing and beautiful place. I first visited a few years ago and we explored the beautiful botanic gardens. Just walking across the beautiful greens was spectacular. Last week we visited the California Academy of Sciences museum. The entry price (substantial at $36 for adults) provides a full day of entertainment. There is an aquarium, a planetarium, and many natural history exhibits. We had a delicious and surprisingly reasonably priced lunch at the cafe. We especially loved the rainforest exhibit with all the butterflies. I highly recommend.

reviews.title: Nature, calm, green, fitness, tai chi
reviews.text: I just can say this place is awesome, totally a must in SFO, the Botanical Garden catch you and the environment is so beautiful. I truly recommend to give a complete ride around and enjoy the morning 😊

reviews.title: Large Area
reviews.text: We went here as part of a local bus tour. Hard to believe it was all man made. Nice area. Only disappointing point was the Japanese Tea Garden had a change to enter. We did not do that.

reviews.title: Segway tour
reviews.text: Loved it. It was totally awesome. We all took to the Segway like fish to water. Entire group of people in the tour, some in their 60s (8 in all, unrelated) were all comfortable using the Segway. Tour use Uber fun. I would do it in a heartbeat. Tour guide Jeff was super fun. I would give the experience 10/5

reviews.title: Beautiful walk through all the gardens
reviews.text: We walked all over Golden Gate Park, enjoyed tea in the Japanese Tea Garden and enjoyed ourselves thoroughly

reviews.title: Large, beautiful and diverse park
reviews.text: This park is very much worth a visit.  It is free (although the botanical garden and Japanese tea gardens and museums have entry fees), and it offers diverse opportunities for sports, walking, hiking, botanizing, photography, picnicking and year-round special events.  We only got to see a small part of this splendid park, but look forward to spending more time on our next visit.  I should mention that I had my cell phone out taking pictures and out of the corner of my eye I saw a man seemingly angling towards me and when I switched hands he veered to my other side. Perhaps it was a coincidence but when I put it away, he walked away.  You might want to keep an eye out and keep your phone, purse or camera close.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: So many places to walk. Beautiful outdoor space. Well used by all the local populace. We enjoyed all the huge trees, the many flowers blooming and the rose garden.

reviews.title: Beautiful Park
reviews.text: It was a beautiful day walking through this park, stopped in at the museum and continued our journey through the gardens.  This is a must see in San Francisco!

reviews.title: Yet another free national park done right
reviews.text: Not to be missed and a great place with interesting and approachable engineering exhibits and explanations. Quite windy and a bit chilly even in July on the bridge, and too many tourists obv, but not be missed. Great views near the 1st tower. Free presidio crissy field ride is good. Dont take the presidio hills route which is a waste of time. After than catch the free downtown bus from Presidio transit center.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: We traveled to Golden Gate Park and the views and the sights were incredible. Take a jacket as the wind coming off the bay is chilly

reviews.title: Japanese Tea Garden
reviews.text: I really enjoyed the garden once I got past the cashier who was very rude to me after taking my money.  I asked if there was a map and she gave me a dirty look and just waved her hand at me like keep moving.

reviews.title: This is must!
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is wonderful. This place is so beautiful you can spend hours of time just strolling through the acres and acres of green or just take a nap if you need a rest. I love the atmosphere, so many people, so many gorgeous views. The park is huge! We especially enjoy picnics on the park. Take a basket and fill it with yummy delights then head over to the Park. You’ll definitely have a GREAT time!!

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: We stayed in the Sunset area and walked to the park every day. There is so much to see-the botanical gardens, the Japanese tea garden, museums, etc. it was great to spend time in the city and then walk through the park. The views atop Strawberry Hill are worth the short, steep hike, not to mention the waterfalls you can see on your way up. This park is a must-see.

reviews.title: Easy to get lost - but don't miss!
reviews.text: The city is not good about signage.  You are likely to pass right by the location you are looking for without realizing.  The botanical gardens, tea garden, and conservatory are a plant-lover's paradise.  Lunch at the museum was delish!

reviews.title: Free Park
reviews.text: I had wasted several minutes looking for the parking lot. There is no need to do so since there are some places that you can do street parking. The park is huge, so at least bicycle is recommended if you want to hop around a few spots. The park is huge and free. It would be an ideal place to do picnic or even a lunch bbq. With the timing right (seasonwise), rose garden would be very beautiful.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: If you want a relaxing few hours in lovely surroundings, this is the place, so quiet, so beautiful, nice for a picnic

reviews.title: One of the best
reviews.text: This park is really big and nice.It is the best place for cycling or walking for a long time and so smooth.It has different parts with different kinds of flowers  and they are changed with changing the season and I definitely recommend it.It has a contemporary museums like De Young and botanical garden that are nice to visit.

reviews.title: Very nice
reviews.text: This park had a lot to offer.  Gardens, golf course, walking trails. Etc.   I thought it was the best San Francisco had to offer.

reviews.title: One huge park
reviews.text: I didn't realise how big this park was until I got there. It has 3 golf courses, Botinical gardens, Japanese gardens and much more.It's poorly signposted both for motorists and pedestrians (there's almost a complete lack of signposts for pedestrians and I seemed to ask for directions at every turn) and very expensive to park. Unfortunately it's also home to lots of homeless people.Don't let my negative comments put you off, it's a fun place.

reviews.title: Nice park
reviews.text: well kept nice and the science museum is built in it. so a good place to go sit and relax before of anfter a visit.

reviews.title: Beautiful Way to Spend a Day
reviews.text: The history of this park and the transformation of this local area is fascinating. Learn the history and then tour the park to appreciate it even more. There are many things to do for all ages. It is very clean and well maintained. A wonderful place to spend a day with the family and friends.

reviews.title: What's Not to Like?
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park in a San Francisco Icon. In the park is the DeYoung Museum, The Japanese Tea Garden. The North American Hall, the Arboretum, the Planetarium, and on and on... It is not a one hour venue, nor a one day venue, but it IS a place you can return to again and again and never tire of it. I strongly recommend going to the park foranyone who likes adventure. There is something for everyone in Golden Gate Park.

reviews.title: Wonderful Place
reviews.text: I only visited a fraction of this vast park which is one of the best I´ve ever seen. On top of the enormous variety of plants in the park itself, the Botanic Gardens and Japanese tea garden, there are other attractions well worth visiting such as the De Young Museum and the Academy of Sciences Museum. There are lots of places to eat or have a picnic. My only regret is that you generally have to pay to get into these although the Botanic Gardens was free when I was there. This can make a day out a bit pricey especially with a couple of kids.

reviews.title: Beautiful Park!
reviews.text: So much to see and explore. If you want to get lost there you could all day long. Rent a bike and enjoy discovering all the treasures it has to offer!

reviews.title: Plan on visiting here
reviews.text: Golden Gate park is a must for all tourists and residents.   It has something for everyone from the garden lover to kids to animal lovers.  It is a huge park great for running and cycling or just having a picnic.  We ate at some wonderful restaurants just south of the park as well.

reviews.title: Walked the entire park
reviews.text: So we walked the entire park from east to west, about 1.5 hour, some stops for pictures   It was nice lots of variety, also nice for biking etc.

reviews.title: Drove though - Didn't stop
reviews.text: Beautiful Park which we had allowed more time to explore this park   Wanted to go to the Tea Garden but didn't have enough time.  If we ever return that will be first on the list.  Heard it was amazing.

reviews.title: Out of this planet
reviews.text: No words to discribe this area.Please, take at leat, one day to visit this place. It has many good things to enjoy. Bring some food and do a pinic and relax.

reviews.title: An enticing variety of activities and sites.............
reviews.text: Expect to spend about 4 full days if you want to do all of this great attraction, which includes miles of walking and biking trails, restaurants, museums, a giant greenhouse and a diverse and lush vegetation throughout. There is easy access to the all of the park plus free parking. Best advice: be sure to obtain a map of the park before you go. The weather was perfect while we were there, but a rain/wind jacket is advisable.

reviews.title: It was such a pretty park, I loved the crytal glass hothouse and comments on Aussie gumtrees!
reviews.text: Twice I heard the guide complaining the introduction of Australian gumtrees using all the water in the park,so I commented that they exist in a 7 year drought in the Australian outback with no water,they have tap roots but are the last thing watered.It has a pretty lake you can hire a paddle bike for fun.Its trees are varied and landscaping more or less let grow lush and some very old trees.

reviews.title: Expensive
reviews.text: Beautiful huge park but beware, very expensive as you have to pay to go into some of the gardens.The Japanese Tea garden is lovely but the tea and snacks very over priced

reviews.title: Loved it here!
reviews.text: On our last day in San Francisco my husband and I knew we wanted to make our way to the Golden Gate Park. We hopped a cable car downtown, hopped a bus and thanks to the nice bus driver (directing us to the next bus stop that would get us there) we made it. I knew I wanted to explore the Japanese Tea Garden. I wanted to just take our camera and shoot away. We were not disappointed at all. We love parks and this one is now high on our list of great parks to visit. I would recommend putting a visit here on any tour itinerary!

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: We visited the Stowe Lake inside the park. The boathouse is charming and there are canoe and paddle boat rentals. There is a great walking path around the lake, which wasn't steep at all and took about 45 minutes to get around walking at a strolling pace. There were geese with babies as well as many other birds. There were quite a lot of flowers in bloom for the time of year. It is a beautiful and relaxing place to visit.

reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit, rent a bike if you can!
reviews.text: This is a beautiful part of San Francisco and we spent 4 hours cycling, sitting and drinking coffee. It's a lot larger than you expect, but the good news for anyone cycling is that it's not too hilly! Highly recommend a visit!

reviews.title: Lots of fresh air & fun.Great views.
reviews.text: Nr Haight & Asbury. Walk on into the Park. Lots of open spaces & things to do.Go and find the de Young Museum. There is a free entry viewing area on the top floor. Pass the lines for entry to the exhibition & walk around the rear, take elevator to top floor.36  degree viewing area.Worth the trek.

reviews.title: Nice Park
reviews.text: Despite having been to San Francisco twice before, it wasn't until my third visit that I finally came to the park.  We didn't walk around too much but we circled the park by car and saw sooooo many people taking picnics, jogging, walking, etc.  We went to the Academy of Sciences and that was a majority of where we spent our time at the park.  My aunt & uncle have apparently been to some concerts and gardens in the park, loving them all.The park is 20% larger than Central Park but I don't find it as walkable or nice.  Still, like I mentioned, there were so many people - certainly thousands.

reviews.title: Plan to spend a whole day!
reviews.text: So much to do in this park we were so suprised! We uber-ed there which I recommend because parking seemed very tight. We did the BEAUTIFUL botanical gardens & the Monet exhibit at the Art Museum. The area around the park has some cute restaurants and shops. The grounds were very well kept and ended up being our favorite part of our visit to San Fran!

reviews.title: Too much to see, do, experience and it's all wonderful!
reviews.text: No matter what your interests are, something in this phenomenal park will make a visit worthwhile.  Whether it's simply the assortment and arrangements of plants, the museums, or the ability to exercise in a beautiful setting.  This park is excellent.

reviews.title: Wide open spaces
reviews.text: Despite there being a lot of people around, we never felt crowded. There is tons of space and lots of beautiful plant life to experience with sunny or shaded areas to sit and quietly enjoy.

reviews.title: Great urban park
reviews.text: We spent a couple of hours wandering the park and paid a visit to the DeYoung Museum.  It is a truly great urban park and a wonderful respite from the otherwise very urban environment.

reviews.title: Visit it
reviews.text: Lovely park. While you're there, be sure to stop at the deYoung art museum and the Japanese Tea Garden. Both charge for entry, but are worth the cost.

reviews.title: walk
reviews.text: Had a nice walk here today. The weather was perfect, sunny & warm with a slight ocean breeze. A nice thing to do & a different view of the bridge

reviews.title: It's Huge and stunning
reviews.text: We only saw a small part of it, but it is huge like Central Park in NYC, you could easily spend all day there, perhaps hiring a bicycle to get around  (available at the gate), would be idea.

reviews.title: Family Time
reviews.text: Golden gate park s filled with amazing destinations. Stow lake, Botanical gardens, Spreckels lake, conservatory of flowers, etc. Take a #1 California bus, 2 Clement bus, 38Geary bus and exit on 6th AVENUE. Clement and 6-8 Avenues has numerous Chinese take out foods. Gourmet Dim Sum and Good Luck Dim Sum are great!! Cash only. Order your baked pork buns, shrimp dumplings, egg rolls and chow mein etc at Gourmet Dim Sum, great price and delicious! Either place among many are great. Fill up that pink bakery box and walk into golden gate park on Fulton Street. Clement,then Geary then Anza, Balboa, Cabrillo and then Fulton Street. You will see numerous places to sit and enjoy your food. Buy a cheap bag at Goodwill on 10th and Clement and a straw blanket at another Chinese dollar store in clement . You will have a great day!!!

reviews.title: So much to see
reviews.text: Park has so muchThe trees that span from the haight to the oceanThe littke lakesThe cultural places luke the musuems the tea gargen the house of flowers the festivalsThe carosal and kids play plays

reviews.title: Fun and Educational
reviews.text: It is a great place to kill some time. While strolling the park you see different kinds of trees, plants and even animals. It is very educational in a fun way and i enjoyed most is getting in touch of the nature

reviews.title: Fun place for everyone
reviews.text: This park is huge! Lots of things to do for everyone and anyone. My favorite would be the children’s park. Lot of over size hermit crabs, a giant fish & nice big waves to play. There’s this really cool slide made out of cement with lots of cardboard of help go down thF slide! My 3yo couldn’t stop climbing up the stairs to slide down!

reviews.title: Nice park area with some museums
reviews.text: We were on a tour stop so we only had 45 minutes. There is a science museum, art museum, play grounds, and a japanese tea garden. You have to pay to get into each. It’s a park where a lot of runners and dog walkers like to go to.

reviews.title: Magical and Green with Prospects of Privacy
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park, an immense expanse of gardens that continues from the beautifully, white-carved intricacy of the Conservatory of Flowers through multiple paths ad gardens, past the excellent Art Museum, all the way to the ocean, is a jewel. It’s a place any visitor to San Francisco must visit. Absolutely do not miss spending hours, or, better yet, a full day here. It’s the perfect place to walk, meditate, visit art, admire formal gardens and follow pathways that loop beneath many types and shapes of trees. It’s a haven, a cathedral to nature, an unforgettable space.

reviews.title: Come and Enjoy
reviews.text: The Golden Gate National Park is a wonderful place to see the Bay and the Golden Gate Bridge.  Take the time to relax and ride a bike or just stand and  watch the Bay and the Birds not to mention the people. On a nice day you can see people surfing at the base of the Bridger. Don’t forget to stop in at the Warming Shack and Snack Bar for some refreshment and to sit and get out of the Bay wind.
