The profits are all for a good cause – The Golden Gate National Park Conservancy.

reviews.title: great great great!
reviews.text: have a walk, a ride, visit the Conservatory of flowerss or just stroll around this lovely park that offers everything for a grest outing finishing at Ocean beach with the Holland Windmill

reviews.title: Not what we expected
reviews.text: This park is pretty, but goes on forever, so don't expect to hike from one end to the other.  There is also a ton of greenspace with not many attractions or things to see or do in between.  It's not like Central Part in New York.  After walking almost 2 hours, we eventually called an Uber to take us to Ocean beach because we weren't even half way through the park.

reviews.title: Gorgeous Park
reviews.text: Massive park with some stunning little books and crannies, definitely worth a visit.We were there in February so the evenings were a little chilly but the sun was shining and we managed to find a large pond with birds and a waterfall, we sat down after a lot of walking and took in the scenery, it was so calming and tranquil.We only saw a tiny part of the park so can only imagine what the rest is like given its size, the place is HUGE!Would love to come back and make a proper day of it and hope that one day, I will.

reviews.title: A Gem
reviews.text: This park is huge and includes lots of things to do, as well as just beautiful landscaping to enjoy on a stroll, run, or bike ride.  Very well-maintained.

reviews.title: Lots to see and do
reviews.text: Such an amazing space to explore. So many things to see and do.Everything from japanses tea gardens, to Chinese pergolas, and bison!Definately worth a visit, plan a whole day so you can take in all there is to see and do in a relaxing manner

reviews.title: The park
reviews.text: Beautiful gardens in a very big and busy city. A botanical oasis.  Parking along streets. Picnic on many benches, enjoy the many flowers.

reviews.title: Huge!
reviews.text: That’s lots to do here and very big park. You could easily spend all day here. Various food and drink places and little areas to go see. Worth a visit if you have some time!

reviews.title: A good day out
reviews.text: There is plenty to see at this park, and it is very easy to reach by bus.  You will need more than half a day to see it all.  Plenty of walking involved.

reviews.title: Beautiful park, lovely to visit
reviews.text: Still a great place to visit! I was fortunate enough to attend the Bill Graham Benefit Concert here many years ago. Large open space, plenty of great spots to picnic and relax. Bring your walking shoes, a blanket, a good book and a smile. Enjoy!

reviews.title: A large park in the city
reviews.text: The large park is minutes from the city. It has botanical gardens, Japanese themed garden and a lot of walking and running trail. A good place to savor the gardens, have picnics and/or have walks or run. People watching is also suggested.

reviews.title: Better than Central Park
reviews.text: Having gone through the Park on the tour bus I was blown away by the facilities on hand. What a wonderful location and well maintained.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: Beautiful acres of landscape and open space right in the middle of the city, the botanical gardens green house was especially  interesting and we loved that there were so many other places to see and do inside of the park compound.

reviews.title: Nice Escape from the City
reviews.text: This is the first place we visited during our weekend stay in San Francisco.  It was a great place to start the day.  There are a large number of trails that take you past a  variety of wildlife and flowers.  We started our visit with a hike around the lake and to the top of Strawberry Hill, which offered a panoramic view of the city and the Golden Gate bridge.  Our kids loved walking on the stepping stones near the waterfall. We also walked to the Japanese Tea Garden in the park and then drove to the windmills.  We were able to do all this in less than 4 hours.

reviews.title: A huge Park with more things then you'll be able to find
reviews.text: For many Golden Gate Park is something they just drive through. Or they've heard about it in a story or a book or TV show and think they have a picture of what's in Golden Gate Park. Well I'll say this no matter what you think's in there, there's a whole lot more. Depending upon the time of year there are many things that bloom around the park tulips bamboo trees, all kind of flowers, and a whole bunch of things I haven't found yet. There are windmills made in honor of Queen wilhemina, there's a buffalo Paddock with buffalo in it, there's a science museum the living roof, and a planetarium oh, there are walking trails oh, there are running trails, there a bike routes, and many buildings to explore if you can find where they're at. It's a long Park and goes all the way to the ocean, and in between the winding roads bring so many things. Come early for good parking. Come early for free parking. I have had a good time every time, and we'll be back for more Good Times. Sometimes it's the science museum, sometimes it's the flower gardens by the windmills, sometimes it's just a walk in the park

reviews.title: Beautiful park, Japanese Tea Garden is a Must!
reviews.text: This park was beautifully designed and has been excellently maintained. There is plenty to offer here for families, such as the playpark near Robin Williams meadow, and the California Academy of Sciences museum (incl. a dinosaur display!). Personally, I was enthralled with the Japanese Tea Garden which is beautifully curated and actually does serve teas and small snacks! I'd recommend renting bike and riding around on a Sunday because it's the one day of the week where they close the park to car traffic. Gorgeous!

reviews.title: Incredible Park
reviews.text: Even though it was a cloudy and colder day in the high 50s, Golden Gate Park is a wonder. We only had time for the Botanical Garden (free Tuesday) which was spectacular in mid May, the Monet Last Years exhibit, and walk around the Academy of Sciences area. It deserves several days to explore and enjoy.

reviews.title: nice Japanese tea Garden
reviews.text: A pleasant visit in the month of April. The garden is located in  the middle of Golden Gate Park, which is 20% larger than Central Park of New York. The garden is very well maintained and was clean. Flowers bloom and birds chime. It requires about an hour to strode along and take photos. The best part is the admission free before 10 AM.

reviews.title: The sun is shining and all is beautiful!
reviews.text: People always talk about the cold summer weather in San Francisco. Here is my take on it....layer up and have fun! If you don't like the weather wait a few minutes. It will change. I highly recommend wick away clothing. You can be warm when it's a bit cloudy and windy and then good when the sun emerges. I always bring a light sheet to lay down on the grass and snacks and water. The view is epic and the people watching even better. It's simply a great place to chill, especially on a clear day.

reviews.title: Beautiful spot🌴
reviews.text: The Golden Gate Park there’s many different spots big big park many different places to go and walk many different places for the children to play together ⛲️♥️ gorgeous park plus horse stables 🎻

reviews.title: All free
reviews.text: Worth the trip out for a break away from the city. You have to pay for the better areas (conservatory of flowers, botanical gardens etc) but there is ample parking and picnic space. If you have children the play area is great.

reviews.title: Interesting area away from the city
reviews.text: Take the number 5 bus from the city and it drops you outside. This is a very large park, goes all the way to the ocean. The glass houses are a must see

reviews.title: Amazing park area!
reviews.text: This park is huge and has many different areas to it.  ie. soccer fields, gardens, historic windmills, trails.  Too much to mention.  Very clean as well.

reviews.title: Botanical gardens are wonderful
reviews.text: I walked around the botanical garden for over an hour one recent morning. It was so peaceful and beautiful and I really appreciated the zen like calmness. Great place to meditate or just relax. The grounds are immaculate and it is hard to believe you are in an urban area.

reviews.title: Allow a whole day
reviews.text: We didn’t really do this park justice only arriving mid afternoon Easter Sunday - so missed the music which was about 1pm. The area we saw was mainly grass trees and a lake with some poppies outside the conservatory. No other flowers. There was an admission charge for the conservatory of flowers, the botanical garden and the Japanese Tea Garden. None of which we did. That Park was really too big to explore it all late in the day. So my advice is to spend the day there and be prepared to pay for each individual section.

reviews.title: One of my Favorites
reviews.text: I love San Francisco. One of my favorite places in the city in the city is Gold Gate Park. It is beautiful to walk around for exercise or just a casual stroll. The are many pedestrian friendly pathways. I enjoyed walking by the pond watching paddle boaters enjoying their afternoon. The Botanical Gardens is filled with flowers and interesting plants. I did just, on this visit, stumble upon two Dutch Windmills at the edge of the park. However, my favorite part of the part of the park by far is having tea at the Japanese Tea Garden. There is an admission fee of about $9 to walk around the garden. I think it is worth it. There is a Coy Pond, pagodas, flowers, bridges and shaded pathways with benches. You can also enjoy tea and treats. There is also a gift shop.

reviews.title: Can't imagine San Francisco without it
reviews.text: From the botanical gardens to the De Young museum to the free music, this is a beautiful place with something for everyone. A nice escape from the more hectic aspects of the City, and definitely a respite from touristy places.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: We had a walk at the golden gate park and we enjoyed it. The park is so big and we had a Segway tour at the park. It was fun and informative. We didn’t have a chance to visit the Japanese tea park.

reviews.title: Verdant Jewel of SF
reviews.text: Regardless of weather or season, one should spend time at GGP to marvel in the beauty and serenity of this 150 year old city oasis. Granted-San Francisco in general is a beautiful city-but the park provides literally miles of green lushness for you to run, walk, or drive through, or better yet, to plop down in for a picnic or a respite with a book and maybe a bottle of iced tea or rosé.One of my family’s favorite places is Stow Lake, because we enjoy feeding the waterfowl and strolling around the lake and environs. Recentlymy elderly dad fell near the lake despite using his cane. While I sat with him on the ground waiting for him to stabilize enough to get up, several passersby stopped to inquire if they could help. A group of four men and a woman helped me get Dad up and to a nearby chair. What does that incident have to do with GGP? Well-the Park is a place where the community comes together to enjoy nature among fellow San Franciscans. On that day, I was reminded of our good fortune to be residents of this great city and to have such kind and caring neighbors-strangers though they may be.

reviews.title: Sweet and nice place
reviews.text: Good to visit in the evenings.A place for peace and fun.Can really enjoy a lot.Location is also good

reviews.title: Cycling disppointment
reviews.text: Maybe after extensive cycling the day before over the Golden Gate Bridge and around to Tiburon and on the Embarcadero and in the city we were expecting too much.We were expecting a ride in a park literally not a ride mostly on roads shared with motor vehicles The trails we did ride on were poorly marked (as was the park mostly) and we got the feeling that the park administrators were ambivalent about visitors on two wheels not being on the road.Our hire bikes were past their use-by dates with worn tyres and brakes and needing replacement. In the end we just wanted to get them back.All sounds negative but this was the lowlight of our visit to San Francisco.

reviews.title: So much to do here you can't list it all
reviews.text: As a city park, this is larger than NYC's Central Park.   With great landscaping and lots of museums and places to either explore, or just sit and enjoy, allow at least half a day to see the sites here.

reviews.title: Enjoy hours at Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: A beautiful Japanese Tea Garden with blooming cherry trees. A very interesting museum, de Young, with a Monet exhibition and a tower of free access and magnificent views. The California Academy of Sciences museums with a varied offer to children, teenagers and adults. People dancing old time melodies here and there. Exuberant vegetation, painters, picnicers and all kinds of activities. Unforgivable not to go there on a sunny say.

reviews.title: Stunning outside space
reviews.text: Having spent a few days visiting the city, getting out to this lark was a welcome relief from the buildings for me! I was surprised to find it so tastefully designed, maintained and with interesting features to explore! It was a very romantic to wander the paths, enjoy the plants and wildlife, and discover the various different areas. We visited the Japanese garden whist here as well which is well worth it also.

reviews.title: Girls Trip 2019
reviews.text: Very nice park. So much to see. I only viewed the Japanese Tea Garden. Was a little disappointed. I thought it would be much larger.

reviews.title: Plenty to see and big enough to escape the crowds
reviews.text: We happened to (unintentionally) choose the annual 4/20 day for our visit to the park, completely oblivious... until we got there. However everyone seemed in good spirits and we soon left those crowds with a walk to the tea gardens then on past some of the lakes and open fields before eventually making it to the beach. Even on 4/20 and with thousands heading to the all day concert the park is so large you can escape the crowds. After a five mile walk from one end to the other though we did call upon Uber to get us back to our hotel but a very enjoyable walk it was before that.

reviews.title: The  "Queen" of  SF parks!
reviews.text: Whether hiking ,  biking, horse-back riding, or  boating,  Golden  Gate Park has  it  all & in  every season! Gardens  abound, blooming  all  year  'round! Museums,  too,  can be  visited- all  within the  Park. The  Arboretum,  is a botanical garden most rare for  its redwood  trees, in  addition to gardens one  would  see all over  the  world!

reviews.title: Lots of activities
reviews.text: There are so many things to do in the park I can see why it’s so popular.  We walked to the botanical park and the tea garden.   Unlike NYC there are actually restrooms available, and nice picnic tables.  You have to share the bike path, but people seem to be pretty forgiving.

reviews.title: Beautiful park worth the time
reviews.text: We visited GG Park with our teenage sons. They enjoyed our brief time their seeing how SF residents enjoy the green space in their city. The Japanese Tea Garden closes in the late afternoon so plan your visit accordingly.

reviews.title: One of the World's Great Parks
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is one of the world's great parks in the Western Part of San Francisco. The park stretches from the Richmond and Inner Sunset Districts, near the famous Haight Ashbury Area and ending at Ocean Beach, the Outer Sunset and the Outer Richmond/Precidio Areas. At the Ocean there is famous Cliff House on one end and the Windmills at Judah/Outer Sunset District on the other end, with great sand dunes and wonderful sun sets, thus the District name. In the center of Golden Gate Park there is the Botanical Garden, japanese Tea Garden, Academy of Sciences Museum and other great museums and places to explore. Golden gate Park is a must visit place on any visit of San Francisco.

reviews.title: Just go it’s lovely
reviews.text: The park is stunning for a walk cycle and explore. There is lots to do and the scenery and atmosphere is fab. If your visiting you must go and take it all in

reviews.title: Pretty but confusing
reviews.text: Nice area, but for some reason the trails seemed so confusing.  We kept having to pull our google maps out to figure where we were.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: A beautiful park.  Lovely to walk through.  Its so great that the locals and toutrist alike have this wonderful park to explore.  We went to the De Young for the Monet exhibit and next to it was the Japanese Garden with the trees in full bloom.  Just Beautiful!

reviews.title: Huge expanseof parkland.
reviews.text: The largest park ion San Francisco and lots of walking to see all the sights. Park has a lake with paddle boats to hire and a rsetaurant. Other sights are the many play areas, golf course, flower exhibits, chinese garden etc. You need time here. Name is deceptive as it is not that close to the Golden Gate bridge. Well worth spending time here.

reviews.title: Enjoy a day of bicycling in the park
reviews.text: Bicycling is such a fine way to explore this park.  We had our own bikes, and I don't know about bike rentals, but assume that there are some. Take a picnic lunch.  Stop at the deYoung Museum, California Academy of Sciences, botanical gardens, any number of smaller attractions.  It is a great way to experience some of the history of San Francisco and to people-watch.  From one end to the other, it is about 8 miles (our calculations), but the many side attractions can make it into a 12 mile ride on relatively flat terrain. We started on the East side and ended up at the Beach Chalet for lunch... A beautiful early spring day.  At least on a weekday, the roads are reasonably un-crowded and there are special bike paths that take you on an adventure.

reviews.title: Relax and spend the day!
reviews.text: So much to see in GGP!!!  The windmills are spectacular!!!  Plus you can stop by the buffalo paddock!!!  There are several there. Take s stroll through the Japanese gardens.  Gorgeous anytime of the year!!!  The conservatory of flowers is stunning!  The building was badly damaged in storms several years ago and repaired to it’s original beauty.

reviews.title: Central Park of San Francisco
reviews.text: A lot to see in this park and very close to the Botanical Gardens.  People relaxing, sometimes a bit too much as we encountered a man relieving  himself in the middle of a path.  Not sure he was homeless either.  Other than that a nice peaceful place to talk a stroll

reviews.title: Always a treasure
reviews.text: Hats off to the person who had the idea to develop the park and to the politicians who made it a reality.  It’s a delight to visit and (as I do) drive through it daily.

reviews.title: Oasis of calm (cliché alert)
reviews.text: It's a beautiful park, so much to see and do. Or you can just stop and chill and enjoy the sunshine (weather permitting).  It is huge. To visit all parts you either need a bike, or 2 or 3 days on foot.  But well worth it for kids and adults alike.

reviews.title: Don't overlook
reviews.text: This park is beautiful and has world class museums. Although the creator of the park hated sculptures in nature, others can appreciate art and nature in one great setting.

reviews.title: Must Stop Photo Stop
reviews.text: It is too beautiful to miss while in the bay area! Take some time to enjoy the city without bring in the city ;)

reviews.title: Excellent day out
reviews.text: So much to do, from barbeques, pedal boats, Lindy hop dancing and beautiful gardens. Well worths visit. Amazing to see so much wildlife in such close proximity to everyone also.

reviews.title: Nice run at the park
reviews.text: The park was very clean and well maintained.  I ran around the park (inside loop) and it was a nice route.

reviews.title: Golde Gate Park
reviews.text: GG Park should be added to one of SF's must see areas to visit.  The summer music events held in GG park are generally free and offer a variety of fun and music to satisfy all visitors.The music offered can range from local talent to big name performers.  (Sheila E, etc) In the summer all you need to bring are your blanket, chairs and eats!!!  And of course beverages!!!!  They will usually have all types of vendors available so you can purchase anything you forgot!!!  You mingle with folks that actually live in the area, as well as lots of outsiders.  This makes the visit even more enjoyable, when you end up with new friends from all over the world!!  Nothing is more enjoyable, than good entertainment and sharing the experience with new people.  Music is universal!!!!

reviews.title: Pleasant place to sit or to walk around
reviews.text: This small park was lovely to walk around or sit and relax for awhile. You can watch the swimmers braving the cold water and admire some of the old ships docked nearby. Quiet place to gather your thoughts or jsut to admire the scenery

reviews.title: A must visit for SF from local resident
reviews.text: Enjoyed the beauty of the park on Saturday.  Some streets in the park closed to auto traffic on Sunday,  highlights to visit are the California Academy of Science and the Dejoung Museum.  Across the concourse from each other. We saw the excellent Monet exhibition at the Dejoung yesterday. Nice walking opportunities abound. Be sure and go up in the Dejoung observation tower for a 360 degree view of the City. Admission is free.

reviews.title: Very popular park
reviews.text: We toured the park via segways on a nice Sunday afternoon and it was packed with people. It was very pretty with some interesting areas, unfortunately I was too busy trying not to run someone over on my segway to see all the sites. I'd recommend walking.

reviews.title: Japanese Tea Garden
reviews.text: We enjoyed driving around  this nice park seeing all of the interesting trees.  We saw the Japanese Tea Garden and decided to visit.  We have a huge amazing one at the Missouri Botanical Garden in St. Louis if you are ever in St. Louis.  This is nice because it is compact, has nice simple trails and you get to see some very pretty trees and shrubs and nice buildings.  The cherry blossoms were blooming and they were beautiful.  Definitely worthwhile.

reviews.title: Unique Urban Park
reviews.text: Golden gate Park is, as compared to other parks around the world, pretty unique. I'd say it's even a bit more unique then Central Park in New York. if you start at the foot of Haight Street, the Eastern end of the park, and walk all the way down to the Pacific ocean, you will cross through some of the most bizarre and diverse Park settings that you could imagine.You'll find true blue, 1960s hippies on hippie Hill. You'll find 1970s roller skating going on in the park. There are giant open Fields where you can picnic or just lay out on the grass. There are cattle, and there are lakes stocked with fish. There is even a world-class art and science museum. Then, as you approach the westernmost side of the park, you'll find giant windmills reminiscent of Denmark.

reviews.title: Long walk
reviews.text: Beautiful park. My 17 yr old didn’t find it too exciting though. We walked around, ate some food (but finding food wasn’t that easy).

reviews.title: Nice park
reviews.text: Huge park, nice to wander around. We were amazed how expensive it was to visit any of the buildings eg flower display. We did visit the Academy of Sciences which was great

reviews.title: Huge park
reviews.text: We went to this park in January with our son & his wife & grandson. We couldn't believe how big the place was!! It's much bigger than Central Park in New York!!! You can drive through it or walk. We stopped at the visitor center & walked around the shore to see the Golden Gate Bridge. The visitor center had good displays & the staff was happy to answer questions. We had limited time so weren't able to see much of it, would definitely like to go back & spend more time there!

reviews.title: So many things to do here!
reviews.text: You can visit a museum, walk through gardens, enjoy wildlife, or just relax. There as many choices as there are miles to explore.

reviews.title: Love this Park
reviews.text: Beautiful, safe, friendly and so very much to see!!Great walking and bike riding.We will be back to explore more!!!

reviews.title: Beautiful Space
reviews.text: Absolutely take the time to explore this beautiful green spaceIt’s very peaceful.  Lovely walking paths and cleanLoved it

reviews.title: The Soul of San Francisco
reviews.text: Much like New York's Central Park, Golden Gate Park is the place San Franciscans come to play.   Its sprawling lawns host soccer and touch football games while bikers enjoy the roads through the park. Add the beautiful botanical exhibits at the gardens and consevatory, the  world class art at the DeYoung Museum and the animals on display at the California Academy of Science, and you could fill a week without leaving its borders, but you'd want to go beyond to nearby restaurants serving a variety of cuisines that represent the diverse tastes that feed the city's heart and soul.  For us, it is a spring traditional to visit the botanical gardens. We head to the deYoung when an interesting new exhibit is on display. Street parking can be tough but we've never had problems getting parking in the lot that serves the CalAcademy; increase your chances to find a space by getting there before 10 am, especially on weekends.

reviews.title: A Must Do - On any List!
reviews.text: Truly this is the most unbelievable park I have ever been to....!  Like Central Park,  it is man-made and dates back to 1871 - and the  turn of the century.  At one time, it had been uninhabitable land of sand dunes - now it is an incredible paradise of nature.  We had the great fortune of spending an afternoon here - on a Segway Tour that left from the Music Area of the park... We went in gardens that were exotic and remote, around lakes, and to the important landmarks.... the deYoung Museum (featuring Monet), the William Shakespeare Garden (with plants and flowers mentioned in his plays), a serene Aids Memorial grove of remembrance, a Music Concourse with a huge band shell, the Academy of Sciences (with a living roof), the Japanese Tea Garden, the Botanical Gardens, and the Conservancy of Flowers.   Hippie Hill, a gentle sloping green space - overlooking Robin Williams Meadow -was the site of the Summer of Love in 1967 - and hosted musicians and bands like Janis Joplin, the Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane, and George Harrison.  (It is still used as a concert/event venue to this day.)   There are so many other places - just on the Eastern Part of the park, that we did not even have time to sample.... There are reportedly two windmills on the west side of the park - and tulips in bloom in March.Throughout our travels, we witnessed the genius of John McLaren who is credited with planting over two million trees within northern California - and taming the wild lands into this beautiful park... Exotic species were brought in from around the world and grown within the park's boundaries.  Today, we were told that the park employs 300+ gardeners...and it is indescribably beautiful with walkways, lakes, gardens,  blooms and blossoms everywhere! It is truly one of those places one needs to visit many times - but will appreciate from the moment you arrive....A fabulous hint:  the tower at the de Young Museum is free.... From its vantage point, one can see in all directions - in the park and to the city beyond.  (just follow the signs inside to the elevators...)A caution:  We had a lot of problems with Uber Drivers not being able to "locate us" - even though we were right at the east entrance of the de Young Museum.

reviews.title: Fantastic Experience in nature
reviews.text: You can spend the whole day there, so much to do and so much to see, if you love nature and exploring the park, you must visit the Japanese Tea Garden is a must-see, with Palace of Fine Arts, the art museum, the science museum

reviews.title: Tranquil spot easily accessible from downtown.
reviews.text: On a sunny day, this is a lovely place to wander and chill. The botanic gardens are delightful and we loved the old carousel, at 2 dollars a ride for adults and 1 dollar for children, it’s a bargain! You can walk there or get a no7 bus, also very cheap.

reviews.title: One of the Best City Parks
reviews.text: My husband and I decided to walk from one end of Golden Gate Park to the other. We took the Muni bus to the start of the park and went through the Botanical Gardens and Japanese Gardens. We then kept walking towards the Pacific through miles and miles of this beautiful park. It was a week-day, so many of the paths were relatively empty.  What started as a sunny, blue-sky warm day at the top of the park, turned into chilled cloudy fog as we neared the ocean.  Most of the walk is down-hill, and there were bikes for rent as well. When we reached the windmills and ocean at the bottom, we exited the park and took the Muni Bus back to our hotel. The gardens charge an entrance fee, but the rest of the park is free. It was a lovely way to spend an afternoon in San Francisco.

reviews.title: A must do
reviews.text: An incredible diversity and a must - just remember to truly embrace you need to spend the day and bring your walking shoes

reviews.title: Lots to do.
reviews.text: Amazing park. The space for children to run around in and burn off energy is vast. Through out the park there are lots of separate areas, from children's play areas to gardens to explore or to sit and watch the day go by. We only got to see a small section of the park the main area being The Japanese Tea Garden which was spectacular. The Pagoda's could do with some refurbishing but the whole area was stunning.

reviews.title: Lovely open space
reviews.text: Great park for outdoor activities and picnics. Great movie screening in the summer. Very busy at weekends

reviews.title: Best seen by bike
reviews.text: I hired a bike a cycled around the park,  I started at the bike hire from a rental place close to the Ferry building. The city's cycle lanes make it easy and safe to get there. I hadn't been on a bike in years and wasn't sure about cycling in the heavy traffic.  But I felt fairly safe using bike lanes.

reviews.title: Golden Gate park
reviews.text: This is one of SF biggest heart. So much to see and do here that it may be impossible to all the activities. Tea Garden, Conservatory, the Aquarium, AIDs Garden, ocean Beach even a fun little 9 hole golf course (best in the AM).

reviews.title: Great from a bus !
reviews.text: Although we were on a bus trip , the journey around the park showed us all sorts of things. It looked like a lovely park but the weather was against us. Lovely trees and plants and historic sights.

reviews.title: A day here is a day in Paradise!
reviews.text: So much to do in the park. Arrive early and there is plenty of parking on the street (4 hr). The museums, flowers, running, walking, and green beauty surrounds you!

reviews.title: Huge park
reviews.text: Massive park with a lot of different activities. Clearly popular with the locals for running, cycling.... A nice green area in San Francisco.

reviews.title: Spend days here!
reviews.text: This parc has almost everything! Museums, attractions, lovely green areas, botanical garden, nice walks and whatever one could wish from a park! Prepare enough time!

reviews.title: Love this park - gr3eat place in the city
reviews.text: I love the deYoung Museum, the Botanical Gardens, and just walking around. You can take a city bus to/from almost anywhere. Uber is also available, and not expensive as the city itself is surprisingly small.

reviews.title: So much to do and see!
reviews.text: Long rainy day of walking in the park- Saw the bison, one of the windmills, de Young Museum, Botanical Gardens and Japanese Tea Garden. Loved all of it. I would rent a bike or segway if I returned again.

reviews.title: So Much
reviews.text: I had the opportunity to walk the full length of Golden Gate Park (boy do my feet hurts). Sadly it was raining when I got there so I opted to skip some of the gardens. But soon the sun came out and the park was full of people: joggers, bikers, walkers and tourists. There is a shuttle that goes through the park but I never found out what the route was. The real draws are the Academy of Science and the De Young Museum and both places were hopping. The lakes and ponds are well maintained as were all the grounds. Definitely a must.

reviews.title: More that a day to see and enjoy it all
reviews.text: A wonderful space to walk, enjoy the vies and see locals enjoying themselves. So many places to visit/ When we were there there was a wonderful Monet exhibition at the De Young which would have been worth coming to San Francisco for on its own. But walk and if you get tired ride the free shuttle bus.

reviews.title: Refreshing Experience
reviews.text: The Golden Gate Park in San Francisco is a public park and is bigger in area than the Central Park in NY city. It is a pleasure exploring this park by just walking around. There are several things to see within this park. It is truly a refreshing experience.

reviews.title: So many things to do in Golden Gate Park, make it a day trip!!
reviews.text: The beauty of Golden Gate Park is the sheer size of the place. From the beach end up to Haight Ashbury end there is all kinds of stuff to do there. There is the Japanese Tea Gardens to walk through and see all the flowers and ponds. The Academy of Science Museum is fun to walk through and the de Young Art Museum is an art lovers destination. We loved the Conservancy of Flowers that has a giant old school botanical gardens of all types inside. Its a full day, probably two.

reviews.title: Beautiful Park
reviews.text: Rode around to take in the scenery of this absolutely huge park. It is a beautiful place and has great story behind how it was built from barren hills.

reviews.title: A gorgeous 1000 Acres with 10 Lakes!
reviews.text: I’ve been exploring new areas in SF in an effort to socialize a foster dog. Although I have been to the museums and gardens, I had never spent much time walking around the lakes. There are 10 of them - I had no idea!! Lovely walkways, varying terrain, water life, birds and a mix of facilities available. A lovely way to spend an hour, an afternoon or a day!Golden Gate Park is an underutilized gem in a city that is not short on beauty. EnJOY!

reviews.title: Its beauty comes from its position in Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is big. It's close to 50 city blocks from east to west and 4-5 from north to south. There are many attractions including museums, gardens, the Botanical Gardens (aka the Strybing Arboretum, one of the jewels in the crown of this much-jewelled city. My favorite places are: 1. the arboretum, free to local residents but inexpensive to tourists and one of the best anywhere in the country; the canopied-by-trees space between the De Young Museum and the Academy of Sciences; and Stow Lake, with its island which has a pagoda and is suitable for jogging and walking, where you can hire a boat or simply sit on the edge watching the ducks and geese and seagulls. Of course there is a huge variety of trees and birds everywhere in the park. Sometimes it's good to walk - and you can walk for miles here, accompanies by people in lovely solitude. There is a bison paddock, children's playgrounds, polo fields, and a stables where you can hire horses or go on a hack during the summer. To my mind, the museums and the tropical house in the picture above are replicas of better institutions elsewhere in the US or Europe. It might be said that Europeans (and I include Brits) will be disappointed by the De Young and Academy since their home versions are likely to be bigger, more comprehensive and, ironically, more culturally cutting-edge.

reviews.title: Expansive with Attractions Included
reviews.text: We took a bike tour of Golden Gate Park and learned of its history and took in the beauty on a gorgeous sunny day.  The California Academy of Sciences, de Young Museum, Botanical Gardens were all included in the park.  We stopped and entered the Botanical Gardens for a delightful visit.  The Park itself is huge with ponds, grassy open areas, tons of trees and plenty of opportunities.

reviews.title: An heaven of peace
reviews.text: The park must be seen from spring when the flowers are out, but it is an heaven in the town (or rather on the side of the town), with great museums, a lovely Japanese garden, lakes, walks, picnic areas,...We also were fascinated by the bison paddock.

reviews.title: Huge park with lots of attractions
reviews.text: Beautiful park, you can spend hours walking through it's pathways. There are some museums and attractions inside the park but those are way too expensive

reviews.title: Beautiful and so much to do
reviews.text: This park is such a beautiful, unique park with so much to do from walking/running, museums, canoeing, to botanical gardens and more. The scenery is breathtaking easily one the top 3 best parks I’ve been to in the world (compares to Central Park NYC, Hyde Park London, Vondelpark Amesterdam, etc). Spent either half day or full day here so worth it. Walking the length of park will take a couple hrs but well worth it.

reviews.title: Great big park
reviews.text: Love the park. It is really huge. You will need time to fully explore it. Plus there are other things inside the park. But you can still explore without paying.

reviews.title: Awesome park
reviews.text: If you know Hyde Park, then Central Park, you just need to enjoy Golden Gate Park... awesome, with nice museums inside, it deserves a planned visit with enough time to walk along

reviews.title: Two Windmills
reviews.text: I'm a windmill freak and was surprised that the park had two authentic Dutch windmills--both were amazing.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: We rented bikes and rode through the park. Fun adventure. Wish we had more time. Beautiful place. So much to see

reviews.title: Beautiful and Massive Park! Worth a few steps to see it!
reviews.text: Staying in Richmond district, we decided to take a walk through Golden Gate Park all the way to Ocean Beach.  It took us a few hours but was well worth it.  This park has everything! Paddocks, angling lakes, roller bladers, a cycling track, a polo/soccer field, a museum & café, Japanese Gardens, lush green fields, windmills fitness stations and lakes to name a few things!Reaching the beach at then end was the icing on the cake!

reviews.title: Nature's Beauty
reviews.text: Had the opportunity on a recent trip to enjoy Golden Gate Park. This is a must off the concrete path of the city and has many beautiful paths to enjoy with gardens and museums. It by far beats the usual tourist sites of the city and is an enjoyable scenic delight. There is an observation tower (elevator) at one of the museums to get a panoramic view of the entire city to take photos of all the different parts of the city. Well worth your time!

reviews.title: Huge Green Space
reviews.text: This is the most green you will see in San Francisco. I’ve heard the park is bigger than Central Park. Lots of trails for biking, running, whatever you’re up for. Fields of grass for romping. The views of Golden Gate Bridge from the Bay Area of the park are beautiful!

reviews.title: Great place to spend the day
reviews.text: The park is beautiful.There are many interesting options for things to do, like the Academy of Sciences, the Japanese tea gardens and so on.You can also find a quit place to just sit around and rea a book.Lovely.

reviews.title: Amazing park
reviews.text: Beautiful spot in SF full of surprises.  From windmills to buffalo the park has a lot to offer including de Young

reviews.title: Mahoosive
reviews.text: This is a little gem in the city. There are plenty of things to do in this park without even putting your hand in your pocket. They even have a Bison enclosure... Bison in San Francisco. We wondered around whilst looking for the big bus stop. If you don’t like walking...... stay away. I’d imagine in the summer it’s absolutely stunning.

reviews.title: What a park in the city
reviews.text: The sheer size of place blows your mind as its in the middle of San Francisco. So many things to see and do. This place is so big it's got its own complimentary transport to get you around the park. But it's worth going on a weekend and walk it to see all that's going on . What a facility.

reviews.title: Another way to blow through a day
reviews.text: I highly suggest taking the street car down Irving towards Ocean Beach and walking the length of the park back towards the university. Stop at the Devils Baking Company to load up for breaks...nothing better than sitting in the grass and having a snack lol. Even just wandering around the East end is a great experience, even on a busy Sunday I was able to explore the trails/ stay away from the crowds.

reviews.title: Amazing if you love long walks in the nature
reviews.text: The Golden Gate Park (far from the Golden Gate Bridge) is a very very long park. You should really go if you like nature and long walks. We walked for hours across the entire park until we reached the beach facing the ocean. The walk back was another 50 blocks, but still enjoyable. Plus a good way to keep fit :)

reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.text: Great happy adventure Park is huge Happy happy new year Year of the peace and harmony Many interesting things

reviews.title: Japanese Tea Garden- Stunning
reviews.text: What can I say about this place....Its simply stunning!What a lovely little hidden gem. Had a wonderful time.Definitely worth the entry fee. Everyone should visit this place when in the vicinity.

reviews.title: Outstanding
reviews.text: This area is well maintained, and has a lot to offer.  The Japanese Tea Garden is magnificent as is the Botanical Garden and the Conservatory of flowers.  The free shuttle that runs on the weekends is great to get around to the different places.

reviews.title: Just lovely
reviews.text: We spent several hours here, brought a picnic lunch and enjoyed a great time.  They have a very nice playground for children.  I took advantage of a walking trail.  There are public bathrooms.

reviews.title: You can forget you are in the city
reviews.text: Very pleasant break from the city traffic, lots to visit inside the park and free shuttle buses at the weekend if you can't walk the full 3 miles long.  Japanese garden was particularly nice.

reviews.title: Didn’t expect this
reviews.text: I didn’t expect the park before the bridge. The drive was awesome and the trees were so cool. Do it.

reviews.title: Wonderful urban park!
reviews.text: So many hidden gems within Golden Gate Park: the conservatory of flowers, Japanese tea garden, and many museums. You could easily spend the whole day and then some exploring this park. Note: kind of a misnomer, Golden Gate Park is NOT surrounding Golden Gate Bridge. The bridge is 3 miles from the park.

reviews.title: Nice..
reviews.text: Very different from parks we are used to. We thought this would be a fairly walkable park but were definitely mistaken, it is a lot bigger than we were led to believe and there are a lot of roads throughout which made it quite hard to get fully lost and enjoy the park experience. We had also read there was plenty of places to rent bikes (around and in the park) to ride through on but this wasn’t the case either, we were half way through the park when we found a bike rental and had already decided to leave. Over all it was nice, pretty and clean but not what we were expecting at all. I would call it more of a collection of small parks or gardens with stuff in between, than an actual park.

reviews.title: A "must" in St Francisco!
reviews.text: Exciting experience, the Golden Gate is an absolute icon. Plenty of possibilities for visiting, we rode by bike all along

reviews.title: A beach, rebuilt!
reviews.text: This park which is worth hours and hours of visit has everything: sports arenas and horse areas and buffalo (!) and lakes and archery and model boathouse with special lake and fly-fishing ponds and and and....a model is in the Beach Chalet.  Made in the 1880s by Scot John McClaren, it originally was a beach.  The "night dirt" of SF was sent to this area by train, and the soil of the park was created in this way.

reviews.title: Loved it
reviews.text: It's such a large park you could walk round it all day. I particularly enjoyed the Japanese tea garden which is $9 to enter but is very beautiful.

reviews.title: Quite the central park
reviews.text: Started a day of touring the city in this area. Impressive park. Very reminiscent of New York City's. All sorts of paths and facilities. Well worth spending some time exploring corners and crannies.

reviews.title: Wonderful park!
reviews.text: We visited Golden Gate Park during our SF visit.  The place is amazing!  Unfortunately it was raining on and off during our visit but that didn't stop us.  We enjoyed the beautiful landscaping and went to the Flower Conservatory.  That place was such an enjoyable place to be.  The whole park is super family friendly we saw joggers, families with kids in stollers, biking and dog walkers.  Very enjoyable

reviews.title: Too Much Beauty
reviews.text: So much to see and so much to take in. The beauty will take your breath away. It shows how a true park should look. One can feel completely alone even surrounded by people. The layout is superb.

reviews.title: Amazing views
reviews.text: There are so many places to get a great view of the bay, the bridge, and the whole area. Wasn’t too crowded when we went on a Sunday morning. Good location to park and then walk the bridge. Clean restrooms and easy access from the 101. Enjoy your day.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: We walked around and enjoyed the beautiful nature amongst the big city. The Science Museum was amazing!

reviews.title: You haven't seen San Francisco if you don't explore Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is the city's garden and playground. There are numerous sculptures, meadows, lakes, picnic areas and secluded spots to enjoy a private moment. In addition there us the Japanese Tea Garden,  the de Young Art Museum, the California Academy of Sciences....plus the Rose Garden, Conservatory of Flowers, the Bison Herd (really!) and you can rent a row boat on Stowe Lake. And, out near Icean Beach there are two working Wind Mills with flower gardens that were built more than 100 years ago and refurbished in the last 20 years. Whatever you're looking for in a city garden you can find in Golden Gate Park.

reviews.title: More than a Park.
reviews.text: It is another excellent place to see in San Francisco. It is a picturesque area.  You can find beauty in beauty!.  Very nice place to take pictures and videos.  It is unfortunate not to see this Park.

reviews.title: Lots to see and do
reviews.text: We went here as part of our Hop On Hop Off tour. We spent hours here. The Japanese tea gardens are beautiful. The Buffalo paddock is cool.  The Museum & Conservatory of Flowers worth the trip. The gardens and sculptures are huge and beautiful. There are food trucks there too.

reviews.title: Great place to wander around
reviews.text: Visited during our recent trip to San Francisco.  We followed a self-guided walking tour from our guide book which we really enjoyed.  The park is clean & felt safe.

reviews.title: Something for everyone!
reviews.text: Whether its the pond, biking, the De Young museum, watching people to Tai Chi or reality jousters just playing around, the water falls, the lovely trees and parks....there is truly something here for your entire family to enjoy. We walked this park for several days and kept discovering new things!

reviews.title: From Parks to Art - There's something for everyone.
reviews.text: In your visit to San Francisco, be sure to take a day and spend some time at Golden Gate Park. There is plenty there for the youngest to the oldest to enjoy. Paddle boats and a snack shop will make the young ones happy and the de Young Museum has much to love for teens and young adults. Don't miss the observation tower at de Young to get a full 360 view of the city!

reviews.title: Must See!
reviews.text: The park is beautiful, we went on a sunny, cold day early January and it was wonderful. The Japanese Tea Garden inside this park is very tranquil and pretty. Worth going and exploring.

reviews.title: New Years Special
reviews.text: We met our friend at Golden Gate Park while on vacation in S.F. over new Years. Two attractions were free.The De Young Museum and the Flower Garden.We only had time for one so we went to the museum. It is a beautiful place with many galleries and lots of variety in art forms.Take time to go to this museum in the morning and into the city in the evening!

reviews.title: What a beautiful park
reviews.text: Spent some time here and was impressed by the actual size and diversity of this park. It was very pretty place to wander and it was greta to see so may people and families enjoying the area.Well worth  a look.

reviews.title: This place is huge
reviews.text: I didn't even cover the whole thing but very cool place to visit. You could spend many days here and see many things without leaving this area. Be prepared to spend some time. Visited in August 2017.

reviews.title: Breath of fresh air
reviews.text: This is such a well put together and well maintained park. There's loads to do in it. Well worth it to get a break out of the city

reviews.title: Central Park West
reviews.text: A beautiful park in he middle of a beautiful city.  Whether you are enticed by museums, aquariums, botanical gardens, cultural attractions such as the Japanese Tea Garden, statues of previous leaders in music, and countries alike or, wish to visit a few sites so important in the 60's and hippie movement, you will find it all here.  Enjoy my friends and do not forget to wear a flower in your hair.  PEACE!

reviews.title: Super visit with wonderful weather!!
reviews.text: This was a Christmas visit and the weather was great.  Lots to see and the views are great.  Such a wonderful relaxing place to visit.  So many nice people to meet.  Take the time to visit, enjoy the park and you will have great memories.

reviews.title: Country in The City
reviews.text: If you are an outdoor person and especially traveling with children, GG Park is a must do for you. From the Panhandle (beginning east end) to the Ocean (west end to watch a sunset) it is a 3+ mile walk, run or bike to explore the beautiful mini gardens (e.g. rose, dahlia), Japanese Tea Garden [savor a cup of tea], Botanical Garden and Conservatory of Flowers; enjoy a paddle boat ride [a children favorite] on Stow Lake; art at the Fine Arts Museum (aka DeYoung); science and natural hx at the CA Academy of Science (see an albino alligator/children love this place/good caferteria); ride the carousel by the tennis courts; watch the Bisons; participate in a variety of lawn sports/even golf; and Dutch windmills. When you reach the ocean, take care of your hunger pains & thirst at the Beach Chalet Brewery & Restaurant - maybe see the sunset if you time it right. On weekends & holidays there is a free shuttle bus that stops at the major attractions. Also, the main thoroughfare is closed off to traffic.    Or simply pack a picnic lunch and pick a spot to enjoy the peace and tranquility of nature. It is easy to get to by public transport from downtown SF on the #5 Bus to 8th Ave & Fulton (middle of the park where museum, Japanese Tea Garden, CA Acad of Sci, Botanical Garden are located). There is something for every body.

reviews.title: Best place for a run
reviews.text: I went for a run by myself through The Panhandle and Golden Gate Park on a rainy Saturday morning. There were heaps of runners out, and most importantly I felt very safe. (I was visiting from Australia.) This is not what I expected from a big city park. It is superb! Whilst I know it is not natural, it certainly feels it. I love that it is not a well manicured botanic garden type park. It is big - you can find any distance run you like. It is pretty flat, and there are heaps of paths to take. As someone who has been running forever, this is definitely one of my favourite runs ever. I highly recommend it for a walk or a run. It is also a great place to go and relax solo or with friends and family. Lovely, lovely haven in the city of SF.

reviews.title: Beautiful park to cycle through to the beach
reviews.text: We rented bicycles from the cycle shop, Avenue Cyclery, which was much better than the tour companies. From there, we cycled though the park all the way to the beach. It was a Sunday, so the road we were on (JFK Drive) was closed for cars, which made the experience so much less stressful. The park is beautiful, and there is lots to see. At the beach, we got a coffee from the Beach Chalet, then cycled back up. The return journey was a bit hilly, but generally doable. We’ll definitely be back to see the things we missed.

reviews.title: Highlight of our visit to SF
reviews.text: The park is beautiful and a wonderful way to escape from SF the city into SF the California coast. The botanical gardens are off the scale amazing, so well organized and labeled. Make sure you get to the scent garden, never experienced anything like it. So many plants with strong and alluring scents, too many to try to list. Best 3 hours of our time in SF!

reviews.title: We had fun here
reviews.text: We rented electric bikes and went through the park to ocean beach....it was pretty but lots of cars, the bikes are what made it great

reviews.title: Taylor trip
reviews.text: Great open space - we visited the  Japanese Garden. It’s lovely albeit that any enjoyment of the peace and tranquility is spoiled by the crowds. Admission is charged ($9 per adult we think) and the tea room is quite expensive. This is not a cheap day out. We took an Uber from the centre of the city which was quick and cheaper than it would have been in the uk - it is advisable however to specify a location you want to be dropped off at. We just said the park and effectively got dropped off in the middle of a wood!

reviews.title: Beautiful scenic park
reviews.text: The park is full of beautiful scenery & a variety of activities inside the park. You can see bison (on loan from the zoo), a botanical garden, & the flower conservatory. Great park for walking, riding bikes, or renting segways or mini cars.

reviews.title: Simply magnificent!
reviews.text: This place is so beautiful and full of splendor!  Great for families or a great stroll in the park. There’s something for everyone here.

reviews.text: Art enthusiast, tree hugger/nature lover, science buff, casual perambulator, picniker... the attractions are endless.  Enjoy and have fun surrounded by some of nature’s best offerings.

reviews.title: The vision of John McLaren
reviews.text: I imagine that like me, most visitors would be amazed by the sheer size of Golden Gate Park – at over a thousand acres, it is actually 20% larger than New York’s Central Park. Close to fifteen million visitors come to the park every year. This park dates back to the late nineteenth century. Today, it is hard to believe that before 60,000 trees were initially planted here, this was just an expanse of arid sand dunes. The credit for this goes to the vision of John McLaren, this park’s superintendent for over fifty years starting 1887. The first major event held here was the California Midwinter International Exposition in 1894. The park's most famous attractions including the Japanese Tea Garden and the building that later became the de Young Museum came up in those very early days.The Golden Gate Park demands at least a full day of exploring. This park is quite literally miles of green, dotted with lakes, trees, flowers and more than 7000 kinds of plants – all in the heart of San Francisco! Apart from the famous Japanese Tea Gardens (please see my review of the Japanese Tea Gardens), Golden Gate Park is home to many others including the Botanical Garden, Rose Garden, Tulip Garden, and Garden of Shakespeare’s Flowers (embellished with quotes from Shakespeare’s works). The Conservatory of Flowers is an indoor garden of rare tropical plants housed in what is reputed to be the oldest glass and wood Victorian greenhouse in the Western hemisphere – close to a thousand butterflies flitter around as you walk through here. There is also the AIDS Memorial Grove set up in 1988 to honour the millions of people affected by AIDS, which was later designated by Congress as a national memorial. Built and maintained by volunteers, this happens to be the first AIDS memorial set up anywhere in the United States.While here you can also visit the California Academy of Sciences which is quite an experience – a natural history museum, planetarium, aquarium, a living rain forest, a coral reef system. Right across from the California Academy is the art collection at the de Young Museum – a collection of American art spanning the 17th through 21st centuries, plus art from other continents as well. The 9th floor Observation Level of the Hamon Tower at de Young Museum offers a spectacular view of the city and the Pacific Ocean. While admission to Golden Gate Park is free, both the California Academy and de Young are ticketed attractions.Other attractions in the park include:Stow Lake – a man-made lake where pedal boats and row boats are available on rent. Great place to while away an afternoon.Strawberry Hill – this island in the middle of Stow Lake is the highest point in the park. If you take the Rustic Bridge or the Roman Bridge and walk up to the top of the hill, your reward is an excellent view of Mount Tamalpais in Marin County and the Golden Gate Bridge. Buffalo Park – where you can see the majestic American bison roam in an open habitat.Beach Chalet – located steps away from the Pacific Ocean – enjoy the fantastic ocean view at this place where you can also have lunch or dinner.Spreckels Lake – a wonderful place to jog or stroll around, or just sit down and relax under the Monterey Cypresses.Hippie Hill – having acquired some notoriety for the flower children who gathered there in the 1960s, the meadow and the slope are a good spot to relax and watch people go by.Music Concourse – was built to stage the performances of the California Midwinter International Exposition of 1894. Don’t miss the statues of historical personalities lining the concourse. One of the high points here is the grove of pollarded elms, maples and walnut trees.San Francisco’s amiable, invigorating weather makes Golden Gate Park a great spot to tie the knot. The park authorities are happy to suggest the many locations available here where thousands of couples have exchanged their wedding vows in these sylvan surroundings.

reviews.title: Multitudes of attractions to savour in the sylvan paradise
reviews.text: A marvellous and vast park with an abundance of interesting attractions. We enjoyed strolling in parts of the fabulous amenity.We took in some of the sights, including the Academy of Sciences and de Young institution, both excellent.

reviews.title: Stunning Park
reviews.text: This park is so beautiful! Definitely go see if you can, there's lots to see in the park. The de Young museum is amazing, and houses a beautiful collection of art.

reviews.title: Nice place, with a lot to see
reviews.text: Loved going up the De Young museum for the 360° view of the city, and unfortunately did not have enough time to visit all the different places (garden, exploratory museum, etc.).  Need to plan a full day to visit everything there.

reviews.title: Loved the park
reviews.text: Unfortunately I wasn’t able to spend much time hear, but there’s lots on offer from museums to botanical gardens, Japanese tea garden, the bison paddock, and lots of lovely park land and beautiful walks down to the coast/sea ( I didn’t have time for this unfortunately)I got the bus from the city centre, walked into the parked and visited the Japanese tea gardens, it was very well kept and relaxing, I also had tea in the Japanese tea house while watching the coi carp fish. After I took a walk though the park, past lakes and boating lakes to the bison paddock

reviews.title: Nice for kides
reviews.text: That is a big park in front of golden gate .kides enjoy here becoz it has a big garden and other activities also

reviews.title: Lovely huge park
reviews.text: There are so many beautiful places in this park and I especially enjoyed the spectacular views from the de Young Museum (free). My favourite place was the quiet Shakespeare garden with flowers mentioned in his plays, beautiful trees and the Bard's bust.

reviews.title: Beautiful Walk!
reviews.text: Even in December the walk through this park was awesome, lots of yummy fragrances from different flowers and herbs!

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: This park is huge!  Something I would have never even known was there if I didn't take a hop on hop off bus tour.  A pretty part of San Francisco and some cool history to go along with it.

reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.text: The science academy, is a must see, a fantastic experience for family’s, the hands on experience for children is fantastic.Having experts on hand to explain things is great. We will visit again.

reviews.title: Best day of the trip
reviews.text: There is something for everyone in this amazing park. The art museum, the science museum, Japanese tea garden, or just strolling around. It is a wonderful way to spend a day.

reviews.title: we enjoyed driving around it
reviews.text: This was my 1st time driving in the park and we had a great time as it is a big place with many big trees, big lawn areas all in the City! The park is a great place to escape the noise the stink and fast pace of the city.  the beach area is very nice - yes we parked and walked around here and there to enjoy GG park

reviews.title: Not to be Missed
reviews.text: GGP is one of the most beautiful parks in the country, only rivaled by Central Park in NYC. The Botanical Gardens are gorgeous any time of year, not to be missed, the Conservatory of Flowers (above) is a hot-bed of tropical plants, and currently they are having a light show reflected on the glass panes nightly, two world class museums, the DeYoung Art Museum with exciting exhibitions and the Academy of Sciences, designed by Renzo Piano, has a tropical forest, filled with butterflies, colorful birds, and a planetarium, and an aquarium not to be missed. Stow Lakes is popular for traversing and paddling boats in the warmer weather. Lastly are the buffalo. Rental bikes. And there's more!

reviews.title: Bike Ride in Golden Gate park
reviews.text: If you like to bike ride and are in SF on a Sunday, one of the main streets in GG Park (JFK Drive) is mostly closed to traffic.   Find a bike to rent and take a leisurely (and mostly car-free) ride from the Panhandle (near Stanyan St) all the way out to the Ocean.   It's downhill on the way to the Ocean, then mildly uphill (but not much work) on the way back.   It's a total of about 10 miles for this round-trip.    And lots to stop at -- including the brew-pub at Ocean Blvd, about 500 feet south (turn left) along Ocean Blvd.     Enjoy!

reviews.title: Great Place For A Walk!
reviews.text: I was touring the city on the HopOn HopOff bus and I got out to walk around Golden Gate Park.  Lots to see and do and beautiful on a nice, sunny day.  I would recommend getting to Golden Gate Park via public transit versus trying to drive in and park!

reviews.title: Lovely Park
reviews.text: Even in December, there were lots of plants to see.  It is a vast place with a remarkable variety of very happy plants.

reviews.title: 17% vehicle burglary happened in Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: Do not leave anything inside your car. Our car window was broken and a camera was stolen. Called 911, but Policemen didn't show up. The park looks peaceful, but it is a crime site. Be careful!

reviews.title: An amazing variety of things to do here
reviews.text: A treasure for a city where space is at such a premium.Paths available for walks and biking vie with a world class art museum and a Japanese garden.Be warned- free parking is tough to snare tho there is a pay lot available

reviews.title: Oasis of the city
reviews.text: This 3.5 mile long and half mile wide park stretches from the Haight to the Pacific Ocean and is marked with nooks and crannies.  Highlights are De Young Museum, California Academy of Sciences, San Francisco Botanical Garden, AIDs Memorial Grove, Japanese Tea Garden, Conservatory of Flowers and a century-old carousel.  Worth walking around to enjoy the highlights.

reviews.title: Nothing particularly special but it was right next to the museums
reviews.text: The park is nothing special but a pleasant spot to relax in between going to the Museums. The Academy of Sciences does an incredible evening on Thursdays 6-10pm which has music and beers - would highly recommend!

reviews.title: Great drive!
reviews.text: Huge trees, a herd of bison, great views of the ocean. Lots of hiking trails-- what isn't to like here.  We would have liked to explore more.

reviews.title: Magnificent Park
reviews.text: Very large park with lots of things to see. You could easily spend an entire day here just  walking here and there. There are impressive views from the top of Strawberry Hill of San Francisco. If you like big trees and very fresh air then you will love it here.

reviews.title: Fun times in GGP
reviews.text: Visit the Botanical Gardens and the museums. Take your time and bring your patience as many others will be there. So much to see. Can be a nice place to relax.

reviews.title: Great walk
reviews.text: Had good 5 mile walk through this park to the ocean.  Get the number 5 bus from Powell street.  Just a shame it’s more geared for the cars than the pedestrians as we had to walk on the pavement on the roadside quite a lot.  Super little cafe near centre by boating lake.  Very cheap too!

reviews.title: Don't limit yourself with Japanese Tea Garden!
reviews.text: It is an amazing park and greatest place to spend times during week-end. Everyone wants to go to Japanese Tea Garden to take some pictures but still you don't have to spend that much money to enjoy the park. There are many amazing places in Golden Gate Park which are free to enjoy with great views and nature. Go to Botanic Garden, and Strawberry Hill. But still, you can try Japanese Tea Gardens as well for less than 10$.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: There are a multitude of places to take in at the Golden Gate park; The Japanese Tea Garden, The Flower Conservatory, The California Science Museum, The Botanical gardens....All were high quality and very enjoyable.  The fee for entrance to each was $9 and there were a few food trucks available as well as a cafe at the Art Museum.  Plan to spend around 4 hours here.

reviews.title: Wish I could have spent more time here
reviews.text: Beautiful green space inside a crowded city. Was in the park for a morning race but could have easily spent the better part of the day here.

reviews.title: Rent a bike
reviews.text: We walked the entire length of the park, which was a mistake since it was only part of our day. To explore the entire park, a bike would have been so much better particularly when there are miles and miles where there isn't much to see but green and the road right next to the walking path. We loved the East side of the park, particularly the Gardenia Garden.

reviews.title: a great few hours drive n see
reviews.text: this was on my list of places t see - sadly we just toured and stopped about the West side as time got away from us. the Zoo will have to wait as it was closing in an hour after we toured the park. We really enjoyed going in and around the park, never did find the tea gardens but went by the location twice according to the map.  we are genuine tourists lol

reviews.title: Walk , Walk and more walk
reviews.text: If you are curious about the city this is probably first thing that will make you curious. There is Golden Gate bridge which is nowhere near this park. From mid San Francisco to the west Ocean Beach, this park has multiple attraction within it. When I visited there was a fancy International Witches Confluence with people wearing Harry Potter costumes and selling fancy things during Halloween. Walk in the Park is awesome. Just be aware of the unleashed dogs.

reviews.title: Beautiful area
reviews.text: Large park area out of the town before you come to the Golden Gate Bridge.  Beautifully kept gardens and parks.  You would need a whole day here to wander about and visit the various buildings and gardens.  Lovely place to relax.  If you have plenty time and want to escape the city this is the place to go to in San Franciso away from the crowds.

reviews.title: Beautiful and relaxing. Great botanical gardens
reviews.text: So nice to be in such beauty yet also be in such an exciting city. Great for a picnic. They have some grills for meat roasting

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.text: Its a very impressive park and its a decent size. Was a good park to walk around. Lot to see. I recommend to go check out the japanesse tea garden, which costs but is worth the money.

reviews.title: Japanese tea garden!!!
reviews.text: My wife and I went to the Japanese tea gardens and wow was it amazing! She loved it so much! We bought some tea to go and drank some there and loved it.

reviews.title: Segway though the park
reviews.text: We chose to do a segway tour through the park which was an amazing way to see it. However, we took a bit more time after to go to the Japanese tea garden which was so beautiful and relaxing.

reviews.title: Great place to spend a day.
reviews.text: Lots of cool things in Golden Gate Park including de Young museum, California Academy of Sciences, Japanese tea garden, conservatory and botanical gardens (also the buffalos and windmills). Parking all around the various streets. Can be busy but you can probably find something if you keep looking. Street parking limited to 4 hours. There are also a garages under the museums. Most things cost extra except for the buffalo, wind mills or beach access on the most western end. Botanical garden is also free to walk around. The extra costs are worth it. Conservatory at $9 is nice. The Japanese tea garden at $6 is worth it too ( best in spring and summer). CAS is $39. Not sure about de Young but a city pass can really bring down prices overall. Make time for a day in Golden Gate Park and all it offers. You will enjoy it.

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: Visited recently. A lovely oasis, with some intrusive road noise. Good for mobility pared visitors although some uphill grades for wheelchairs etc.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: I didn't realize how big the park actually is!  There is so much to see I definitely have to go back to spend more time.

reviews.title: Beautiful park...always something to see!
reviews.text: We love going here....always something to see.  A  great oasis in the middle of the city....and there is so much around the park in the neighborhoods, too.

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: Golden gate park is truely amazing. You could spend days on end checking it out The scenery around the park is spectacular

reviews.title: what a wonderful park!
reviews.text: It is a park so beautiful, pleasant and friendly, with expanses and green lawns. Great signs that helps you get around. A cute playground, lovely corners, flowers, birds and healers. Who needs more?

reviews.title: Beautiful park
reviews.text: This park is huge - you could spend a full day here if you wanted to, especially if you did a museum or one of the paid gardens in the park, and took a picnic, etc. We just spent a couple of hours here walking off our hangovers - it took an hour from walk to one end and then the same back again but the park is beautiful and well kept. Would recommend to anyone visiting San Francisco who wants to get out of the busy city for a while.

reviews.title: Must stop in San Francisco
reviews.text: The de Young museum and Calif. Academy of Science are centerpiece visits along with the beautiful Japanese Tea garden.

reviews.title: Beautiful park with lots to do
reviews.text: We spent the day biking, walking and scooter-ing through the park.  The botanical gardens are really nice, as are the outside of the Japanese Tea Garden.  We unfortunately were running out of time so we didn't go in.  The brewery just outside of the park on the west side is very nice too.

reviews.title: Great tour
reviews.text: Great tour on Segways with friends especially on a warm sunny day..You can enjoy great sceneries!Recommended!

reviews.title: Huge park, loads to do.
reviews.text: There’s quite a few entrances so it depends what your looking for, a university, coffee, ice-cream, flower display, art museum and much more.

reviews.title: One of the largest human-made parks in USA
reviews.text: Absolutely amazing must see park if you visit San Francisco! Very green, safe, friendly place with lots of lakes, golf course, soccer fields, restaurant on the very west side with great local wines and beer selection, overlooking the ocean from the West and GG park from the East.

reviews.title: Huge Park
reviews.text: So much to take in and see. We enjoyed riding through the park on bikes and seeing the different people/groups and activities that were going on

reviews.title: Green Oasis in the City of San Francisco
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is a beautiful and very relaxing place. There are numerous places to sit and enjoy nature. I used to go to a dentist who had an office near the park. After a visit to the dentist's office, I'd visit the park and spend a few hours taking pictures and relaxing among the green trees. I have to say, because of the visit to the Golden Gate Park I actually looked forward to my next dental appointment. :)If you are a tourist, call an Uber - they will pick you from your hotel and will take you to the park. If you have plenty of time and like public transit and people watching, you may take trolley #5, which connects downtown San Francisco with Ocean Beach. It is a slow ride, but I rather enjoy it.

reviews.title: Rural paradise in busy city
reviews.text: Minute away from crowds and bustle you will find a quiet spot to walk, smell flowers, sit and enjoy nature or visit an outstanding museum.

reviews.title: Large and beautiful place.
reviews.text: Another easy bus ride from downtown. Expansive and varied park with huge trees, grassed and bushy areas and flower gardens, walking tracks, bike paths. The park has it all including a conservatorium. A credit to the city of San Francisco.

reviews.title: nature
reviews.text: this is the only beautiful thing I have senn in SF. Beause of it's trees and botanical garden. the only place I Could breath there

reviews.title: Beautiful place to take a walk and visit Museums
reviews.text: he Young Museum the Young Museum, the California Academy of sciences, and if you want to see something authentic go to Hippie Hill on the northern part of the park.

reviews.title: Glorious day in Golden Gate Park on a Segway
reviews.text: An excellent and fun way to explore Golden Gate Park. The initial training to get our bearings on the Segway was comprehensive and quick. We covered a good portion of the park’s geography - a little off roading too! And to top it off our guide, Rosie, was outstanding! She shared interesting facts and anecdotes with a bit of comedy while making sure everyone in the group was attended. I definitely recommend this experience for visitors as well as residents.

reviews.title: Smell the earth and breathe real fresh air !!
reviews.text: Golden Gate park was one of the highlights of my visit to San Francisco. It is a HUGE park. Even though I visited on a Sunday when a lot of people were out in the park, there were still a number of paths that were quiet and calm. Especially early in the morning, one can smell the earth and get some real fresh air...makes you feel happy about everything in life! If you have time to spare, taking some long walks for 2-3 hours is worth it

reviews.title: A must when visiting San Francisco
reviews.text: Other than just the Golden Gate Bridge and Fisherman's Wharf, visitors will appreciate all the beauty that this park has to offer. From the park itself, to the beautiful Japanese Tea Garden, De Young Museum, Academy of Arts and Sciences, the flower garden and so many other themed parts of this vast park, everyone will surely enjoy this place.

reviews.title: GREAT PARK
reviews.text: Great place to visit. The park is huge, has several attractions inside for doing sports, cultural places to see, or just walking.The park goes from the coast several km into the city. I reccomend it!!!

reviews.title: So much to See, Touch and Smell
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is representative of the diversity, beauty and intellect of the residents of San Francisco.  Save a full day or two to experience the many facets of this gem.  In addition to the run of the mill playgrounds, there are ponds, lakes with canoes, waterfalls, specialty gardens, i.e. Conservatory of Flowers, The Arboreturm, Rhododendron Dell, japanese Tea and Rose Gardens. The museums can steal an entire afternoon.  Many afternoons there are free concerts in front of the museums.  The park continues right down to ocean beach where there are windmills and  dining options.  The park is best experienced on foot, bicycle or skates.  Traffic can be fierce, especially on Saturdays.

reviews.title: Family Friendly Activity
reviews.text: After brunch at the Serpentine Restaurant we stopped by Golden Gate Park to visit the Flower Conservatory and walk the park. The Flower Conservatory was outstanding. This is a small place that will take less than 45 minutes to enjoy. The park itself is a treasure of San Fransisco. It offers all the walking, running, or relaxing you are inclined for the day. We saw individuals and families playing volleyball, tennis, frisbee, biking, and assorted yard games. If you are looking for a place to unwind from the week this is the spot for you.

reviews.title: Gorgeous park
reviews.text: You could spend hours in here! Amazing waterfalls, flowers, museums, lakes, trees and more! Go get lost in it!

reviews.title: Serenity in the City
reviews.text: Walk from one end of the Park to the other and its around 3 miles. Very flat so an easy walk but beautiful views and plenty of things going on especially on a Sunday when it is closed to traffic so probably the best time to do it.

reviews.title: Beautiful park!
reviews.text: If you love nature, and need a break from the busy city, DEF stop by this park. Plenty of quiet spots to relax, enjoy a hike through the park, or stop by the gardens. One of my favorite stops in SF.

reviews.title: Beautiful birds
reviews.text: The east end of the park can be overcrowded, but from about Stow Lake west is spectacular. Climb to the top of Strawberry Hill for amazing views.
