reviews.title: Come for the buffalo, stay for the raccoons*
reviews.text: *yes, Americans, we're aware that raccoons are pests, but they are so freaking cute.We spent a day in the park and had a great time. We were pretty excited about seeing the buffalo, but they were pretty far away and we didn't get great views. On the other hand, the raccoons and squirrels offered plenty of entertainment. Lots of nice birds too.We started at Beach Chalet Brewing at the far west of the park, which was nice enough, but nothing special. We then walked to the east end, taking us a good few hours, including stops. Be prepared for sore legs, but if you like nature, there's a fair bit to explore here. Tip: if you're ending at the east end, it's worth the extra 15-minute walk to Magnolia Brewery for a well-earned beer.

reviews.title: Beautiful huge park.  Favorite was the tea garden
reviews.text: We visited the park and toured through the Japanese tea garden and the botanical gardens.  Both are quite pricey.  If you had to choose the tea garden was our favorite, although the entrance staff at the botanical gardens hands down was more polite.

reviews.title: Beautiful, Authentic Japanese Tea Garden
reviews.text: I lived in Japan for 3 years and so was excited to hear about the Tea Garden in Golden Gate Park.From the moment you arrive at the main gate it feels like you are in Japan.  There is an entrance fee but it is absolutely worth paying.  It is clear that your fee is well-spent: the quality of the planting, traditional tree-pruning, and authentic buildings and details are exceptional: they must take extensive and continuous maintenance.The tea and traditional sweets served in the garden are served just as they would be in Japan.  In October when we visited there were some gorgeous leaf colours on acers and ginkgo trees.  The trees and shrubs are so varied that there would interest all year round.  I would recommend this to everyone.

reviews.title: Huge
reviews.text: This is a really huge city park and will take a few days if one really want to cover the entire place.  It definitely serves as a green and relaxing place to go to.

reviews.title: A must visit for tourists!
reviews.text: A great park that has so many different things to offer like museums, different gardens, awesome picnic opportunities, Ocean Beach etc. We walked the full length one way and took the free shuttle back that runs every Saturday, Sunday and on holidays. A good option is to rent a bike to go around the park. We had a fantastic day in the park and I’ll make sure to go again the next time around.

reviews.title: Huge park with much of it a bit rough
reviews.text: Only a small part of this park is kept nice and manicured. Much of it is a bit wild, unkept and home for the homeless. We loved the Japanese tea gardens which is free before 10am on certain days of the week. The botanical gardens are not free, so we didn't go in. Most cities have botanical gardens free for visitors, so this was disappointing. Also have to pay for the Flower Conservatory. So basically nothing that's worth looking at is free in this park. Oh the viewing tower within the De Young museum is free and definitely worth going up to, great views. You don't need a ticket for the museum to enter the tower viewing area.

reviews.title: A great park in the middle of a large city
reviews.text: This park is huge and has something for everyone.  The best way of exploring it is on foot and you would need at least half a day to walk around and check it out.  I saw my first Bison here in the Bison enclosure, even though they were not very active at least it is a chance to see them.

reviews.title: Fabulous botanical gardens
reviews.text: This park is so big it would take a few days to explore. We only had one day and we walked around the gorgeous gardens plus we also visited the Japanese Tea Gardens which were breath taking.

reviews.title: More to experience than Central Park
reviews.text: Well away from the tourist crowds, the city dwellers come to the park. Bisson, windmills, restaurants (the Beach Chalet which over looks the ocean is my favorite). Gardens of all kinds, botanical, the ever romantic tea in the Japanese Garden, the lakes. Then the attractions, the De Young with some of the best art shows in the world, the Academy of Science ( a play land for kids and adults) and the Arboretum (a unique time travel experience back to the World's Fair). Spend some time on their website and find what is right for you to see. There is way too much to do in a day. Find something hidden too. Sure, some points of interest are just points in your trip, but they are all memorable and sometimes even private glimpses of the city few people see.

reviews.title: Massive Park!
reviews.text: Be prepared to walk! this park is massive. It holds to be very well know Museums that are worth visiting. Surely one could spend the whole day in this park.

reviews.title: Excellent visit
reviews.text: Went up to the observatory tower, which was free. This is a beautiful, clean, park and I highly recommend visiting.

reviews.title: Lots for everyone
reviews.text: We hired a stretch limousine and our marvellous driver took us through this wonderful venue. People enjoying the basics of the place, but so many other attractions, games and pleasures on the land and lakes. The park is massive and a delight to visit,

reviews.title: Give yourself more time
reviews.text: Coming from PA we thought it would be a walkable Park. It is not but shuttle busses provide slow but usable way to get around.De Young a must see.We were there one a dreary day so enjoying the out of doors and beautiful gardens was not successful BUT on. Great day take a picnic and enjoy.Not many choices for any type of food other than a hidden hot dog, so come prepared

reviews.title: Vantigo tour
reviews.text: Great way to see the park and learn the history too. The city park board has done a fabulous job of keeping it a treasure for everyone.

reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.text: We walked through the park and around the lake. We walked to the park from Hays, it took about an hour from there. There’s not a great deal to do there but we walked around the lake, a nice place to go if you are looking for something free/cheap to do.

reviews.title: A spectacular park.
reviews.text: Huge in size and varied in type of attraction, this is a stunning park to wander round. I wish I’d had a bit longer to see everything but from what I did see, I highly recommend the Japanese Tea Gardens, which are stunning and genuinely comparable to anything I saw in Tokyo, Kyoto or Nara.

reviews.title: Huge place!
reviews.text: This place is HUGE! If you do not know exactly where do you want to go then you’re going to end up walking till your feet hurt. Good scenery, well preserved!

reviews.title: A Huge Park
reviews.text: This park is bigger than Central Park in New York. We walked through the Park to get to the California Academy of Science and decided to see various parts of the Park while we were here.

reviews.title: Beautiful Park
reviews.text: Such a huge park filled with life and well maintained gardens. We visited the Conservatory and loved it.

reviews.title: Gotta visit when in SF!
reviews.text: Beautiful park! Must visit the pond and if have time rent a paddle boat and the Japanese Tea Garden is absolutely beautiful.  There is a fee.    Expect at least two hours here.  A true gem in the city.

reviews.title: Great way to spend a day.
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is so large and there is so much to do it is like a city in itself. It is over 50 blocks long and contains everything. There are tennis courts, riding stables, a zoo, a restaurant, a museum, a band shell and more. You can spend all day in here but will need a car. Great for the whole family.

reviews.title: Beautiful flowers and green space
reviews.text: We visited the Conservatory of Flowers on a glorious fall day and there were so many flowers in bloom! The park itself is huge with lots of sweeping lawns. Parking was pretty full when we went so it probably would've been easier to take public transport. We went to see the Bison and were lucky to get a glimpse of one in the paddock. It was a wonderful place to spend time and take a break from the busy city.

reviews.title: Pretty park
reviews.text: This park is great for Sunday stroll for couples, friends and families. At the park are many things to do such as see botanical garden or have a picnic and enjoy the weather and do some people watching. If you are looking for a place where to jog in SF you should go to Golden Gate Park!

reviews.title: Huge Area worth a visit
reviews.text: We had spent all day on cycles by the time we reached Golden Gate park so we didn't manage to see it all. The Japanese tea garden is cute but it was a bit annoying having to pay.

reviews.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass Festival - fabulous!
reviews.text: Great music, amazing venues and really well organized!  The Hardly Strictly Bluegrass Festival brings amazing talent to the park for an enjoyable day of listening to music from well known grammy artists to new bands with original songs.  There's such talented guitar, fiddle, mandolin, and so much more artists that perform over the weekend.  What a treasure!

reviews.title: Proposal Spot
reviews.text: I Had my husband propose to me at the Japanese Tea Garden! would highly recommend going here. There is so much to do, I feel like you would need a few days to make the most of everything in the park.

reviews.title: A Must See
reviews.text: If you visit San Francisco then you really must come here. A really stunning park & much bigger than you imagine. Great museums & a brilliant trolley bus that does a great tour.

reviews.title: Beautiful Park providing a lung for the city.
reviews.text: The park is a large slice of greenery about 1.5 square miles containing gardens, lakes , model boats , a Japanese Pavilion and a number of music venues. Great for walking , cycling , sitting and relaxing, the park provides everything you would want from a park. Oh and of course a herd of Bison. A great spot.

reviews.title: An idyllic escape from the CBD
reviews.text: So much to see and do; beautiful parks and gardens, some like to be active by walking or cycling around, others just like to escape the hustle and bustle of the city which is an easy 15 minute drive.

reviews.title: Leave more time
reviews.text: Went to Golden Gate Park and in what we saw found a great place to relax from the hustle and bussel bustle of travelling. We did not allow enough time to appricare the whole area.Plenty of room for the kids to run aroun.Did enter from Haight street which had lots of shops and eateries worth visiting

reviews.title: Great by bike
reviews.text: We drove here and easy free parking on the inner roads. We hired bikes for an hour and did the whole circuit including Ocean beach. Very easy cycling and little traffic. Didn't have time for the Science Museum although this looked good also.

reviews.title: something for everyone
reviews.text: easy to reach by public transit, use google maps. I lived next to the park for several years. I am pleased to see it's just a beautiful as ever and so many people enjoy it. Prepare for your visit and plan to return more than once.

reviews.title: It was really good in some parts and really dingy in some parts.
reviews.text: What I liked: The design of the park and how its neatly placed in between the city in a long strip so lots of localities have access to it. I liked the museums and other areas to gather in between. They were neatly manicured gardens and it was all quite nice. Hiked up a small butterfly hill but alas we didn't see any butterflies. The view was nice though from top. The view point from the De young museum was good too. It doesn't cost anything to see the view from top.What I didn't like: The lakes/ponds were quite stagnant and there were so many flies and mosquitoes. That's something I didn't expect. Some smaller ponds were covered with moss too. There was one big pond which had floating ducks and that was neat and had lots of visitors.

reviews.title: Must See in SF
reviews.text: I would tell my friends this Park is a must-see in San Francisco (SF).There are fields for all kinds of sports, varying from tennis, soccer to cycling. There are beautiful gardens for flowers and plants. There are landmarks like the windmills and several lakes. There are de Young Museum and Science Museum too.On my walk across the park, I happened to see the marine school symphony bands competing. Watched the competition a bit and it was quite fun as well.

reviews.title: A real surprise!
reviews.text: Not really sure what to expect but a real variety of experiences.Great to see lots of people out and about in lovely surroundings and really enjoying themselvesHighlight has to be the driver of the 'freebie bus' who was both informative, stopped virtually anywhere and was hugely entertaining.

reviews.title: Spectacular
reviews.text: We had the good fortune to be there when The Blue Grass Festival was going on.  The park was very clean and when there is no concerts there is always some activities.  The city should be very proud!

reviews.title: Japanese Tea Garden
reviews.text: We got the bus to Haight Ashbury and then walked to the park.  It is huge!  There is so much to do and look at.  We spent a long time in the Japanese Tea Garden.  it is stunning.  We also set off to see the bison - still didn't make it.  Should have got a bus there.  Whether you just want to wander or go into the museums and exhibits it is definitely worth a visit

reviews.title: Awesome - a park for the people and the peoples park.
reviews.text: Awesome day spent in this park, there was a live afternoon/evening at the Opera on the Sunday we were there, thousands of people were there that day, listening to the glorious arias and the Orchestra playing Mascagni from Verdi's opera.  Brought tears to my eyes hearing a New Zealand Opera Tenor perform that day - the music itself just left you feeling incredibly moved and uplifted.  A true joy.

reviews.title: Beautiful, needed more time!
reviews.text: We got off a the Science museum...walked across the outdoor concert area..to the Zen Garden...very beautiful. Very similar to the real thing in China. Drove by Botanical garden...looked gorgeous!

reviews.title: Japanese Tea Gardens
reviews.text: Our time in Golden Gate Park was mainly spent in the Japanese Tea Garden’s. It is so breathe-taking. The park is massive, so much to do

reviews.title: Japanese Gardens
reviews.text: The park has extensive areas to see and you can spend the day and only see a small part of it. I decided to go see the Japanese Gardens as they are usually a good option, it is very pretty as I imagined it would be. The bridges, the manicured areas, the ponds and fish and so on. I enjoyed spending the time and taking lots of pictures.

reviews.title: Beautiful and big
reviews.text: We recently went on a hop on hop off bus tour which stopped at the park we had a lovely walk through a small part of the park and learnt so much about how it became the park which was really interesting We were lucky we had a lovely day and had such a great view there is a good view of the bridge in partsIt’s to big to walk right through when you’re in a hurry but it’s worth a walk even for a short timeIt would be nice to have places to stop and have a drink but if they are there we didn’t spot it although we didn’t spend to much time there

reviews.title: Nice park
reviews.text: We had a nice stroll but weren’t blown away. Ok if you’re willing to pay admission to the museums. Can be hard to get away after closing hours.

reviews.title: Bad experience
reviews.text: The park is not maintained and i even stepped on some poop of some pet. Otherwise the park was pleasant and good .

reviews.title: Great place to visit while in San Francisco
reviews.text: Located at one end of the city. Lovely place to walk amongst trees, birds and lakes. Have something for all like the California Academy of Sciences , Japanese tea garden, de Young museum....

reviews.title: Keep your expectations low
reviews.text: This park is not very well maintained on the outer edges. It looks like Jurassic Park. It is not very inviting. I had no desire to go explore it.

reviews.title: Beautiful - so much to explore!
reviews.text: We only had time to go around the Japanese Tea Garden which was amazing, then there was also a free concert happening just opposite so you can grab a tea or coffee and listen under the dappled shade

reviews.title: Beautiful park!
reviews.text: What a natural beauty park.  We actually spent most of the day there and we had no intention of doing that.  Beautiful, serene.  Very relaxing.

reviews.title: Go on a weekend
reviews.text: This is a BIG park; situated in the middle of the city stretching all the way to the Pacific coast it is around 3 Square Miles of grass and woodland with some great gardens, museums and loads of roads for cycling and jogging. Just beware that these sae roads are open to normal traffic Monday - Friday so mid week it is a bit less relaxing

reviews.title: Very large beautiful park in the heart of the city
reviews.text: There is so much to do in this large park that you can't do it all in one day.  I wish we had more time when there.  The little lake, the flower and plant building, the AIDS memorial garden, the windmills,....just too much in one day.  Driving though it at night, I would definitely not recommend walking or biking through it after dark.  It is very large and very dark.

reviews.title: Beautiful Green Spot
reviews.text: It's really a beautiful park where you can enjoy the nature in a big city. Very well maintained. So many activities to do.

reviews.title: Great Vistas
reviews.text: Park near the water and view the Golden Gate and Bay bridges.  Good running and walking and picnicking.  Pick up food from one of the many sandwich shops located on the perimeter .

reviews.title: Fantastic green spave
reviews.text: Like many things in America, this park is on a grand scale.  Arrived here after a morning’s walk.  The park is absolutely massive so if you want to do the whole thing, you’d need a full day.  We took a general stroll, saw the AIDS memorial area but spent most of our time In the Botanical Gardens, which are lovely, although at a cost ($9).  The guy at the access kiosk was great; pointing us to areas currently worth a visit.The park is big enough to have a number of roads running through it; some used by bus service, which was pretty handy for us!

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text: This is a very large park we could have spent more time in. We only found about a quarter of this park at best. The bison were on the move, lovely quiet walks. Plenty of options for different transport.

reviews.title: Really nice park in the centre of a busy city
reviews.text: We spent a whole day in the park which is several miles long.  There are various museums etc within the park so we visited the de Young Museum, the Japanese garden and the Glasshouse.  The only disappointment were the bison who seemed to be asleep!

reviews.title: Wow what a surprise
reviews.text: I had no idea how large this park is! Offers a lot - beautiful grounds, places to ride bicycles, museums, and more

reviews.title: So much to do and see
reviews.text: This place is so much more than a beautiful park!  There is the Academy of Sciences, Aquarium, De Young Museum, Japanese Tea Garden, Botanical Garden, to name a few things to do.  You could easily spend more than one day here.  Don't miss this!

reviews.title: Beautiful place
reviews.text: A wonderful place to visit. A great place to spend the day. The Conservatory of Flowers is amazing. Gray Line Hop on hop off is a good way to see the park.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: There's something significant about a park full of greenery in the middle of a city anyway, but Golden Gate Park is just stunning!We hired bikes to go to the bridge and went via the park.There are plenty of open spaces for picnics, flat open cycle routes and of course lots of monuments, buildings, conservatories and flowers and plants to see on your way around. Well worth a few hours of your stay in San Francisco, especially if you have a bike (not sure how realistic it would be to see much on foot).

reviews.title: Nature Tour
reviews.text: Again we got there early so we moved around easily because there were no lines.  Food was great.... loved the ice cream.  Water fountain easily located to refill our water bottles.  And was so greatful for the available seating.

reviews.title: West Coast bus trip
reviews.text: Wow! Great afternoon visiting Golden Gate Park! The Japanese tea garden is beautiful and the statuary is spectacular! The concert venue is also very cool.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: You could spend a day here. We got a bus to the west entrance and saw the main museum buildings, Japanese tea garden, flower conservatory. Did not go inside anywhere actually ( Kew Gardens is on our doorstep) but probably should have paid to visit tea garden. Beautiful weather- loved this place. Then got a bus no 7 back to downtown .

reviews.title: People, People
reviews.text: Great place to relax and enjoy the people. This was my introduction to "Bubble Soccer" in the park and it was very interesting. They seem to enjoy bumping into each other more than scoring. FUN!

reviews.title: Quiet Walk in the sunshine
reviews.text: On our last full day in the city, we took the electric bus out to this beautiful park. Bigger than Central Park in New York, it was peaceful especially in the botanic gardens, even though there are cross-roads across the main park.

reviews.title: Not worth
reviews.text: Park is not great at all & hefty charges are there for visit,very small & less attractive park,its Japanese tea garden

reviews.title: Great on a sunny day
reviews.text: Was nice to walk around here in the sun. Most things charged 9 dollars to get in but the De Young museum had a viewing tower that gave great views of the city - which could be accessed for free!

reviews.title: Opera In The Park
reviews.text: One of my favorite events of the year in San Francisco is the free Opera In The Park concert held every year on the first Sunday of September right after opening night of the regular opera series at the formal Opera House.   Beautiful outdoor setting in Golden Gate Park and wonderful orchestra and singing.  Folks often show up hours ahead to set up picnic extravaganzas for their friends. Even arriving right before the 1:30 performance is OK if you are willing to stand or sit between others folk's blankets.  The mood is relaxed and festive.  The music is glorious.  Do check it ou!!!

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park
reviews.text: A panopoly of sights and activities. You can see windmills, bison, muscovy ducks, Canadian geese, a carousel, the DeYoung Art Museum, California Acadeny of Sciences, giant redwoods, a rose garden, a botanical garden, a Japanese tea garden and can walk or hike miles, golf a short 9 hole course, shoot with bow and arrows, ride a surrey, paddle a boat on Stowe Lake, lawn bowl, play tennis, play a long frisbee course, or just picnic and if you’re  lucky you might be around for one of many special events held yearly, weekly or spontaneously. Have fun!

reviews.title: Many different areas to enjoy
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park includes the De Young Museum, excellent for art, and the California Academy of Sciences, featuring live alligators, a rainforest, and a Planetarium.  Next to the De Young is the Japanese Garden and Tea House, a favorite of my children when young as they walked over stones in a stream and up and over an arched bridge.  They liked the tea and cookies, too.  All of the above charge for admission. Walk a little further away from the TeaHouse and you come to the Arboretum, a lovely place in all seasons, with plants from many different countries, especially those from Mediteranean climates, view points, and paths for the children to explore.  A small fee here.  Further west and for free are the Polo Fields and near the ocean, the Windmills and Tulip gardens.  Many picnic spots and meadows.  At the East End of the Park is the Conservatory of Flowers with tropical plants, again a small fee. You can rent bikes on Stanyan Street and main roads of the park are closed on to auto traffic on weekends.

reviews.title: Crissy Beach
reviews.text: Worth a visit.  You can get lovely photos of The Golden Gate Bridge from here.  A pleasant day out.  We took the Street Car here from our hotel.

reviews.title: Sooo beautiful!
reviews.text: Omg this place amazed me! It is so big so green, so beautiful! It’s a great place to take a walk, to seat quiet, to take beautiful pictures or to get together with friends or family. Japanese tea garden is lovely! It is free 3 days a week before 10 a.m. There’s so much to enjoy! I would recommend to come in a vehicle, the place is really big to walk it all the way. But is you have plenty of time you may enjoy it walking.

reviews.title: Beautiful park
reviews.text: The park was beautiful. We stopped and had tea at the Japanese Gardens. It was very peaceful and serene.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: This was on our list of must sees while in San Francisco, and it did not disappoint. Before heading there I looked up options to see as much as possible without knowing the area. We chose a Segway tour and saw so much more than we could have dreamed. This would be my go to place if I lived in the area. Beautiful and serene plus we learned so much about it's history during our tour.

reviews.title: Great park
reviews.text: Very cool to rest inside one busy  city like San Francisco. We can enjoy the museum, comcernt or biking,...lot of activities here

reviews.title: Lots to do
reviews.text: Spent a few hours walking around the park and there was lots to do and see. Really enjoyed seeing the bison as I havent seen them before and also visited the wooden model boat club and chatting to some of the owners about the club and seeing the boats on the lake. It was also enjoyable to walk around and enjoy the plants and trees. Its a large park and didnt have time to see it all as our time was limited.

reviews.title: Huge park
reviews.text: We only had the briefest of visits - this park is so big it warrants more time - so astonished to discover WILD BISON - in a city park!

reviews.title: Very Pretty
reviews.text: Our tour guide took us through some pretty places, this would have to be one of my favorites after seeing" The Golden Gate Bridge," great photo spot, beautiful gardens and across the road you can see some beautiful San Fran homes.

reviews.title: So Much To See
reviews.text: We could have spent  half a day here, however with so much to see in San Fran we only stayed for about an hour. The park is a huge oasis in the city an the only knock is the amount of homelessness.

reviews.title: Rent a bike and go enjoy
reviews.text: Amazing place with amazing view, open spaces lots of happy people exercising and ..dogs lots of well-behaved dogs.You might want to continue to Golden Gate Bridge which you can cross by foot or bike

reviews.title: Lovely Park to wonder through
reviews.text: Lovely park which we wondered through, there are nice fountains in the park and also whilst we were there the Golden Gate Band were playing songs from famous Disney films which was great to hear and see everyone just relax and chill.Japenese Gardens are beautiful, well worth a visiting.

reviews.title: Park
reviews.text: We did the open top bus all around and it was lovely riding through the Holden gate park. The weather was brilliant today than it has been in the pass 4 days we’ve been here. Manage to get a tan lol.

reviews.title: Lovely park
reviews.text: Quite large for an urban park with lots of curving street and paths. A good size conservatory and plenty of gardens. The parking is a bit tricky with a bike path between the sidewalk and parking lane and the driving lanes aren’t that wide either. It’s well used so be very careful opening car doors.

reviews.title: Spend the Day
reviews.text: We were dropped off at the Japanese Garden, beautiful but some of the iconic buildings were very deferred, very disappointing.  The grounds are beautiful and worth the price of admission.  Then we walked to the Botanical Gardens, again beautiful and worth the price.  Again we walked, this time to the Conservatory of Flowers and sat outside enjoying the view.  You can spend a couple of hours or all day.  There is so much to see and do.

reviews.title: Too Much to See and Do
reviews.text: This huge park holds many attractions as well as having a bountiful supply of varied natural environments. Catch a glimpse of T-Rex at the museum or drink tea in the Japanese Tea Garden. Look out for the many hidden statues. The garden's designer didn't want statues in the park so whenever the local authorities put one in, he surrounded it with shrubs. They even put one of him in the park. He 'borrowed it' and buried it in his back yard.

reviews.title: The most beautiful garden
reviews.text: I never saw flowers so beautiful before, just seat in the lawn and admire the surroundings. This park is big and beautiful.

reviews.title: Baseball
reviews.text: We stayed in San Fran for 4 nights we took an afternoon out to visit the park it was a Sunday and we came across a baseball game , we stayed and watched a game played by local people, the sun was beaming down it was a great afternoon plenty to do here with the the gardens etc or just for a leisurely stroll

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Lots of greenery, now at immediately at the base of the bridge (which confused me). Great to walk around or drive by.

reviews.title: We saw the Bison/Buffalo
reviews.text: We went to see the bison/buffalo which was a nice 20 minute stop for the kids.  It wasn't too exciting for me but thats what they wanted to see so we did it! I wouldn't recommend going to see them unless you are already in the area - not worth traffic.

reviews.title: A large and delightful park
reviews.text: Biking through this park was a great time and it offered many sights along the way. On the West side of the park is Ocean beach so that was a great finish to the bike ride.

reviews.title: GOLDEN gate park rocks!
reviews.text: You will need more than one day to see Golden State Park -I suggest taking a look at the park and deciding what interest you and start from there -I ran out of time during my trip to San Francisco - but the few hidden gems I saw - tempt me to return -Hope this helps my fellow travelers -

reviews.title: So much to enjoy - it could take days
reviews.text: There are beautiful bison, gardens, interesting trails, pedal boats, museums etc.... A wonderful area to enjoy when in SF.

reviews.title: NOT SO GREAT
reviews.text: We were in San Francisco and made a mistake to include it in our To-do-list. The main reason is the park area is huge and not possible to cover in few hours by foot. There are many small gardens inside it and to me it didn’t appealed much.We came here after seeing the Alamo square by Bus 5R. After going it, we found a conservatory which was appealing at least from outside. But we couldn’t go inside as the entry fee was $11- too much compared to gardens in my own country. Also we targeted Japanese Tea Garden but again it was $11 for a tiny area! We kept ourselves to free items like Lily Pond, Rose Garden etc. after when we realised that probably spending time at Fisherman’s Wharf would be a great idea rather then spending energy here.

reviews.title: Plan to make enough time to see and do here!
reviews.text: We walked around the park since we had a little extra time. There was so much to do and see there that you really want to set a whole day for this place! Simply beautiful!

reviews.title: Need two weeks to see the whole thing
reviews.text: I took my wife and granddaughter there for the day and we only had time to see the Japanese Garden, Botanical Garden and Science Museum...and we rushed through that. So much to see do and experience!!!

reviews.title: ESCAPE INTO THIS PARK AND EXPLORE ITS MANY POCKETS
reviews.text: [Warning: Young adults from Central Florida in for vacation] As someone who prefers the calm of nature, this was a great escape from the bustle of the city. There were many places to hide away from crowds even though there’s many attractions scattered throughout this park to attract them. We actually rented a bike and traveled as much as we could from east to west. There were many sidewalks to share with walkers, but most of the time we cycled on the road and felt relatively safe due to the slow speed limits.SOME THINGS WE SAWHalf the areas inside the park require an admission price such as the Science Museum and Japanese Tea Garden while others were easy to just enter and view such as the bison enclosure, the Dutch windmill, many playing fields and playgrounds. RESOURCES FOR A VISITORThere’s a few areas to grab a snack or drink, but not open as late as some attractions. With many trails and relatively calm roads, you’ll run into many joggers and cyclists. We were also content at the pretty good bathrooms, plus it seems the homeless, mentally ill squatters of the city haven’t really affected the park.

reviews.title: Beautiful Gardens
reviews.text: We went to the arboretum and the Japanese Tea Gardens.  It costs $9 for each individual activity, which is a little pricey but worth it.  We had tea at the Tea Garden with matcha.  This is a fun thing to do.  We enjoyed both immensely.

reviews.title: For a walk....
reviews.text: Nice park to go for a walk, to run, to sit on the grass and relax -- enjoying the view... With the urban jungle near by, this is one of the quiet places to be close to nature ;-)

reviews.title: Stunning gardens
reviews.text: The gardens of Golden Gate Bridge offer many unique things like a museum, Japanese garden and botanical garden These are stunning and very well maintained and the Japanese garden also offers team and snacks

reviews.title: Wonderful Afternoon Visit
reviews.text: Went to the deYoung museum, loved the outdoor sculpture park, loved the Japanese Tea Garden and the Museum of Natural Sciences.  Need to go back and spend a whole day'!

reviews.title: Relaxing escape
reviews.text: What an awesome escape in San Francisco, great to talk a walk and have some well earned relax and rest. Food available for purchase for lunch in the park!

reviews.title: Fun to Explore
reviews.text: We were here on a very cold day with wind and rain. As such, we just had to drive around and didn't get to get out and really experience the park. However, it was really fun to drive through and see the many things available to see and do. There were many picnic areas as well as interesting gardens and sculpture areas. If I'm in the area again, I will hope for better weather so we can explore more closely.

reviews.title: Beautiful park
reviews.text: We walked for hours and still saw only a small part of this beautiful park. We fell in love with the Chinese Tea Garden and spent two hours admiring all the beauty contained within.

reviews.title: Fun place for a picnic
reviews.text: Nice park with pretty views. Close to the bridge. Worth a visit. Fun place to walk, ride bikes and picnic

reviews.title: Free fun plus cheap transportation
reviews.text: San Francisco has been getting a lot of negative press lately because of the homeless population but they are no different than most cities.  I stay away from Powell Street, Union Square down to Market....better to use the Bay Ferry/Financial district area for connections....including great ferry rides.You can buy a 7 Day Muni pass as a visitor for about $50 and travel on all buses, cable cars and historic street cars... a 3-day pass is about $34.....remember a one way ticket on a cable car is $7 alone so buy the muni pass.Then you can go from the financial district all the way across town on the number one bus (Chinatown route) to the number 44 connecting to the huge Golden Gate Park.   Takes about 35 to 40 minutes....There you can hike for miles and see very nice people on a walking path around the hidden lake which includes a bridge built in 1893. If you go across the bridge and up the hill pathway to the top you'll actually see ruins of the exposition from that same time. Paddle boats looked like fun...and both the gardens are worth it....return the same way.....44 bus in front of Academy of Science....You can also travel on the California street  cable car...far fewer people....it goes only to Van Ness but you can stop directly at Trader Joes for the best food and wine bargains in town...on Van Ness you can take the number 30 to Fishermans wharf and Fort Mason....and back again or wait an hour in line for the cable car to Powell and California.....Most people stay in one of the three above hubs....and the buses I mentioned had plenty of nice visitors on board....the Fulton area bus is fine as well....but there are always exceptions....just get off if you are uncomfortable another bus will be along soon....Enjoy

reviews.title: Nice park
reviews.text: Big and lovely park. Go further to the beach. The bisons are cool, see the picture. Botanical and japanese garden is 9 dollars/adult in fee, if you not are SF citizen.

reviews.title: Trees trees and trees
reviews.text: If you're searching for serenity and peace in the city ! Its a definite visit. Go with a relaxed mind,a book if you love reading, some snacks and water. The park is huge with beautiful trees that eill mermerize you and make you relaxed.

reviews.title: AVERAGE PARK
reviews.text: Besides being a very huge park,The Golden Gate Park really has nothing unique to offer,except for having a lazy stroll around same

reviews.title: Beautiful park in the city!
reviews.text: This is San Fran’s version of Central Park. It is huge and definitely feels like a sanctuary from the hustle of the city. There are some pretty tall trees here and gorgeous flowers. Don’t miss the rose garden, Japanese tea garden, and theCA Academy of Sciences. I’m so glad we took the time to visit this park during our stay.

reviews.title: A must see day in the park!
reviews.text: From the beautiful Windmills , Buffalo grounds, Tennis Club, Concert, Arboritum and more this is huge. Bring a picnic and enjoy! They have so many events from 5k races to get concerts. I 've been here over a 100 times and love it. DON'T come at night as the homeless and shady character hang out. But in the day it's safe and nice.

reviews.title: What an amazing place!
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park covers a HUGE area and is very spread out.  I feel that the only way to do it justice and get your bearings is on a bus tour.  We did the Gray Line Hop on Hop off bus tour of San Fransisco which stops in the park and includes a smaller bus tour (Golden Gate Park Trolley).  We timed it just right and caught the Trolley (with guide) which took us from outside the Academy of Sciences and rode around the immediate vicinity passing the Japanese Tea Gardens, museums, waterfalls, bison paddock, lakes (stopping for quick photo opportunities), botanical gardens, and conservatory of flowers. It then further afield in G G Park to the Legion of Honour and Holocaust memorial (another stop), to Lands End, the beach along the Pacific coast, zoo and then back past the windmills.  It was a hop on hop off bus too but unless you wanted to visit the museum at the Legion of Honour or the zoo, I think the quick stops for photos and toilets were sufficient.  We enjoyed our tour very much and when we got off went to visit the botanical gardens ($8 each) which were amazing (see separate review).  We would have gone in the Japanese Tea Gardens too but at $8 each again we decided against it as we were short of time.We loved Golden Gate Park!

reviews.title: SO, SO MUCH to see and do
reviews.text: What a magnificent urban park!  Gorgeous trees and flowers, but the various facilities, museums, etc. are incredible.  So much we wanted to see but didn't have enough time.  Would have loved 3 days here.

reviews.title: Amazing place with plenty of parking
reviews.text: This place is sooo big. So hard to find parking in SF but not here. Gardens are amazing so many and too varied. the museum are awesome especially when you see the majority building where from an expo in early 1900's.

reviews.title: Fun and pretty
reviews.text: There were so many things to do in the park. We walked through the whole park. It took us quite a long time but it was worth it. :) So many cool places. The Dutch Mill is a must!

reviews.title: Nice, but pricey
reviews.text: I had looked forward to going to Golden Gate Park to see The Japanese Tea Garden, botanical gardens, carousel, museums, etc. I did not realize that each of them was going to cost money ($8+ per person for each). I was expecting it to be more like Central Park or Boston Common, where you could just walk around for free. But from the little I saw, it was sectioned off with fees. Now, there may have been areas that weren’t like this that I didn’t make it to. I only saw small area of Golden Gate Park.

reviews.title: Go on a Sunday or Take A SFCItyguide tour!
reviews.text: Where to begin...golden gate park is the Central Park of the West. (It’s actually larger than Central Park). I have taken several FREE tours here through the sfcityguides (google it) that offer free tours all over town. I have much more appreciation for the park and it’s rich history because of these tours. The botanical garden is nice if you want a break from th bustle. Currently $9/pp. You can see beautiful views of the city for FREE by taking the elevator up in the de Young Musuem waking right past the admissions desk. It’s totally kosher and allowed. You aren’t being sneaky or anything. Great 360 views. I love to come on Sunday when they have swing dancing in the park and roller bladers dancing in the park. They shut down the streets to cars for pedestrians and bicyclists and swing dancers and groovy roller bladers to enjoy every inch of this beautiful park. The Japanese tea garden is neat. I appreciated it more after my tour.

reviews.title: Not really a park
reviews.text: This is not really a park, its more a highway through a greenish area. If you want to have a nice walk through a park, go elsewhere.

reviews.title: Oasis in the city
reviews.text: This park is just wonderful - beautifully landscaped gardens, hiking and biking trails, as well as recreation areas. There's truly something for everyone and you'd be mad not to visit. You could lose yourself for hours here and forget that you were in the fabulously crazy buy crazily busy San Fran!The AIDS Memorial Garden is particularly beautiful and incredibly tranquil.

reviews.title: Great outdoor space and gardens
reviews.text: We toured the park on bicycles and stopped at multiple points. The arboretum and trees through out are great. Plenty of trails to explore.

reviews.title: Not worth the time to visit.
reviews.text: We visited the park on a 3 day trip to San Francisco and it was not worth the time.  I guess it is great for the locals but does not offer enough attractions for foreigners. The park is really hard to navigate through and any points of interest are far apart.

reviews.title: Mother Nature at her best!
reviews.text: This park is just absolutely stunning, gorgeous little gardens around every turn and a complete display of Mother Nature at her best.

reviews.title: Super Pretty
reviews.text: Super Pretty wish we had more time in it.The Japanese Garden was a definite highlight in the garden.

reviews.title: Beautiful Green Space!
reviews.text: We had the best time walking the Golden Gate Park. The grounds are beautiful and the Japanese Tea Garden is a must.

reviews.title: Fantastic Time!
reviews.text: Came for a few hours and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. There is so much to see here that you can hardly do it justice in one day. Very easy to get around with kids. Bathrooms were close by. Will definitely be back.

reviews.title: Pleasant but the science academy is a must
reviews.text: It was a nice visit. We did not have a lot of time there. Went into the museum to use the free viewing area at the top. Great views up there. Find the museums in America expensive so we did not go into that part.Kept our money for the Science Academy in Park which was great.

reviews.title: Amazing!!!
reviews.text: This place is incredible, it's sad to not have spent more time there. It is a place to spend the whole day or more than one day. There is also a museum that plays a DJ on Thursdays nights and is for adults only. Super cool!!! I love it..

reviews.title: Great Grand Park
reviews.text: A truly grand experience far better than NYC Central Park, though they both have different focus. Here you can get fantastic museums, leisurely experiences, and some fun. That said, GG Park does host large scale events and that will detract unless you're into the event. I also highly recommend that you don't dally past sundown when crime rears it's ugly head.

reviews.title: Great
reviews.text: This is such a fab park with so much to see and do in and around it! The history of the park is good too! I would recommend hiring a bike to go around x

reviews.title: Beautiful respite from the city
reviews.text: Lots to do and see with all the history and parks. Trails to hike, bison and old windmills to see, beautiful plants, often concerts or a random drum circle are going on. The lake is a nice place to rent a boat or get food and a beer, and ofcourse it leads to the ocean beach. Like it has its own little micro climate as well.

reviews.title: Central Park or San Francisco
reviews.text: I walked through a good amount of Golden Gate Park on my way to the beach and really enjoyed it. There was a lot of construction while I was there though, causing multiple bathrooms to be closed more noise and construction traffic which wasn’t much fun. The bison paddock was cool to see and I like the windmills at the west end. You can also access several museums from the park, which is cool. Allow a solid couple of hours to explore if you are walking. Also know you have to pay extra to get in the tea gardens or botanical garden.

reviews.title: Nice place to visit
reviews.text: This is huge and beautiful park. There is pretty much always something going on. We parked by the botanical garden and then walked from there. We felt very safe during the day and didn't run into a lot of homeless people. Look at a map beforehand and map out what you want to see. There were some cool museums and lots of statues to see. Watch out for bikers, they are sometimes going way too fast and not watching out for pedestrians at all.

reviews.title: Saturday at the park!
reviews.text: Beautiful! In particular the Japanese Tea Garden and Conservatory of Flowers.  Never saw the shuttle bus though.

reviews.title: Lush
reviews.text: Just a breath of fresh air in the city. Great picnic spit, unreal vibe, amd great heaven for runners and cyclists.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: What an amazing park.  We visited during a foggy misty morning.  It was gorgeous and goes on for blocks and blocks.  Didn't see too many homeless persons.  Many options to explore.  You could almost spend a whole day just at the park.

reviews.title: Stunning Views
reviews.text: We went to Golden Gate Park, not really knowing what to expect.  It is huge. There are two museums and Botanical Gardens. It was too much to see in one day. There is a free shuttle that you can take around the park. We didn't know about this until later, however and it is really too big to walk. Many people rent bikes, and this is a good option if you have older kids.

reviews.title: Don't miss this
reviews.text: Give yourself half a day to wander the park as there is plenty to do here aside from just relaxing.We chose a Segway tour which allowed us to cover a lot of ground too.

reviews.title: Great afternoon or day trop
reviews.text: Not near the eponymous bridge as its name might suggest, this giant park is packed with activities such as museums or just an opportunity for long walks and hikes. It resembles Central Park but hillier. Use a nearby bike share and don’t miss the Japanese garden (small entrance fee).

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Just had a short time to experience this lovely park, but will get back there sometime to spend the day !

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Unfortunately we were not able to find parking, but were able to drive around the park. There were so many visitors, children and tourist. It was a cold day and we enjoyed just driving around the park.

reviews.title: Not to be missed
reviews.text: Very beautiful park. Great to spend a whole day. Take your time at the Japanese Tea Garden and the Lake.

reviews.title: A key San Francisco destination
reviews.text: With its museums, gardens, activities, and serene spots for reflection, it’s easy to spend a full day or more in this 1,000-Plus acre park. Whether for a casual stroll or some serious cultural intake, this park is an ideal destination. Visit the DeYoung or Museum of Technology on a rainy day, or enjoy the outdoors in fine weather. There is no admission fee to the park itself, many of the attractions do have entry fees.

reviews.title: Great park to have a long walk...
reviews.text: ...and enjoy the green, the different parts of the parkt, the buildings, etc. If you have time, you can spend 1 day visiting the japan gardens, the museum, etc. Definitely one beautiful part of SF.

reviews.title: Top Notch
reviews.text: Bring your spouse. Bring your family. Bring your children. Bring your friends. This park has everything to make a cloudy day shine bright!

reviews.title: Lovely and beautiful huge park.
reviews.text: We visited this park on a Sunday for the free bandstand concert which was 2 hours long. It was a unique experience finding our way on foot in the park, as we took a city bus here. The park is very large, so we only saw a part of it. We had lunch at the De Young museum cafe, and this was extremely expensive, so I'd recommend bringing a picnic lunch if you can. We really enjoyed the concert by the Golden Gate band, which has been performing there for 136 years! It was very relaxing and enjoyable. They perform each Sunday in the summer months.

reviews.title: Delightful park - Free Sunday concert in the park
reviews.text: Every Sunday they have a band play in the park. When we were there they did music of Disney. This is a free concert but the quality was excellent.  Highly recommended. Family friendly - lots of little kids dancing on the platform in front of the stage - encouraged by the director.

reviews.title: Nothing is free
reviews.text: Seems like a beautiful place but every single bit costs $9 per person for what would be free in most European countries. I wasn't prepared to pay $36 for 4 people to have a quick look at the tea garden and another $36 for the botanical garden, so quickly got back on a bus and moved on. Unless you love gardens and are prepared to spend time here, give it a miss.

reviews.title: Lovely and huge
reviews.text: We saw this only by bus so my review does not do this beautiful park justice. There is a lot to do and the weather makes touring perfect.

reviews.title: Huge and Beautiful
reviews.text: My family of 4 (two teenagers 16 and 18) loved this park. It is absolutely enormous. It is very hard to believe that you are in the middle of a major city. We spent many hours wandering around, eventually making our way to the Pacific coast for a first splash in the Ocean. I guess we walked 4 or five miles, maybe more. We were certainly footsore at the end. But without a doubt, this is one of the most incredible parks, in a City, in the world. I really envy the locals, who were all skating, throwing frisbee's, cycling, running, hanging, chatting and laughing. They are very lucky! A beautiful, relaxing haven in the middle of San Francisco. Loved it.

reviews.title: Nice
reviews.text: Nice area people enjoying the Sun and glorious weatherClean and very tidyAnd a view the Tattoo ladies

reviews.title: Great place to visit!
reviews.text: We had all of about an hour to check out Golden Gate Park, so we did not see nearly enough, but in comparison to NYC’s Central Park and Boston’s Commons, SF gets the definitive edge! Plenty to do, great weather year-round, and numerous spots for great picture taking.

reviews.title: One of the highlights of a trip to SF!!
reviews.text: Our tour guide drove us through the park in our luxury mini-van and regaled us with stories of events and activities related to this magnificent floral treasure!  I imagined that if I lived in SF I would spend a great deal of my time in this lovely oasis!

reviews.title: Sunday afternoon
reviews.text: This park is HUGE! We only really saw the Japanese garden (which you have topay to enter) It has a nice Japanese cafe and lots of plants, Koi carp, and a weird bridge that is almost vertical to climb! Lots of photoopportunities.

reviews.title: A day in the park
reviews.text: If you have a day to spare, the park is tremendous an d wonderful for a nature walk, but most exhibits/museums, tea garden...all have an entrance fee..we only paid to see the tea garden and the fee is to help preserve and maintain it .  A special treat were the dahlias garden at the flower conservatory...stunning!

reviews.title: One of my favourite places on earth
reviews.text: Love hanging out here, some great places to visit around too. Never seen it too crowded, always a good vibe.

reviews.title: Delightful
reviews.text: Either bike or walk.  Top are the Japanese Tea Garden self tour with a cup of their clear soup (Misto?) if it's chilly.  Rent a bike on Stanyan and to the ocean an d back.  Bite at Land's end cafe.  If you like gardens, the Botanical Garden is tops.  It's also close (about a 4 block walk) of to the Inner Sunset neighborhood where you can catch the N-Judah trolly car back to Market, and eventually to the Ferry Building.  Extremely iconic, scenic ride.

reviews.title: terrible experience
reviews.text: The park is beautiful but the experience was horrible. My car got mashed in 15 min when my friends and I were taking a small tour in the park. We parked the car along the road with many other cars, and at the same time 4 cards were mashed at the same place where we have parked. No camera so no way to find the thefts.

reviews.title: Awesome park
reviews.text: I will definitely be coming back to this park, and will spend more time here. I took a small walk as a I was limited for time. If you visit here allocate extra time as it is a large park with museums and a lot of walking/biking trails to enjoy.

reviews.title: Ok
reviews.text: Disappointed with park, poor signage for walking in from different directions. Main issue was lack of cafes, as tourist didn't have picnic with us, which is way to enjoy the park. Eventually got to Haight area, which made our day, lovely food and people watching

reviews.title: Gorgeous! Must explore!
reviews.text: There are so many things to see here! Incredible trees and flowers, winding pathways and roads,and views of the bridge!you could honestly spend a whole day here! I would suggest packing a P.O. nice and finding a spot to just sit for an hour, then ride a bike, a scooter, walk orDrive to see all that you can!!

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: A really lovely park, but the scale on the map is as the crow flies, it will take you much longer to get around. The Science museum is the reason we came here, but it cost way too much money and we just could not afford to go inside, which's a real shame!

reviews.title: Perfect picnic spot!
reviews.text: Beautiful park and really well maintained. We spent hours here walking through as there is so much to see and it is so pleasant. Lots of areas to have a picnic!

reviews.title: pretty, well maintained, lots to do and see
reviews.text: pretty, well maintained, lots to do and see - we walked the whole park from the beach to Haight via a quick stop off to the 16th Ave Tiled Steps. a good walk, paths well maintained, lots of other things to see and do inside.

reviews.title: Some nice spots
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park has some nice spots to sit with a picnic etc or just chill out and play sports. My only complaint is that much of the park is taken up by musuems etc, making it less inclusive.

reviews.title: Beautiful Gardens
reviews.text: My husband and I traveled to San Francisco for our 35th anniversary and one of the sights we took in was the Golden Gate Park.Beautifully landscaped and rich in historical significance to the city, we especially enjoyed the Conservatory of Flowers and the Japanese Tea Garden.  While we didn't spend a lot of time there, we enjoyed what we saw. nd we enjoyed the narration by our guide. Probably better if you take a lunch and pend more time.  Worth seeing.

reviews.title: Great park for stroll
reviews.text: This was our first trip to this park. It is a hidden gem and deserves a visit. We wanted to make a quick stop but ended up spending over five hours there. It has a lot to offer whether you want to visit museums or just stroll thorough the grounds, explore the Japanese tea gardens or the rose garden.

reviews.title: Once you find parking...
reviews.text: It’s a cool place to see. Nice views of the bridge and city on a clear day. Many activities surround the area too.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Lots to see & do by car, bike or walking. Keep in mind this park is huge....watch out for the hippie VW tour buses.

reviews.title: So beautiful!  What a view!
reviews.text: A thousand acres of things to see.  Japanese Garden, A museum or three, a planetarium and the Dutch Windmills to name just a few things to see.  GO!

reviews.title: West coast central park
reviews.text: Didn’t realize there was any green space in the city until we happened upon this beautiful space. There were so many different areas and plenty to explore. The architectural pieces were great to see as well!

reviews.title: Favorite place in San Fran
reviews.text: You could spend a week in this biodiverse collection of luxurious plants. Definitely make time to stroll in after cruisin down Haight/Ashbury

reviews.title: Runners Paradise
reviews.text: Spending 5 days in Frisco to see all the sights. Coming from Texas to escape the heat. Back home we belong to a run club and on that Saturday was our annual kick off run. Since we were in San Francisco we decided we would start out or first day with a run in the park, We got up early that Saturday and found parking in the Park. We knew that you could either run on Martin Luther King drive or JFK drive with plenty of views and paved running-walking paths. My wife, her friend and my buddy were supposed to only run 3 miles, so they ran down MLK, while I planned to run at least 6 miles down JFK. What a great place to run. Excellent weather 55 degree, terrific views, paved paths and plenty of other runners, walkers an bikers enjoying their workouts. I got close to the ocean before I had to turn around to get my 6 miles a meet back up with my group ( thinking they only did 3 or 4 miles.) They ended up doing close to 6 also and had been able to run up MLK to the ocean and then come back on JFK. We loved the park and so jealous of those that get to run this everyday .

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Take a stroll in this beautiful park in one of the most beautiful city’s in the world. Enjoy the scenery and smells. Surrounded with the most beautiful neighborhood shops with fresh fruit.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Used the hop on hop off bus to get there.  It is a very quiet and calming place to walk around.  It is an easy place to  walk around. Have a large memory card in your camera!  The statues, fountains, trees and flowers are exquisite.

reviews.title: Huge park for everything
reviews.text: What an area!!!! You can do almost every kind of activity there and you will meet people of any kind there as well. We walked the park from east to west and spend almost one day there.  More attractions are in the east part. Little lakes and silent areas are there as well as the museum, the science park, botanical gardens and much more. Food is available in the park. Plan your own trip and discover it. Busses run along the park on all sides. Get the tourist pass first and then take the MUNI or the busses, will save a s.... lot of money. Get it at the tourist Information centre at powell street.Enjoy the park where they started the summer of love in 1967.... 🤩

reviews.title: Fun and free on a weekday
reviews.text: Arrived on a Tuesday around 11:30am.  Parked for free near the baseball fields on the south side of the park.  Short walk to the California Academy of Sciences.  Took my 7 year old son to visit just the public spaces.  Found a hot dog stand behind the stage adjacent to the museums.  I think the park is an enjoyable place for some free time, without having to pay for the extra museums and activities.

reviews.title: Nicely maintained
reviews.text: Bike paths, pretty views, a huge park which gets well used and is a great place to get in some exercise.

reviews.title: Walk in the park
reviews.text: We took a walk throught the park on a Sunday afternoon and enjoyed seeing lots of locals enjoying the space and meeting family/friends.  We felt more flowers would be good and more signage for tourists.

reviews.title: San Francisco vacation
reviews.text: This place has all you need to spend a day with the family and friends . Just go there to enjoy light , green space  and institutions that show art , science and wonders.

reviews.title: A lot of open space
reviews.text: The park is good for long walks and to relax.  I found the park to be somewhat dirty and it was very crowded (which can be a good thing).  Overall it was just OK.

reviews.title: Bison!
reviews.text: Real live bison just chilling in San Francisco, how is that not awesome? Totally worth stopping by to say hello.

reviews.title: much to see and do in a very large urban park
reviews.text: We spent a couple of hours in Golden Gate park and only scratched the surface on its attractions. We visited the the Japanese Garden and Botanical Gardens and paid $9 a person to visit each one. Both were beautiful and provided excellent picture taking, but recognize that access to them requires a fee. We also visited Stowe Lake which has rental boats and a hiking trail on the inner island. We took a Lyft to the park expecting to use the free shuttle to get around but the shuttle only runs on Saturday and Sunday. The park is very large so alot of walking or biking may be required when the Shuttle isnt available. It seems that SF MUNI also has routes through the park so that may be an option.

reviews.title: Most of the good stuff has a fee to enter
reviews.text: The good.  Its big.  The weather is nice and cool in the summer.  The buffalo are really cool.  The bad.  Pay here.  Pay there.  Pay everywhere.  About the only thing we could do that did not charge admission was the buffalo and walking around.The ugly.  There is nothing natural here.  This used to be a sand dune, near-beach habitat that has been bulldozed and watered into the hodgepodge of invasive species and spectacle that it is today.

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text: This park has something for everyone. Really. The science museum is super fun for the kids as they give them a backpack full of stuff and a scavenger hunt of sorts for them. The Japanese tea garden is modestly priced and is absolutely beautiful...the tea and cookies are top shelf there. Queen Wilhelmina tulip garden under the Dutch windmill was really nice to see right next to the Pacific Ocean. It is a day of walking, but if your feet can hack it, you should spend a day here. They also have disc and traditional golf courses.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: For our last day on vacation we spent the afternoon in Golden Gate Park. What an amazing green space to have, so many things to see and do, and open spaces to relax.We visited the de Young Museum and had lunch at their Cafe. Then we walked over to the Conservatory of Flowers, which was open later.  We were able to have a nice visit before getting dinner and heading to the airport for our red-eye flight home.

reviews.title: A wonderful green space to visit -with lots to see and do for all the family!!
reviews.text: We were very fortunate to be staying quite close to Golden Gate Park.  We spent time exploring the lakes and museums plus walking its length down to the sea! A must for visitors !!

reviews.title: Huge and gorgeous park
reviews.text: This was our second trip to San Francisco in the past year and both times we enjoyed Golden Gate Park.  During our first visit, we focused on some of the major attractions that are contained in the park:  California Academy of Sciences, de Young Museum, Conservatory of Flowers, and the Japanese Tea Garden.  This trip we were there on a beautiful sunny day and just wanted to spend the time outside.  So, in addition to just walking around the park, we went through the Rose Garden, San Francisco Botanical Garden, and rented a paddle boat to cruise around Stow Lake.  Wonderful day.

reviews.title: Wonderful escape from the city!
reviews.text: The park is gorgeous and diverse in its offerings. There are trails for more strenuous hiking, paths for meandering, beautiful gardens and a moving AIDS memorial grove.  Plenty of space for cycling, walking, paddle boating, canoeing or just relaxing and enjoying nature.The conservatory of flowers is stunning and Strawberry Hill in the middle of Stow Lake is a great climb and has amazing views from the top!Easily accessible by public transportation and plenty of parking if you drive, definitely a must-do while visiting SF!

reviews.title: So much to do here!
reviews.text: I loved this park, so many places to see and to walk to!Shakespeare's garden was very small but pretty, but what I really loved was the Japanese Tea Garden ! You pay extra to go in but lots of history and nice on a hot day to sit in the gardens with an iced green tea and sugary treat! (or miso soup or noodles if being healthy)I didnt get to see the whole park because its BIG and had walked quite far already to get there - but if you can, i have no doubt the rest would be just as stunning!

reviews.title: Lovely Park for all
reviews.text: I highly recommend the science museum, though seems pricey it is well worth it. There is a separate review on that. Within the park I loved the Japanese Tea Garden, fun fact this is where the fortune cookie was first created!!! A chiense/Japanese recipe!!

reviews.title: Loved it.  Hated multiple entry fees at each point
reviews.text: The park  is HUGE.  We fortunately had a two day hop on hop off which  included passes to the 'green line ' which is an old woody bus taking you around the garden... It includes three LAKES (more like ponds)  and huge grounds for family time with kids. The highlight.... LANDS END.  stunning views of the pacific bay and if you stand at a particular point and look over your right shoulder you have a great corner view of the Golden Gate Bridge. There is a botanical garden,  Japanese garden,  and a world class planiturum,  but  all with additional entry fees.. Right at the beginningAlso has its own zoo with its own entry fee. The beach is unmanned (no lifeguard) and is supposed to be great for surfing,  which was apparent,  but also has many warnings for rib currents.

reviews.title: Amazing park
reviews.text: We spent 3 hours biking around the park and loved it. The park is really beautiful and each area has something special.

reviews.title: Such a large beautiful park
reviews.text: We started at the Japanese Tea Garden.  If you want to save a few bucks at the Tea Garden go before 10:00.  The Golden Gate Park is large - I would suggest you check a map for the areas you would like to visit if you are short on time.  We walked about 7 miles.

reviews.title: Very pretty and very quiet
reviews.text: A very peaceful and relaxing park if you are looking for respite from the city. However not as vibrant or interesting as Central Park in NYC or the Public Garden and Boston Common in Boston. It was actually a little boring. No street performers or food venders that we encountered. As with many public parks they charge for everything now. There was an entrance fee for the Japanese Tea Garden and the Botanical Garden. Now that I’ve seen it I’m all set and and don’t feel the need to return.

reviews.title: Refreshing
reviews.text: Take time to visit botanical garden and Japanese garden , price is bit high , 9 $ . However you can discover the park up to the Dutch windmill .

reviews.title: NICE BREAK FROM THE CITY!!
reviews.text: Beautiful park to spend a few hours.  Parking was easy to find on the streets and it was a pretty clean place (no homeless or druggies hanging out here)  We spent an hour or so at the flower garden/conservatory and just relaxed in the shade of the park.

reviews.title: Amazing destination
reviews.text: The botanical and japanese gardens are great.  Walk the whole park and end up at the beach for sunset. A must.  Every attraction works.

reviews.title: Beautiful park on a beautiful Sunday!
reviews.text: We spent part of the day at the Park, and enjoyed the Japanese Tea Garden (though a little expensive), walking around . If we had more time, we would have visited one of the wonderful museums there or rented a bike or segway.  We had not time to make it to see the Buffalos.  The only drawback was it was hard to find a map and it would be nice if they provided shuttle buses in the park to help you get around fast and for those who cannot ride a bike or segway.

reviews.title: From Ocean Beach to the Panhandle there is something for everyone
reviews.text: Stowe Lake is one of our favorite spots for a nice walk around the lake to see the birds and turtles to picnicking at one of the many grassy spots. Then a short walk to 9th n Judah to visit one of the many awesome watering holes or restaurants.

reviews.title: One of the best Urban parks in U.S.A.
reviews.text: This man made and design park is an Oasis in San Francisco. There are world Class Museums, a botanical gardens, a lake for row boating and paddling, Bison to be viewedand numerous parks for children to play. There is something for everyone in this park.You can access this park at numerous points by public transportation.

reviews.title: Great green reprise among the concrete and asphalt of the city
reviews.text: Great green reprise among the concrete and asphalt of the city.  2 museums, Japanese garden, Botanical gardens, plus lots of walking spaces and other finds. Greta place to walk and decompress

reviews.title: 4th of July
reviews.text: Felix is 4 on the 4th so of course we head over to area by the carousel 👍🏽Perfect in the park for kids ,parents, friends & even a dinosaur surprise visit🦕🦖

reviews.title: Great Park
reviews.text: Checked out the Japanese Tea Garden and the Botanical Gardens. Both were great to check out. Ran out of time to explore other parts of the gardens. Definitely check this park out!!

reviews.title: Worth the commute
reviews.text: There are so many amazing surprises within this extremely large park. There is a Dutch style wind mill, beautiful botanical gardens, buffalo, you can visit the SFPD horses, countless fields for lawn games with friends, BBQs, great for riding bikes, Stern Grove Festival on Sundays in the summer for free music.

reviews.title: Spend the day
reviews.text: It’s massive with so much to do.Sunday with no cars is brilliant and if you are prepared to walk and take a picnic you won’t be disappointed

reviews.title: Not just for hippies anymore
reviews.text: An iconic park.  What a history from the greatful dead and the sixties.  Still a relaxing open place to spend a part of your day.  Why not rent a bike?  Great views for you photographers

reviews.title: Gorgeous park
reviews.text: This is a gem in the middle of San Francisco. It contains Academy of Science and JapaneseTea Garden as well as great roads and trails for running. Helped by Sunday’s being car free!

reviews.title: Amazing Park!
reviews.text: An outstanding day at the Golden Gate Park.  We rented bikes and enjoyed the many museums and sites the park offered.  This is a must when visiting San Francisco, one of the coolest parks with great walking paths, museums and fun.

reviews.title: Golden Gate Park Tennis Courts!
reviews.text: Great courts, nice people. The diehards know their tennis! You can also walk to the Memorial Trail; its truly special.

reviews.title: Beauty all around
reviews.text: A beautiful gem in the middle of the city! So much to discover and see in this park. You could easily spend a day, or 2, discovering all this park has to offer. Full of locals and tourists alike but never felt crowded. An absolute must see during any visit to San Francisco. By the way, it's bigger than Central Park!

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: I wish I had a day to spend just with n the park, beautiful!  I would have loved to try the “earthquake room” in the natural science museum.

reviews.title: Beautiful and gigantic park
reviews.text: But to be honest i cannot rate it 5 stars cuz we had the rental car vandalized and they took our bagpacks.... Too bad cuz the place is really Nice !

reviews.title: You need a whole day
reviews.text: This park is huge and has so much to explore we only did a quarter of it. We should have taken a bus to the park then walked it. Beautiful trees and colours

reviews.title: Big park!
reviews.text: Was much bigger than i thought it would be! we took a tour through it but sadly didn't get to walk it. next time!

reviews.title: Gigantic Park
reviews.text: This part is 4 to 5 miles and maybe a half a mile wide. We walked many miles through this park and ended up hopping on a free shuttle to get us to Ocean Beach. There are lakes and waterfalls and Buffalo and flowers and so much more. So much to see and so little time to see it all. It is a great park and you really should spend some time here checking it out. The Conservatory of flowers, the Japanese tea Garden, and the botanical garden all cost extra ($9 p/p). You can rent bicycles inside the park and there are Segway tours as well.

reviews.title: Large Park With Many Sights
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is quite huge and has so many different areas to visit.  I went to the Botanical Garden there and also the Japanese Tea Garden, which was quite interesting.  Parking is on the street, although one of the museums in the park has a garage.

reviews.title: MY NEW HAPPY PLACE!
reviews.text: Everywhere we walked today was a better step than the last. We started with the buffalos. Buffalos! In SF? Then we meandered by the polo grounds, past a lovely green space with merry Independence Day celebrants, and on to Stow Lake. You can take a romantic paddle in a boat! There’s also food (and drinks!) at the boathouse. Next we hit the Botanical Garden. The chaos spoke to my soul. The Shakespeare Garden is lovely, and I cannot wait to return to the science museum. Hello, T-Rex. I’ll be back with a picnic blanket and some wine and cheese. The park is my new happy place.

reviews.title: Very nice park with lots to see
reviews.text: Large park that can take hours to explore. They have a very nice Japanese garden that is free if you arrive before 10am.

reviews.title: IT says park but it is more
reviews.text: I thought is would be like Central Park with no vehicles allowed (like a Park) but there is cars and buses that drive thru the whole time.  There was not many signs so it was difficult to get around without getting lost or missing a turn.

reviews.title: Great park but too many charge admission
reviews.text: We liked the walk around the park. Lots of green space and walkways are nice.  The only detraction was that there was a not insignificant charge to see many of the attractions.  Even the tiny Japanese tea garden had a charge ($8 if I remember correctly).  We expected a public park to be mostly free.

reviews.title: One of the Best EASY Walks or Bike Rides in San Francisco
reviews.text: The park is exceptionally beautiful almost year around (except maybe during summer fog) for walking and bike riding. The Conservatory of Flowers is one of the must does in Golden Gate Park al year around and is inexpensive, best to buy ticket before arrival as is every venue in the park. The California Academy of Science is one of the best places especially for families. Buy tickets ahead of time if possible and when first arriving go straight to the ticket booth for the planetarium and then view the rest of the building afterward, trust me it is worth it. The butterflies in the huge terrarium are so magnificent as is are all the plants. The aquarium is sure to please as well. And then there is The DeYoung Museum which is worth he visit just to ascend the tower and take in the views of the park and beyond a stop at the Japanese Tea Garden is next door. Stow lake is an easy walk, is where you can rent a bicycle (please, please follow the rules of the road so you don't go home broke and broken) or a paddle boat. The buffalo paddock is a short bike ride from Stow lake and just a little further you can see two windmills and the Pacific Ocean at Ocean Beach, DO NOT TURN YOIUR BACK ON THE WAVES EVER when on the beach, sneaker waves have taken several lives every year! There is good and safe parking underneath the museum but it is not cheap - AND again a warning, NEVER LEAVE ANYTHING IN YOUR CAR, I mean NOTHING! REALLY! Some streets are closed on weekends. The park has really become safe and you will experience much less panhandlers and homeless in the main park; one needs to be more wary of the panhandle.

reviews.title: So much to see!
reviews.text: I spent several hours visiting the various attractions in Golden Gate Park. There are so many things to see, from museums to gardens to beaches that there is really something for everyone to enjoy!

reviews.title: Nice Park
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is actually kinda nice. Great place to walk, exercise, and even to play football.  Nice park!

reviews.title: Some great areas
reviews.text: There is much to see in the park.  However it is very large and spaced out and there is no internal transportation.  Shuttles run only on the weekend.  Each individual site/ museum has a separate fee so figure out what you are most interested in.

reviews.title: A long walk in the Golden gate Park
reviews.text: Today 30th June 2018 we five people have a great walk of 3.4 kilometer in side the park.It was very pleasant.Being Saturday more people were there.Weather was also good.We all enjoyed the walk

reviews.title: M.J. Jackson
reviews.text: Golden Gate Park is lovely, and offers a variety of activities for all ages. Like most parks, these activities are of your own choosing,(i.e. picnicking, Frisbee, lounging with a book, fantastic photo ops., etc...). If you are visiting San Francisco, visiting Golden Gate Park is a “must” on your To-Do list.

reviews.title: Beautiful open space
reviews.text: Great place to visit and recharge Highly recommended Wide open space and several specialist areas to explore

reviews.title: Golden Gate park
